**Anustubh Meter**—When the Moon is in Scorpio and Mars is in Cancer, and they form an *Itthashala* <note>A configuration where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note>, this results in the "Lowest of the Low" *Kamboola* <note>A yoga where the Moon transfers influence between two planets</note>, which causes the destruction of work and brings sorrow. || 33 ||

If the Moon is in Scorpio <note>where it is debilitated</note> and Mars is in Cancer <note>where it is debilitated</note> and they are in a mutual *Itthashala* configuration, then the "Lowest of the Low" *Kamboola* occurs, which destroys the task at hand. The reason for this is that both planets lack essential dignity <note>original: "adhamadhikari," meaning they are in weak or debilitated positions</note>. || 33 ||

**Anustubh Meter**—In this manner, the examples of the previously mentioned variations should be applied. Wise practitioners should deduce the remaining types based on the relationship of the stated characteristics. || 34 ||

These variations are primary at the beginning and end; between them, fourteen other variations should be understood through the relationship of the stated characteristics. In this way, the sixteen variations that are well-known have had their individual examples explained. Beyond these, there are many other variations which the wise must understand through the power of their own intellect, based on the fundamental characteristics provided. || 34 ||

**Anustubh Meter**—The example of "Moon in Aries and Saturn" etc., illustrates the relationship between slow and fast-moving planets. Others have spoken of *Itthashala* and other configurations occurring when planets are situated in the same sign. || 35 ||

In another manner, the *Muthashila* <note>An Arabic-derived term for the Itthashala aspect</note> of fast and slow planets residing in a single sign is described. The verse states:
> "The Moon in Aries with Saturn; in Cancer with Mars; in Virgo with Venus; in Capricorn with Jupiter; or with Mercury in Pisces—these are not auspicious." || 1 ||

This is a variation of the *Arya* meter composed by Samarasimha <note>A famous 13th-century authority on Tajika astrology</note>. The teacher has cited this starting with the phrase "Moon in Aries and Saturn." The meaning is this: if the Moon and Saturn in Aries form a *Muthashila* by their degrees, it results in a "Middling-Low" *Kamboola* which produces inauspicious results. Here, although the Moon in Aries is in its own Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart sign</note>, Saturn is debilitated; thus this yoga is formed. (1) And if the Moon and Mars in Cancer form an *Itthashala*, since one is in its own house <note>Moon</note> and the other is debilitated <note>Mars</note>, it results in an "Excellent-Low" *Kamboola*. (2) Furthermore, if the Moon and Venus in Virgo form a mutual *Itthashala*, Venus is debilitated and the Moon is in its own Navamsha; this is a "Middling-Low" *Kamboola*. (3) Furthermore, if the Moon and Jupiter in Capricorn form a mutual *Muthashila*, Jupiter is debilitated and the Moon is in its own Navamsha; this is a "Middling-Low" *Kamboola*. (4) Furthermore, if the Moon and Mercury in Pisces form an *Itthashala*, Mercury is debilitated and the Moon is in its own Navamsha; this is a "Middling-Middling"...

<page-num>63</page-num>
<header>With Commentary in the Common Tongue.</header>

There is <term>Kamboola</term> <note>A specific planetary configuration in Tajika astrology where the Moon transfers influence between two planets</note>; these five examples are said to yield inauspicious results. The Teacher <note>Referring to the author or a high authority like Neelakantha</note>, citing the example of Samarasimha's statement "When the Moon is in Aries," has expressed the intent that variations also occur when fast-moving and slow-moving planets occupy the same zodiac sign. ||35||

->Translation—That which is joined with a planet in its fall, or with an enemy in an enemy's house,<-
->Is said to destroy the work of the Itthasala; this is clearly stated there. || 36 ||<-

If the <term>Lagnesha</term> <note>Lord of the Ascendant/Rising sign</note>, the <term>Karyesha</term> <note>Lord of the matter being inquired about</note>, and the Moon are in their signs of debilitation or in an enemy's sign, then the <term>Itthasala</term> <note>A configuration where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of a task</note> becomes a "work-destroying" <term>Kamboola</term>. This is the previously mentioned statement and the opinion of other teachers. Here, a variation of the <term>Itthasala</term> occurring in a single sign is also called work-destroying, which leads to an over-extension of the definition. To resolve this doubt, the Teacher provides this verse. The point is: if a planet in its sign of debilitation forms an <term>Itthasala</term> with another debilitated planet or an enemy planet, and the Moon also forms an <term>Itthasala</term> while in a debilitated or enemy sign, this might be possible elsewhere; however, it is improper among the <term>Kamboola</term> variations said to give inauspicious results when in a single sign. This is because two planets cannot share the same sign of debilitation <note>In Vedic astrology, each planet has a unique sign where it is weakest</note>, and it is impossible here for two planets to share the same enemy sign. Where there is enmity, there will be no aspect <note>Planetary "sight" or connection</note>, and without an aspect, there is no <term>Itthasala</term> at all. 

Alternatively, if one assumes an <term>Itthasala</term> is possible because an intermediate planet is within the close degrees of both the <term>Lagnesha</term> and <term>Karyesha</term> (who aspect each other), then this would simply become <term>Nakhta Yoga</term> <note>A configuration where a faster planet connects two others that do not aspect each other</note>. Or, if it is assumed a third planet between the two takes light from one and gives it to the other, it becomes <term>Yamaya Yoga</term>. Similarly, with Saturn and Mars, <term>Manau Yoga</term> <note>A yoga of prohibition or delay</note> is also possible. It was clearly stated before that aspects like the fourth or seventh occur in different signs. If one does not accept the example of "Moon in Aries," then the aforementioned yogas like Nakhta would be contradicted. Therefore, the established principle is that in all yogas, the <term>Muthashila</term> <note>Another term for Itthasala, signifying the "commingling" of influences</note> consideration applies to planets whether they are in different signs or the same sign. || 36 ||

->Translation—In an Itthasala between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Work, if one is in its fall,<-
->And the other is devoid of its own sign or other dignities, then the Moon here creates Kamboola Yoga. || 37 ||<-

If the Lord of the Ascendant—

# Tajik Neelakanthi

<page-num>64</page-num>

->Tajik Neelakanthi<-

If the Lord of the House of Interest <note>Dhishesha: the planet ruling the house related to the specific question</note> or the Lord of the Action <note>Karyesha: the planet signifying the matter at hand</note> is in its sign of debilitation, and the other is without dignity <note>Padahina: lacking strength from its own sign, exaltation, or divisional charts like Drekkana</note>, and the Moon is also without dignity, yet these three form a *Muthashila* <term>Muthashila: an aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of a task</term> with each other, it is still considered a *Kambool* yoga. || 37 ||

> *In the Anustubh meter:*
> In such a case, the success of the task should be known as minimal, just as when a man of one caste begs from another.
> Thus, the poets <note>learned scholars</note> understand this situation. || 38 ||

The result of this specific type of *Kambool* is explained with an illustration: Just as a person of one caste <note>Jati</note> receives very little when begging from another caste, similarly, this *Kambool* yields only slight profit. The clarity is this: if a patron <note>Yajaman</note> calls a Brahmin <note>priest/scholar</note> and gives of his own accord, he gives according to the Brahmin's desire; but if the Brahmin goes and asks himself, the patron gives only a little. The poets say the fruit of this *Kambool* is of that nature. || 38 ||

> *In the Anustubh meter:*
> One who holds no authority—whether auspicious like one's own sign, or even inauspicious—
> and is not aspected by any other form <note>planet</note>, is considered a "Traveler of the Void." || 39 ||

Now, to define the characteristics of *Gairi-Kambool*, the definition of a "Traveler of the Void" <term>Shunyadhwaga: a planet traveling through a vacuum or empty path</term> is first given: A planet that has no auspicious authority in its own house, exaltation, *Drekkana*, or *Navamsha* <note>divisional charts used to calculate strength</note>, nor has inauspicious authority in a sign of debilitation or an enemy's sign, nor even neutral authority, and is not aspected by any malefic or benefic planet, is called a "Traveler of the Void." || 39 ||

> *In the Anustubh meter:*
> When the Moon is a Traveler of the Void while the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Action are in *Itthashala* <note>a configuration of success</note>,
> and because of the lack of dignity like exaltation, there is no *Itthashala* with anyone— || 40 ||
> If this Moon, upon entering another sign, forms an *Itthashala* with a planet situated in its own sign or exaltation,
> this is called *Gairi-Kambool*; it is considered inauspicious if the dignity is lacking. || 41 ||

If the Moon is a "Traveler of the Void" and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnesha</note> or the Lord of the Action <note>Karyesha</note>—either one or both—are similarly "Travelers of the Void," the Moon does not form an *Itthashala* with them. However, if the Moon is about to enter another sign <note>Rashyantara</note> where the planet ruling that sign (either as its home or exaltation) is already seated, and by degrees, the Moon forms an *Itthashala* immediately upon entry, then *Gairi-Kambool* yoga is formed. This also gives results similar to the variations of *Kambool*. Furthermore, that which is situated in another sign...

<page-num>65</page-num>
<header>With Language Commentary</header>

If the Moon, while traveling a "void path" <note>original: "shunyadhvaga"; refers to a planet that does not form aspects with others in its current sign</note>, forms an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>A Tajika aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note> with another "void path" planet located in the same sign, then this <term>Gairikambool</term> configuration gives inauspicious results. This term <term>Gairikambool</term> is a Persian word (Gair-qabul) meaning "not accepted"; it is the opposite of "qabul" (acceptance) and is thus inherently unfavorable. Here, one school of thought suggests it gives results similar to a variation of <term>Kambool</term> <note>A favorable yoga where the Moon connects two planets</note> because an <term>Itthashala</term> state is achieved at the very end or beginning of the signs; however, it remains <term>Gairikambool</term>. This is the consensus of the teachers learned in <term>Tajika</term> <note>A system of Indian astrology heavily influenced by Persian and Arabic traditions</note>. || 40 || 41 ||

->Anushtup Meter<-

> In a query regarding "Will I obtain happiness?", Leo is the ascendant with the Sun in Aries. ||
> At eight degrees, the lord of happiness (Mars) is in Aquarius at twelve degrees. || 42 ||
> There is an <term>Itthashala</term> between them; the Moon is in the final degree of Virgo. ||
> Lacking its own sign or other dignities, it has no <term>Itthashala</term> with anyone. || 43 ||
> But with Saturn in its own exaltation or another sign, it creates an <term>Itthashala</term>. ||
> This <term>Gairikambool</term> brings gain through the help of another. || 44 ||

<margin>Gairikambool.</margin>
An example of <term>Gairikambool</term>: In a query about obtaining happiness, the Ascendant is Leo. The Ascendant Lord, the Sun, is at 8 degrees of Aries in the ninth house. The Lord of the Matter <note>original: "Karyesha"; the planet representing the object of the query</note>, Mars, is at 12 degrees of the seventh house, Aquarius. They are in a mutual <term>Muthashila</term> <note>Another term for the Itthashala aspect</note>. Now, in this configuration, the Moon is in the second house at the final 29th degree of Virgo, traveling a "void path" as previously described. This Moon does not have a <term>Muthashila</term> with the Ascendant Lord or the Lord of the Matter. However, the Moon is about to enter Libra. This sign is the exaltation of Saturn. Saturn is at a degree in Libra suitable for an <term>Itthashala</term>, such that it could form an aspect with the Sun and Mars. Now, as the Moon enters Libra, it seeks to form an <term>Itthashala</term> with Saturn. In doing so, the Moon takes on the purpose of Saturn's <term>Itthashala</term> with both planets. This <term>Gairikambool</term> yoga was created by Saturn through the influence of the Moon; meaning, the fruit of "obtaining happiness" will be achieved through the assistance of a third person. This is the first type. Again, the Ascendant and all else remain as they were. But if, instead of Saturn in Libra as previously mentioned, a planet like Mercury were on a "void path," then this <term>Gairikambool</term> would give inauspicious results—meaning happiness would not be obtained. In this example, one should substitute Mercury for Saturn in Libra. || 42-44 ||

<summary>This page defines the Gairikambool yoga in Tajika astrology, explaining it as a Persian-derived concept meaning "non-acceptance" which usually yields negative results unless a third planet intervenes. An illustrative example is provided where happiness is achieved only through the assistance of a third party, represented by the Moon's transition into a new sign.</summary>

### In the Anushtup meter: When the Moon is in a void path and there is neither an Itthashala nor a conjunction between the two <note>the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Matter</note>, this is Khallasara; it is not auspicious and destroys the fruits of the Kamboola yoga. || 45 ||

If the Moon is in a "void path" <note>Void of Course; not making aspects to other planets</note> and the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> does not form an <term>Itthashala: a favorable aspect or 'connection' in Tajik astrology</term> with the Lord of the Matter <term>Karyesha: the planet ruling the house of the specific question</term>, nor is it in conjunction with them, then this is the **Khallasara** yoga. This yoga destroys the positive results of a Kamboola yoga <note>a yoga where the Moon connects two planets</note>; otherwise, it simply gives inauspicious results. The word *Khallasara* is a Persian term <note>original: "Khallasar"</note> denoting strength or its lack in this context.

**Example of the Khallasara Yoga:**
In a Leo Ascendant, the Lord of the Ascendant (Sun) is at 3 degrees of Aries. The Lord of the House of Children (Jupiter) is at 5 degrees of Aquarius. They are in a mutual <term>Muthashila: a specific applying aspect</term>. However, the Moon is at 20 degrees of Virgo. It does not form an Itthashala with anyone, nor is it joined with the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Matter. This Khallasara yoga will create obstacles in obtaining a son; this is its result. || 45 ||

### In the Rathoddhata meter: If a planet that is combust, in its fall, in an enemy's sign, or retrograde—and thus weak—forms a Muthashila, it is unable to carry the matter forward. Whether at the beginning or the end, it cannot fulfill the task. || 46 ||

The definition of **Radda Yoga** is now given: The word *Radda* is Persian <note>original: "Radd"</note> and is a synonym for "useless" or "weak." A planet is called weak if it is combust <note>too close to the Sun</note>, in its sign of debilitation, in an enemy's sign, in retrograde motion, or "lacking luster" (meaning it is about to set or has just risen, i.e., in an infant or elderly state). By extension, being in a "bad house" <note>original: "khalasthana"</note>, in a temporary enemy's place, or joined with/aspected by malefic planets also constitutes weakness. When such a lusterless planet forms an Itthashala with another, it cannot grant the fruits of that house at the beginning or the end of the aspect. Because it is weak, it can neither receive the brilliance of another planet nor give its own brilliance to another. The name of this combination is the **Radda Yoga**. || 46 ||

<header>With Commentary in the Vernacular Language.</header>

### Upajati Meter - If a planet in a center joins one in a falling house, the work is destroyed at the end.
### If the planet in a falling house joins one in a center, it is destroyed first and happens later. || 47 ||

Another variation of the definition and result of <term>Radda Yoga</term> <note>A yoga of cancellation or reversal where a predicted outcome is undone</note> is as follows: when the planet representing the work <note>Karyesha</note> is in a <term>Center</term> <note>Houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> and forms an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>A specific aspect or 'connection' between two planets</note> with a weak planet, while the Lord of the Ascendant is in a <term>Falling House</term> <note>Apoklima; specifically the 3rd or 9th houses here</note> from that weak planet, then the result will not be permanently cancelled. Instead, the task will first be accomplished but will be destroyed in the end. Here, by "falling houses," the third and ninth houses are taken; because there is no aspect to the 6th and 12th houses, the possibility of an Itthashala yoga does not even exist there. If the planet representing the work is weak and sits in a falling house while forming a <term>Muthashila</term> <note>An application of aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note> with the Lord of the Ascendant situated in a center, then it will first destroy the tasks arising from that house and later grant success in that work. This is the nature of Radda Yoga.

<margin>First auspicious, then inauspicious Cancellation.</margin>

**First Example:** Aries Ascendant. The Lord of the Ascendant is Mars; the Lord of Fortune is Jupiter. The Sun and Saturn are in the sixth house in Virgo at 10 degrees each. Here, the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Work are combust, joined with malefic planets, and located in the sixth house; thus, this is a Radda Yoga. The result: regarding a question of fortune, fortune will be destroyed. Or, **Second Example:** The same Aries Ascendant. The Lord of the Ascendant, Mars, is weak in the twelfth house, and the Lord of Fortune, Jupiter, is in Capricorn (its sign of debilitation)

<margin>First inauspicious, then auspicious Cancellation.</margin>

at ten degrees. Here, the fast-moving Mars, sitting in a falling house, forms an Itthashala with the slow-moving Jupiter in a center; therefore, this Radda Yoga first produces inauspicious results and later auspicious ones. Or, **Third Example:** The fast planet is weak in a center—Mars in Cancer at ten degrees (its sign of debilitation)—and the Lord of the Work, Jupiter, is in the falling twelfth house. Mars forms an Itthashala with Jupiter. This Radda Yoga produces auspicious results first and inauspicious results later. || 47 ||

### Example of Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note>

> *Upajati Meter—If a slow-moving planet is situated in its own sign, exaltation, or other favorable positions, and forms an Itthashala yoga with a fast-moving planet that is lacking such dignity (one-quarter less strength), then the task will still be accomplished. However, if the fast-moving planet is retrograde or otherwise powerless, the result should be declared as failure.* || 48 ||

The definition of the <term>Duhphali Kuttha Yoga</term> <note>A combination indicating a difficult but ultimately successful outcome</note> is as follows: When a slow-moving planet is in its sign of debilitation, or in its own exaltation, decan, term, or ninth-part, and a fast-moving planet is "lacking a quarter" (meaning it lacks the auspicious authority of being in its own sign or exaltation) yet forms an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>A specific aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note>, the accomplishment of the task will occur, albeit with great difficulty. However, if the fast-moving planet is combust, in its sign of debilitation, in an enemy's sign, retrograde, or in a weak state (infant or elderly), and forms an Itthashala, then one should predict an inauspicious result. This is the Duhphali Kuttha Yoga. In the Persian language, the word <term>Duhphali</term> <note>original: "दुष्फाली" (Dushphali/Duhphali)</note> means "difficult to achieve" and the word <term>Kuttha</term> <note>original: "कुत्थ"</note> signifies "auspicious." Thus, Duhphali-Kuttha means "auspiciousness achieved through difficulty." 

<margin>Duhphali Kuttha Yoga.</margin> 

**Example:** In a question regarding happiness, Aries is the Ascendant. The <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> <note>Lagnēśa</note>, Mars, is in the Ascendant at twelve degrees of Aries. The Lord of the House of Happiness (the 4th house) is the Moon, located in the eleventh house at ten degrees of Aquarius, forming an Itthashala. Here, Mars possesses dignity (positional strength) while the Moon lacks it. Such is the Duhphali Kuttha Yoga; it brings about the attainment of happiness through great effort. || 48 ||

> *Indravajra Meter—If both the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Work (the planet representing the matter at hand) are devoid of strength, and neither is joined with another planet situated in its own sign, etc., but if both are strong, then the wise say the task is accomplished through the help of others.* || 49 ||

The definition of <term>Dutthotthadivira Yoga</term> <note>A yoga involving assistance from a third party</note> is as follows: When both the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> and the <term>Lord of the Work</term> <note>Kāryēśa</note> are weak (due to being combust, in debilitation, in an enemy's sign, or retrograde, etc.) but are in a mutual Itthashala, and the faster planet among them is joined with a third, slower-moving planet that is strong in its own sign or exaltation—specifically forming a <term>Muthashila</term> <note>An aspect indicating the coming together of influences</note>—then the task is completed through the intervention of another...

Success will occur, or if another planet possessing its own strength <note>original: "swaksha-adi," referring to a planet in its own sign or exaltation</note> is fast-moving, even if the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnēsha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> or the Lord of the Matter <term>Kāryēsha: the planet ruling the house associated with the specific question</term> is weak, if they form a <term>Muthashila: an aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</term>, the work will still be accomplished through the help of another person. This is the teaching of the wise.

"Example": In a query regarding obtaining a wife, Leo is the Ascendant. The Lord of the Ascendant, the Sun, is in its sign of debilitation, Libra. The Lord of the Matter (the 7th house), Saturn, is in its sign of debilitation, Aries, or is retrograde in another sign. The point is that

->**The Dutthotthadivira Yoga.**<-
<note>original: "Dutthotthadivira," a Persian-derived term in Tajik astrology meaning "influence through a third party."</note>

both are weak. Among them, Saturn is joined with Mars. Because Mars is in its own house, it is powerful. Since the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Matter were weak, the work should not have been accomplished. However, because the powerful Mars is joined with a third planet, one should say that a wife will be obtained through the assistance of another. Or, if two fast planets, the Sun and Mars, are in Aries

->**The Dutthotthadivira Yoga.**<-

and become powerful by being in their respective exaltation and own houses, and both form an <term>Itthashāla: a specific aspect of planetary conjunction or influence</term> with Saturn, then this Yoga is formed. It gives the same result as mentioned before. This calculation should be applied to the appropriate <term>Muthashila</term>. The name of this Yoga, "Dutthotthadivira," is a Persian word. || 49 ||

---

->Translation: A planet at the end of a sign, moving to another, gives its light to another within the degrees of influence; this is Tambira, involving the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Matter. || 6 ||<-
<note>This is a translation of the Sanskrit verse provided in the source.</note>

Now the characteristics of the **Tambira Yoga** are described. When the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Matter are in any positions but do not have a mutual <term>Itthashāla</term> aspect, but one of them is at the very end of a sign <term>Rāshyantagata: situated in the final degrees of a zodiac sign</term> and is about to enter the next sign where another powerful planet exists within the degrees of influence—and in fact, it is about to form a future <term>Itthashāla</term> with that planet—then it gives its "glory" or "light" to that third planet. This is the Tambira Yoga. Its result is the accomplishment of the task.

# Tajika Nilakanthi
<note>The "Tajika Nilakanthi" is a seminal 16th-century Sanskrit treatise on Tajika astrology, which integrates Perso-Arabic astrological techniques into the Indian tradition.</note>

### The Tambira Yoga
<note>Tambira: A configuration where a faster planet transfers its influence to a slower planet via an intermediary.</note>

**Example:** In a query regarding the "attainment of happiness," the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> is Libra. The lord of the Ascendant, Venus, is at 10 degrees of Cancer. The lord of the House of Happiness <note>the 4th house</note>, Saturn, is at 29 degrees of Aquarius. There is no direct <term>Itthashala: a favorable aspect or 'application' between two planets</term> between them. However, Jupiter is at 5 degrees of Pisces. The fast-moving Saturn at 29 degrees of Aquarius is about to enter Pisces and will form a future <term>Muthashila: another term for the application of aspects</term> with Jupiter. Thus, Saturn transfers its light and power to Jupiter. This is a "work-accomplishing" yoga; it indicates that the seeker will indeed attain happiness. || 50 ||

-> *Verse in Upajati Meter* <-
> If a planet is in the Ascendant or near a Center <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, or if it aspects the Ascendant, or is in its own sign, exaltation, or decanate <note>Dreshkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</note> ||
> Or if it is in its own <term>Musallahe: a Persian-derived term for planetary strength</term>, its own Navamsha <note>ninth-part division</note>, or its own <term>Hadda: Egyptian-style 'terms' or bounds</term>, then a slow-moving planet is considered strong. || 51 ||

The fifteenth configuration is the definition of **Kuttha Yoga**. The word *Kuttha* is a Persian term used to denote a "strong planet." This strength is of many types. For this reason, the author first explains the hierarchy of planetary strength: a planet in the Ascendant is strongest; in its absence, planets in other "Centers" <term>Kendra: houses 1, 4, 7, and 10</term> are strong, though less so than the Ascendant. Weaker still are those in the "Succeedent" houses <term>Panaphara: houses 2, 5, 8, and 11</term>, and even weaker are those in the "Cadent" houses <term>Apoklima: houses 3, 6, 9, and 12</term>. In the <term>Durapha: houses 6, 8, and 12</term>, planets are declared powerless. 

Strength decreases in the order of Center, Succeedent, and Cadent houses. Furthermore, a planet is strong if it aspects the Ascendant, or is in its sign of exaltation, its own decanate, its own ninth-part, or its own "Hadda" <note>bounds</note>. Regarding speed: a planet at its "mean motion" <note>original: "nandaksha bhujagaravaih..."</note> is strong; one slower than that is less strong, and one with higher velocity is especially powerful. 

The logic here is that a planet in the Ascendant has full strength (60 units), in a Succeedent house half strength (30 units), and in a Cadent house a quarter strength (15 units). One must calculate the proportions at the cusps. Similarly, a planet aspecting the Ascendant is judged by the nature of the aspect—full strength for a friendly aspect, reduced for a malefic one. A planet in its own sign has full strength, while in the seventh sign from its own, it has no strength; for positions in between, one must use the <term>Trairashika: the Rule of Three (mathematical proportion)</term> to determine the exact strength. Even in the "Durapha" houses, a planet in its own sign may retain some strength. The calculation for exaltation strength should be done according to the prescribed rules. Since the Sun and Moon each own only one sign...

This is established because Mars and the other planets <note>referring to the non-luminous planets: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn</note> possess two zodiac signs as their houses. If the distance from its own house to the seventh house is less than 6 signs after calculation, keep it as is; if it is more than 6, subtract it from 12. Thereafter, divide the degrees and minutes by 30; the quotient will be the result in minutes of arc. This is the traditional method. It should also be remembered that at the beginning of its own house, a planet has full strength (60 units), and at the beginning of the seventh house from it, it has zero strength. The proportion is calculated accordingly: for example, if 1 sign (180 sixtieths) gives a full 60 units of strength, how much will be gained from a specific desired sign? Here, by simplifying with 60, the multiplier becomes 1 and the divisor 30, and so on. 1. The Exaltation strength is as previously mentioned. 2. At the beginning of a *Drekkana* <note>a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note>, the strength is 5, and at the completion, it is a full 10; once it has passed, the strength becomes zero. For instance, the strength is found by multiplying the difference between the elapsed and remaining degrees of the *Drekkana* by twelve. If 5 degrees equals 60, then how much for the remainder, etc. 3. The same should be understood for *Mushallah* <note>a Persian-influenced aspect or dignity in Tajika astrology</note> and *Hadda* <note>terms/bounds; a subdivision of signs used in medieval astrology</note>. Regarding Motion-strength (*Gatibala*), since the Sun and Moon are always swift, their motion strength is equal; for Mars and the others, it is 5. Thus ends verse 51.

> *Upajati Meter—One who has risen, who is in direct motion, who is joined with or aspected by a benefic, and is not perceived by the "sneezing" <note>original: "kshuta" - a specific technical aspectual gaze</note> 10th, 4th, 7th, or 1st sight of a malefic planet, nor joined with a malefic, is strong. In the evening, Venus, Moon, and Mars are strong.* 52.

The strength is described in another way: a planet that has risen (heliacal rising), which is in "direct motion" (meaning it was retrograde and has now turned direct), which is joined with or seen by a benefic planet, and which is subject to the "sneezing" (10th, 4th, 7th, 1st) aspect of a malefic planet <note>the text implies being free from this malefic gaze makes it strong</note>, and which is not joined with a malefic, becomes powerful. Regarding temporal strength, the meaning of the phrase "In the evening, Venus, Moon, and Mars" will be explained in the first verse of the next section. Here, the method for calculating strength is as follows: for Rising-strength, there is a full 60 units of strength on the day of rising and 0 (zero) strength on the day of setting; one must proportion the intervening days. For example, if half the total days from the day of rising to the day of setting equals 60 units of strength, then how much will it be on the desired day? This is the Rule of Three method. 1. The strength of a planet in direct motion should be known as before. 2. For strength from being joined with a benefic: if they are at the exact same minute of arc, the strength is 60; if there is a difference, calculate the difference between the two. That difference will be less than 30 degrees; then, doubling those degrees etc. results in the strength. 3.

# Tajika Neelakanthi

Page 72

Regarding the strength of auspicious aspects: subtract one-fourth from the aspect of the aspecting planet as previously described to determine the aspectual strength (Drishti-bala). Other calculations should be understood in a similar manner. **52**

> *If Jupiter and Saturn rise in the latter part of the night, and the male planets are empowered; others at midnight, and those situated in fixed signs are endowed with strength.* **53**

Venus, the Moon, and Mars are powerful when they rise in the evening. Jupiter and Saturn are powerful when they rise after midnight. Furthermore, male planets <note>Sun, Mars, and Jupiter</note> are strong during the day, while female or neutral planets <note>Moon, Mercury, Venus, and Saturn</note> are strong at night. Planets situated in fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note> are also considered strong. 

The method for calculating this strength is as follows: Since Venus does not typically rise in the evening in this context, for the Moon and Mars, take the difference between the planet and the Sun, subtract six, and divide the remaining degrees by three to find the strength. Here too, the maximum strength is sixty, similar to the calculation for exaltation strength. For Venus, take the difference between Venus and the Sun, multiply by six, and divide by five to find its strength. The logic behind this is a <term>Rule of Three</term> <note>Trairashika: a mathematical proportion</note> where if 50 degrees yields 60 strength, what will the desired degrees yield? By simplifying with a factor of 10, the multiplier becomes 6 and the divisor 5. **1**

Regarding the strength of Jupiter and Saturn in the latter part of the night: if the desired time is after midnight, the strength increases until the third watch <note>Prahar: a three-hour period</note> of the night, where it reaches its peak, and then decreases to zero by the fourth watch. If the time is after midnight, subtract the <term>Midnight</term> <note>Ratri-ardha: half-night duration</note> from it. If it is after the third watch, subtract it from the total duration of the night. Multiply the remainder by sixty and divide by the duration of a watch to find the strength for Jupiter and Saturn. **2**

The method for Day-Planet strength is: if the time is between morning and noon, take the elapsed day time. If it is between noon and evening, take the remaining day time. Multiply that by 60 and divide by the <term>Midday</term> <note>Dinardha: half-day duration</note> to find the strength. The logic is: if half a day yields 60 strength, what will the elapsed or remaining time yield? **3** 

By this same method, the strength of nocturnal planets is derived from the half-night duration. **4** 

The method for the Sun's <term>House Strength</term> <note>Bhava-bala: strength derived from residential position</note> is: subtract the Sun's position from the planet, triple the remaining degrees, and subtract from 60 to find the strength...

Here, female planets from the fourth to the tenth, and male planets from the tenth to the fourth, obtain equal strength in all those houses; this is the rationale. The strength of male/female planets in odd/even signs should be understood in the same manner as the previously mentioned strength for fixed signs. The purpose of describing these various types of strength and weakness (<term>Balabal</term>) is so that the practitioner of <term>Itthashal</term><note>A specific aspect or configuration in Tajika astrology where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note>, or one wishing to calculate an Itthashal, should declare the results based on the planet's condition. Now the characteristics of the sixteenth <term>Durapha Yoga</term> <note>Durapha: From the Persian 'da'if', meaning weak or infirm</note> are described. The Persian word *Durapha* signifies "powerless." This weakness occurs in many ways; therefore, the first verse explains the manifestation of weakness as follows:

A planet is considered weak if it is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house from the Year-Ascendant, Question-Ascendant, or Day-Ascendant. It is also weak if it is stationary, placed in an enemy's sign or its sign of debilitation, is retrograde, joined with a malefic, or is combust (hidden by the Sun's light). Furthermore, it is weak if it forms an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>A Tajika aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note> with an enemy planet or a planet in its debilitation/enemy sign, or if it is aspected by a malefic through a "small aspect" (the 4th, 10th, 7th, or 1st positions). 

Weakness also occurs if it forms or intends to form an *Itthashala* with planets in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, or if it is in the seventh sign from its own home, or located in the "Tail" or "Mouth" of <term>Rahu</term> <note>The North Node of the Moon; the 'Mouth' refers to the degrees it is about to consume, the 'Tail' to those it has passed</note>. The degrees Rahu has already traversed are the Tail, and the degrees yet to be traversed are the Mouth. A planet possessed of these conditions is powerless.

The mathematical method for calculating these points of weakness is the same as previously described. For example, for a planet in an enemy's sign, calculate it similarly to a planet in a fixed sign. For a retrograde planet, it has full strength on the days it begins retrogression, which then reduces to zero over the duration of the retrograde period; if the midpoint gives full strength (60 points), calculate the proportion for the desired day. For a planet joined with a malefic, the strength is zero within nine degrees, and beyond that, the strength should be taken according to the house results. For a combust planet, use the "Rule of Three" <note>Trairashika: a mathematical proportion</note> as one would for a rising planet, then take the strength according to the house results. || 55 ||

Other types of inauspicious strength are described: a planet that does not "see" (aspect) the <term>Lagnat</term> <note>The Lord of the Ascendant</note> is weak. In whichever house a planet's aspect falls, subtract the calculated points from the points of the following house; the remainder is the inauspicious aspect. 1. Additionally, the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>The ninth divisional chart, used for fine-tuning planetary strength</note> which is seventh from the one occupied by the setting (combust) Sun is considered weak. The strength of the setting planet is derived from the previously mentioned method...

Between these points, the strength is calculated by proportion. For example, if full strength (60) is granted at the total orb of light, how much is granted for the degrees already traveled? The same method applies to *Isarafa*. If an <term>Itthashali</term> <note>original: "इत्थशाली" - a favorable aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note> planet is weakened by any of these factors, it fails to give the predicted results; this condition is called <term>Durapha Yoga</term> <note>original: "दुरफ योग" - a configuration of failure or weakness</note>. || 56 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi

Page 76

The Moon is considered weak in the following ten ways: 5. When it is in the seventh sign from its own <note>The Moon's own sign is Cancer; the seventh from it is Capricorn</note>, 6. When it is in Sagittarius or in the ninth division <term>Navamsha - a one-ninth subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> of Sagittarius, 7. > **Shalini Meter:** The Moon is inauspicious if it is waning at the end of a sign, whether at the time of birth or at the time of a query. If Mars aspects the Moon during the bright fortnight, or if Saturn aspects it during the dark fortnight, it is not considered auspicious. || 58 ||

Furthermore, the Moon is inauspicious from the eleventh day of the <term>Krishna Paksha - the dark/waning fortnight</term> until the fifth day of the <term>Shukla Paksha - the bright/waxing fortnight</term>. It is also weak when it is beyond 26 degrees and 40 minutes of a sign, which is the ninth <term>Navamsha</term>. This evaluation should be applied to birth charts and query charts. Additionally, if Mars views the Moon with a hostile aspect <note>original: "shatru drishti"</note> during the bright fortnight, or if Saturn views the Moon with such an aspect during the dark fortnight, the Moon becomes inauspicious for all undertakings. || 58 ||

> **Vasantatilaka Meter:** If Saturn, situated in a masculine sign during the bright fortnight and by day, aspects the Moon; or if Mars, situated in a feminine sign during the dark fortnight and by night, aspects the Moon, the weakness of the Moon is diminished. Otherwise, the fault remains great. This should be understood by the wise in queries or births. || 59 ||

If Saturn sits in an odd (masculine) sign during the <term>Shukla Paksha</term> (bright fortnight) and during the day and aspects the Moon, or if Mars sits in an even (feminine) sign during the <term>Krishna Paksha</term> (dark fortnight) and at night and aspects the Moon, then the previously mentioned fault of <term>Durapha - planetary weakness or debility</term> is reduced. If these specific conditions of Saturn and Mars's aspects are not met, the fault remains strong. This should be considered in birth charts, queries, and by extension, yearly horoscopes. One must always evaluate the <term>Kuttha - planetary strength</term> and <term>Durapha - planetary weakness</term> for all planets. By calculating the difference between these two: if the <term>Kuttha</term> (strength) is greater, the planet gives good results even in a bad position, and excellent results in a good position. If the <term>Durapha</term> (weakness) is greater, the planet gives bad results even in a good position, and extremely bad results in a bad position. All results should be judged based on this scale of strength. Thus ends the summary of the 16 Yogas. || 59 ||

## Now, the Calculation of Joyful Strength (Harsha-bala)

> <note>original: "नन्दत्रिषट्लग्नभवर्क्षपुत्रव्ययइनाद्धर्षपदंस्वभोच्चम्..."</note>
> *The Sun in the ninth, Moon in the third, Mars in the sixth, Mercury in the first (Ascendant), Jupiter in the eleventh, Venus in the fifth, and Saturn in the twelfth find their place of Joy. Likewise, they are joyful in their own signs and exaltations. In groups of three houses starting from the Ascendant, female and male planets find strength respectively, as they do during the night and day.* ॥ 60 ॥

Now, the four types of Joyful Positions (Harsha-sthana) are generally described:
1. The Sun in the 9th house, the Moon in the 3rd, Mars in the 6th, Mercury in the 1st (Ascendant), Jupiter in the 11th, Venus in the 5th, and Saturn in the 12th attain Joyful Strength.
2. Secondly, planets like the Sun and others are Joyful-strong when placed in their own exaltation <note>The sign where a planet's influence is most potent</note> or their own zodiac signs.
3. Thirdly, female planets in houses 1, 2, and 3; male planets in 4, 5, and 6; female planets in 7, 8, and 9; and male planets in 10, 11, and 12 gain strength.
4. Fourthly, female planets gain strength at night, and male planets gain strength during the day.

This strength should be considered in queries (Prashna), birth charts, and annual horoscopes (Varshaphala). To calculate this, create a placement chart; in the column where a planet attains strength, write the number 5.

<margin>Chart of Joyful Strength (Harsha-bala).</margin>

| Planet | Sun | Moon | Mars | Merc | Jup | Ven | Sat |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Position | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Own Sign | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Exaltation | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 | 0 |
| Fem/Male | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 | 5 | 0 | 5 |
| Day/Night | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **10** | **0** | **0** | **5** | **10** | **5** | **5** |

In other positions, mark a zero, then sum them all up. For example, if a planet gains strength in one category, the total is 5; if in two, it is 10; if in three, 15; and if in all four, the total is 20. This is called the <term>Harsha-vinhsopaka</term> <note>A 20-point scale used to measure the 'Joy' or dignity of a planet</note> strength. Results should be predicted according to this.

A specific consideration is this: combine these with the previously mentioned <term>Kuttha-durupha</term> <note>Specific technical strengths in Tajika astrology</note> strengths obtained through the <term>Trairashika</term> <note>Rule of Three/Triplicity</note> method. Triple the Joyful strength and add it. If the auspicious strength is greater, predict highly favorable results; if the weak strength is greater, calculate the difference and predict unfavorable results. This is the tradition of the experts in <term>Tajika Shastra</term> <note>A branch of Indian astrology influenced by Persian/Arabic traditions, focusing on annual horoscopes</note>. ॥ 60 ॥

> *Ananta, of infinite intelligence and son of Chintamani—the jewel-ornament of the lineage of the Great Sage Garga and a master of mathematics—composed this Method of Birth (Janu-Paddhati) to utterly destroy ignorance.* ॥ 60 ॥

# Tajika Nilakanthi
<page-num>78</page-num>
->**Tajika Nilakanthi**<-

> His son, the wise scholar Nilakantha, by the command of the learned Shiva, established the sixteen *yogas* <note>original: "shodasha yogas" - specific planetary configurations in Tajika astrology</note>, the *Harsha* positions <note>original: "harshabhani" - points of planetary joy or strength</note>, and the definitions in this treatise. || 61 ||

In the first chapter on definitions, the author revealed his own name and qualities; the same should be understood for this second chapter. The specific distinction here is that the sixteen *yogas* and the *Harsha* positions are described in this second section. || 61 || Thus ends the chapter titled "Descriptions of Planetary Forms, Aspects, Sixteen Yogas, and Harsha Positions" in the vernacular commentary on the Tajika Nilakanthi by Mahidhara.

---

> **In the Indravajra Meter:** Fortune, Teacher, Knowledge, Fame, Wealth, Friend, Greatness, Hope, and Capability. || Brother, then Dignity, King, Father, Mother, Son, Life, Water, and Action. || 1 || **In the Vasantatilaka Meter:** Sickness, Desire, Strife, and thereafter Forgiveness; Scripture, along with Kin, then Devotion and Imprisonment. || Death, Association, Foreign Lands, Wealth, and Other’s Wife; then Other’s Work, Trade, and Success in Tasks. || 2 || **In the Anushtubh Meter:** Marriage, Childbirth, and Affliction; Faith, Affection, Strength, and Body. || Dullness, Trade, and in the *Sahams* <note>sensitive points</note>, Falling into Water and the Enemy. || 3 || **In the Anushtubh Meter:** Valor, Means, Poverty, Heaviness, and Water-work. || Bondage, Daughter, and Horse—these are the fifty *Sahams*. || 4 ||

Now the consideration of the <term>Saham</term> <note>A Persian astrological term referring to specific "lots" or sensitive points calculated by adding and subtracting the longitudes of planets and house cusps</note> is discussed. "Saham" is a Persian technical term. According to the school of Samarsimha <note>A 13th-century authority on Tajika astrology</note> there are 48, and according to the Greeks <note>original: "Yavanas"</note> and others there are 51; some say even more. Here, the names of 50 are given: 

1. Fortune, 2. Teacher, 3. Knowledge, 4. Fame, 5. Friend, 6. Greatness, 7. Hope, 8. Capability, 9. Brother, 10. Dignity, 11. King, 12. Father, 13. Mother, 14. Son, 15. Life, 16. Water, 17. Action, 18. Sickness, 19. Desire, 20. Strife, 21. Forgiveness, 22. Scripture, 23. Kin, 24. Imprisonment, 25. Death, 26. Foreign Lands, 27. Wealth, 28. Other’s Wife, 29. Other’s Work, 30. Trade, 31. Success in Tasks, 32. Marriage, 33. Childbirth, 34. Affliction, 35. Faith, 36. Affection, 37. Strength, 38. Body, 39. Dullness, 40. Trade, 41. Falling into Water, 42. Enemy, 43. Valor, 44. Means, 45. Poverty, 46. Heaviness, 47. Water-work, 48. Bondage, 49. Daughter, 50. Horse. 

These are stated by the Teacher. Among these, "Foreign Lands" should be understood as Travel, "Marriage" as Wife, and "Knowledge" as Education. According to the Teacher’s school, there are additional *Sahams*: 51. Wife, 52. Liberation, 53. Assets.

54. Paternal Uncle, 55. Distress, 56. Coming and Going, 57. Elephant, 58. Right-mindedness, 59. Killing, 60. Granary, 61. Quadruped, 62. Addiction, 63. Agriculture, 64. Sight, 65. Hunting, 66. ->**Indravajra Meter**<-
<note>original: "सूर्येन्दुचन्द्रान्वितमन्हि..."</note>
If the birth or yearly chart occurs during the day, subtract the Sun from the Moon and add the Ascendant. If at night, subtract the Moon from the Sun and add the Ascendant. This is called the <term>Punya Saham</term><note>The Arabic Part of Fortune</note>. If the Ascendant does not fall between the <term>Shodhya</term><note>the planet being subtracted</note> and the <term>Shuddhyashraya</term><note>the planet being subtracted from</note>, then add one sign to the result. || 5 ||

Now the method for creating the <term>Sahams</term> is described. First, for the **Punya Saham** (Point of Fortune): if the time of the year-entry <insert>Varshapravesha</insert> or birth is during the day, subtract the current longitude of the Sun from the current longitude of the Moon and add the current longitude of the Ascendant <insert>Lagna</insert>. If it is a night chart, subtract the Moon from the Sun and add the Ascendant. This results in the signs and degrees of the Punya Saham. 

However, there is a further refinement: the planet being subtracted is called the *Shodhya* and the planet it is subtracted from is the *Shuddhyashraya*. If the Ascendant does not fall between the zodiac sign of the *Shodhya* and the sign of the *Shuddhyashraya*, then one (1) sign must be added to the previously calculated Punya Saham. If the Ascendant does fall between them, do not add it.

**(Example):** Sun's longitude 4s 8° 10', Moon's longitude 6s 12° 10', Ascendant 8s 10° 10'. In a daytime year-entry, Sun is subtracted from Moon, leaving 2s 4° 0'. Adding the Ascendant gives 10s 14° 10'. Now for the refinement: since the Ascendant is not between Leo (the *Shodhya* at 8°) and Libra (the *Shuddhyashraya* at 12°), add one sign. The result is 11s 14° 10'. This is the Punya Saham. 

If it were a night year-entry: Sun 8s 4° 10' minus Moon 6s 12° 10' leaves 1s 22° 0'. Adding Ascendant 0s 10° 0' gives 2s 2° 0'. Since the Moon was subtracted from the Sun, and the Ascendant does not fall between Libra 12° and Sagittarius 4°, add one sign <note>original: "saika"</note>. This makes 3s 2° 0' the Punya Saham. This refinement of adding one sign if the Ascendant is outside the interval should be applied to all Sahams. || 5 ||

->**Upajati Meter**<-
<note>original: "व्यत्यस्तमस्माद्गुरुविद्द्वयोस्तु..."</note>
By reversing the calculation of Jupiter and Mercury, and subtracting the Punya Saham from Jupiter—reversed by day and as before by night—this is called the **Yasha Saham** (Point of Fame). || 6 ||

->### Tajika Neelakanthi ###<-

Now the method for the **Guru** <note>Teacher or Jupiter</note> and **Vidya** <note>Knowledge/Education</note> Sahams is described. These Sahams are calculated in the opposite manner to the Punya Saham. For example, during the day, subtract the Moon from the Sun, and at night, subtract the Sun from the Moon, then add the Ascendant. By applying the **Shodhyarksha** <note>original: "शोध्यर्क्षेत्यादि" - a mathematical correction process in Tajika astrology where 1 is added if the Ascendant does not fall between the two planets used in the calculation</note> refinement, the Guru and Vidya Sahams are determined. The Vidya Saham is also called the Saham of Wisdom. (3) For the **Yasha** <note>Fame/Success</note> Saham, during the day subtract the Punya Saham from Jupiter; at night, subtract Jupiter from the Punya Saham. The Shodhyarksha refinement applies everywhere here as well. This results in the Yasha Saham. || 6 ||

**Rathoddhata Meter**—Subtract the Punya Saham from the Guru Saham as agreed by the sages; at night, reverse this and add Venus. If the conditions of the Ascendant-like calculation <note>Shodhyarksha</note> are met, add one; the wise call this the **Mitra** <note>Friendship</note> Saham. || 7 ||

For the sake of the Mitra Saham, during the day subtract the Punya Saham from the Guru Saham and add Venus. At night, subtract the Guru Saham from the Punya Saham and add Venus. If Venus is not within the range of the calculation <note>the arc between the two points</note>, add 1. This becomes the Mitra (5) Saham. || 7 ||

**Shalini Meter**—Subtract Mars from the Punya Saham as previously described for **Mahatmya** <note>Greatness/Magnanimity</note>; at night, it is the reverse. Subtract Venus from Saturn for the day and the reverse at night for the **Asha** <note>Hope/Desire</note> Saham; the rest should be inferred as stated before. || 8 ||

For the Mahatmya and Asha Sahams: subtract Mars from the Punya Saham and add the Ascendant. If the Shodhyarksha rule applies, add 1. This is the Mahatmya (6) Saham for the day. At night it is the reverse: subtract the Punya Saham from Mars and proceed as before. For the Asha Saham, subtract Venus from Saturn and add the remainder to the Ascendant; if the addition of one is required, do so. This is the Asha Saham for the day. At night it is the reverse: subtract Saturn from Venus and proceed as before. "Asha" is another name for "Desire." || 8 ||

**Indravajra Meter**—Subtract the Lord of the Ascendant from Mars; at night, reverse this. If Mars itself is the Lord of the Ascendant, then always subtract from Jupiter as before. This is also how the **Bhratri** <note>Brother/Sibling</note> Saham is inferred. || 9 ||

During the day, subtract the Lord of the Ascendant from Mars. At night, subtract Mars from the Lord of the Ascendant. If Mars happens to be the Lord of the Ascendant, then for both day and night, perform the subtraction from Jupiter; this is the **Samarthya** <note>Capability/Power</note> Saham. Similarly, by subtracting from Jupiter during the day or night and proceeding as before, the Bhratri Saham is found. || 9 ||

**Upajati Meter**—During the day, subtract the Moon from Jupiter; at night, the Sun and Moon are given in reverse order...

# Tajika Nilakanthi
<page-num>82</page-num>

->**The Calculation of Sahams**<-

For a night birth, subtract Jupiter from Mars and add the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagna"</note>; the **Forgiveness Saham** <note>Kshama-saham</note> is calculated in this same manner. (21) For a day birth, subtract Saturn from Jupiter; for a night birth, subtract Jupiter from Saturn, and add Mercury to the remainder to find the **Scripture Saham** <note>Shastra-saham</note>. (22) The purification process <note>shodhapakshetyadi - referring to the standard mathematical adjustments in Tajika astrology</note> applies everywhere here.

### Verse 14
*In the Upajati meter:*
Subtract the Moon from Mercury during the day or night to find the **Relative Saham**; for the **Prisoner Saham**, reverse this. For the **Death Saham**, subtract the Moon from the eighth house and add Saturn.

For a day birth, subtract the Moon from Mercury and add the Ascendant; do the same for a night birth to find the **Relative Saham** <note>Bandhu-saham</note>. (23) For a day birth, subtract Mercury from the Moon, and for a night birth, subtract the Moon from Mercury and add the Ascendant to find the **Prisoner Saham** <note>Bandaka-saham</note>. (24) In both day and night, subtract the Moon from the cusp of the eighth house <note>the house of death</note> and add Saturn to find the **Death Saham** <note>Mrityu-saham</note>. (25)

### Verse 15
*In the Upajati meter:*
Day or night, subtract the Lord of Wealth from the House of Wealth to find the **Wealth Saham**. Subtract the Lord of Dharma from the ninth house to find the **Foreign Country Saham**.

In both day and night, subtract the Lord of the second house <note>the house of wealth</note> from the second house itself and add the Ascendant to find the **Wealth Saham** <note>Dhana-saham</note>. (26) Similarly, in both day and night, subtract the Lord of the ninth house <note>the house of religion/fortune</note> from the ninth house and add the Ascendant to find the **Foreign Country Saham** <note>Pardesh-saham</note>. (27)

### Verse 16
*In the Upajati meter:*
Subtract the Sun from Venus for the **Other's Wife Saham**. Subtract Saturn from the Moon, or the reverse at night, for **Other's Work**. For **Commerce**, follow the rule for the day-birth Prisoner Saham.

Subtracting the Sun from Venus and adding the Ascendant for both day and night births results in the **Other's Wife Saham** <note>Parastri-saham</note>. (28) For a day birth, subtract Saturn from the Moon; for a night birth, subtract the Moon from Saturn and add the Ascendant to find the **Other's Work Saham** <note>Parkarma-saham</note>. (29) Subtracting Mercury from the Moon and adding the Ascendant for both day and night results in the **Commerce Saham** <note>Vanijya-saham</note>. (30)

### Verse 17
*In the Upajati meter:*
By day, subtract the Sun from Saturn and add the Sun's Lord; by night, subtract the Moon from Saturn and add the Moon's Lord for **Success**. Subtract Saturn from Venus for **Marriage**.

For a day birth, subtract the Sun from Saturn and add the Lord of the Sun's sign; for a night birth, subtract the Moon from Saturn and add the Lord of the Moon's sign to find the **Success in Work Saham** <note>Karyasiddhi-saham</note>. (31) Subtracting Saturn from Venus and adding the Ascendant for both day and night results in the **Marriage Saham** <note>Vivaha-saham</note>. (32)

**In the Upajati Meter—Subtract Mercury from Jupiter for a daytime birth; for a night birth, do the reverse. Subtract the Moon from Saturn and always add the sixth house <note>the house of enemies and debt</note> according to the stated direction. To find the House of Torment, subtract Venus. || 18 ||**

For a daytime birth, subtract Mercury from Jupiter; for a night birth, subtract Jupiter from Mercury and add the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term> to find the **Birth Saham (33)**. For both day and night, subtract the Moon from Saturn and add the Sixth House <note>Ripubhava</note> to find the **Torment Saham (34)**. || 18 ||

**In the Upajati Meter—Faith is found by the aforementioned direction; then subtract the Fortune Saham from the Knowledge Saham. Love is found by the same method. Strength and Body are known to be equal to Fame. For Dullness, subtract Mars. || 19 ||**

For both day and night, subtract Mars from Venus and add the Ascendant to find the **Faith Saham (35)**. For a daytime birth, subtract the Moon from Saturn, and for a night birth, subtract Saturn from the Moon, then add the Ascendant to find the **Falling of Water Saham (41)** <note>Paniya-patana: often relates to travel by water or rainfall</note>. || 20 ||

**In the Upajati Meter—Subtract Saturn from Mars for the Enemy Saham; in the night, it is reversed. From the Fortune Saham, subtract Mars for Prowess; in the night, it is reversed. For Means, subtract Jupiter from Saturn. || 21 ||**

For a daytime birth, subtract Saturn from Mars, and for a night birth, subtract Mars from Saturn, then add the Ascendant to find the **Enemy Saham (42)**. For a daytime birth, subtract Mars from the Fortune Saham, and for a night birth, subtract the Fortune Saham from Mars, then add the Ascendant to find the **Prowess Saham (43)** <note>Shaurya: courage or valor</note>. For a daytime birth, subtract Jupiter from Saturn, and for a night birth, subtract Saturn from Jupiter, then add the Ascendant to find the **Means Saham (44)** <note>Upaya: strategy or resources</note>. || 21 ||

->**Anushtubh Meter: Subtract the Moon from Venus and add the result to the Ascendant; this is always the Daughter Saham.**<-
->**Subtract the Sun from the Fortune Saham and add the result to the Ascendant; for night births, do the reverse. || 24 ||**<-

<note>original: "चन्द्रसितादपास्योक्तं..." (Chandra-sitad-apasyoktam...). This verse provides the mathematical formula for the Daughter Saham (Kanya Saham) and the Fortune Saham (Punya Saham).</note>

For both day and night, subtract the Moon from Venus and add the result to the Ascendant to find the **Daughter Saham (49)**. For a day birth, subtract the Sun from the Fortune Saham and add the Ascendant. For a night birth, subtract the Fortune Saham from the Sun...

<header>Including the Commentary in Common Language.</header>

By subtracting the Part of Fortune <note>original: "Punya Saham"</note> from the eleventh house and adding it, the Horse Saham <note>Ashwa Saham</note> becomes 50; these 50 Sahams were spoken of by the ancient teachers. Regarding other Sahams mentioned in different opinions, some are included within these, while others will be written in the table. The table of Sahams is forthcoming. One must conceptualize a <term>Saham</term> <note>A sensitive mathematical point in a horoscope calculated by the distance between two points added to the Ascendant</note> based on the specific house related to the matter being considered. For example, for brothers, one should use the third house; for a wife, the seventh house; and knowing the Ascendant, one should calculate the Part of Fortune and others. This is also the opinion of some authorities. || 24 ||

->Upajati Meter—Subtract the Saham's own lord from it; multiply those degrees by its local rising sign value and divide by three hundred. The result in days is the time of its fruition, occurring during its planetary period, or if that is not possible, then otherwise. || 25 ||<-

Regarding the results of the Saham, the <term>Time of Fruition</term> <note>Pakasamaya; the specific time when the predicted event will occur</note> is explained: to find the time of the Saham's result, subtract the longitude of the lord of that house from the Saham. Multiply the remaining degrees by the local rising sign values <note>ascensional differences</note> and divide by 300. The quotient should be known as the days until that Saham's fruition. Some hold the opinion that the days found by this method should be divided by 30, and the resulting signs should be added to the Sun's position at the time of the solar return <note>Varshapravesha</note>. If the signs exceed 12, subtract 12. The time when the Sun reaches this calculated position is the time of the Saham's fruition. Others say that according to the sequence of degrees, the result occurs when the <term>Dasha</term> <note>Planetary period or time-cycle</note> of the Saham's lord begins; this is universally accepted. Between these two opinions, the certainty is this: if the lord's period falls within the days calculated previously, the result will occur during that period. If the period begins after those days, the result will occur that many days after the start of the period. It should also be remembered that if the year ends by this calculation, the result should be predicted for the following year, though this raises many doubts. For this reason, there is the <term>Statement of Yadava</term> <note>Yadavavakya; a reference to an authoritative astrological text or author</note>:

> "One should find the difference between the Saham and its lord, starting from the preceding sign. 
> When the Sun reaches the sign resulting from that addition, the fruit is realized in that transit."

Meaning, for whichever house-related Saham one desires the result, calculate the difference from its preceding house and, at the start of the period—

<meta>catchword: at the start of the period—</meta>

**Vasantatilaka Meter**—If the Lord of the Saham <note>Sahamesh</note> is placed in its own sign of exaltation or other auspicious positions and aspects the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, or if the powerful Lord of the Saham aspects its own Saham, it is considered strong. If it does not aspect the Ascendant, it remains weak even if placed in an auspicious position. In this matter, one must also evaluate the strength of: 1. The Lord of the Sun's sign at birth, 2. The Lord of the Moon's sign at birth, 3. The Lord of the sign where the Full Moon of the birth month ends, and 4. The Lord of the sign where the New Moon of the birth month ends. Their strength should be judged in this same manner; from their strength, results similar to the Saham of Merit <note>Punya Saham</note> should be predicted. || 26 || 1 ||

Regarding the strength and weakness of the Sahams: if the Lord of the Saham is in its exaltation or other previously mentioned auspicious places and looks upon the Ascendant, or if it looks upon its own Saham, it is powerful. If it does not look upon the Ascendant, it is weak even if in an auspicious position. Furthermore, the strength of the Lord of the natal Sun-sign, the Lord of the natal Moon-sign, the Lord of the Full Moon's concluding sign, and the Lord of the New Moon's concluding sign must be considered using this same method. Based on their strength, one should declare results equivalent to the Saham of Merit. || 26 || 1 ||

**Anushtubh Meter**—A planet that is low in the Five-fold Strength <term>Panchavargiya-bala: a specific Tajika system of calculating planetary strength</term> (less than five units) and is not situated in a Place of Joy <term>Harsha-sthana: specific houses where planets gain strength</term>, and by implication does not aspect the Ascendant, is weak. If it is even in a minor position known as the <term>Musallah: a term related to the Triplicity or 'Trairashika' lords</term> and aspects the Ascendant, it is strong. It should be understood everywhere that being in one's own house or exaltation is "Great Authority," in one's own Term <note>Hadda</note> is "Medium Authority," and in one's own Triplicity or Musallah is "Minor Authority." || 27 || 2 ||

**Vasantatilaka Meter**—If a Saham is joined with or aspected by its own Lord or by benefic planets, and if its Lord is powerful, then that Saham will flourish. If it is not joined with or aspected by its Lord or by benefic planets, then the events associated with that Saham will not come to pass; this should be considered first. || 28 || 3 ||

# Tajika Neelakanthi
<page-num>90</page-num>

If the Saham <note>A sensitive mathematical point in the horoscope</note> is associated with or aspected by its own planetary lord or a benefic <note>A "benefic" is a naturally auspicious planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it produces auspicious results such as religious merit. This occurs in the second half of the year—that is, six months after the solar return. If it is associated with or aspected by malefic planets <note>Such as Mars or Saturn</note>, the inauspicious results occur in the first half of the year. || 32 || 7 ||

->In the Anustup meter: If a Saham is joined with a malefic but aspected by a benefic, the bad comes first, then the good.<-
->If joined with a benefic but aspected by a malefic, it is good at first and bad later. || 33 || 8 ||<-

The inherent quality of a Saham changes through planetary contact. If the Punya Saham <note>The Part of Fortune/Merit, calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant</note> is joined with a malefic but aspected by a benefic, it gives inauspicious results in the first half of the year and auspicious results in the second half. If it is joined with a benefic but aspected by a malefic, it gives auspicious results in the first half and inauspicious results in the second half. If it is both joined with and aspected by malefics, the entire year will be inauspicious; if it is both joined with and aspected by benefics, the entire year will be auspicious. || 33 || 8 ||

->In the Anustup meter: In whichever year the Punya Saham is auspicious, that year brings happiness.<-
->If this Saham is unfavorable, even other auspicious Sahams may not grant their fruit; therefore, consider the Punya Saham first. || 34 || 9 ||<-

In a year where the Punya Saham is auspicious according to the previously mentioned rules, that entire year is auspicious. Even if other Sahams are inauspicious, they cannot suddenly grant bad results if the Punya Saham is strong. Conversely, if the Punya Saham is weak or inauspicious, the year passes inauspiciously, and even if other Sahams are auspicious, they do not grant their good fruits. For this reason, the Punya Saham is the primary point to be considered in every "Birth Year" <note>The annual solar return chart</note>. || 34 || 9 ||

->In the Anustup meter: If in the birth chart it is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, or in the year chart it is struck by malefics,<-
->Or if its lord is combust, the Punya Saham destroys merit, wealth, and happiness. || 35 || 10 ||<-

If in the natal chart <note>The chart at the moment of birth</note> the Punya Saham is placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses <note>These are the 'Dusthanas' or difficult houses in Indian astrology</note>, and in the annual chart it is joined with malefics, or if the Sahamesh <note>The planetary lord of that specific Saham</note> is combust <note>Too close to the Sun, thus losing its power</note>, then it destroys religious merit, wealth, and happiness. || 35 || 10 ||

->In the Anustup meter: All Sahams should be reflected upon in this way for the birth and the year.<-
->For the Sahams of Sloth, Enemies, Strife, and Death, the results should be predicted in reverse. || 36 || 11 ||<-

<summary>This page details the timing of astrological effects based on the Punya Saham (Part of Fortune), explaining how its strength or weakness can override other factors in an annual forecast. It emphasizes that for negative Sahams like death or strife, the rules of benefic/malefic aspects are applied in reverse.</summary>

<page-num>91</page-num>
<header>With Commentary in the Common Tongue</header>

In the manner described, one should consider all the *Sahams* <note>Sensitive points in a horoscope calculated by the distance between two planets added to the Ascendant</note> in the birth chart and the yearly chart. If the *Punya Saham* <note>The Point of Fortune or Merit</note> is strong, there are gains of wealth and such; however, if the *Sahams* for Disease, Enemies, Strife, Obstacles, or Death are strong, the results are opposite and correspond to their names. If these five inauspicious *Sahams* are weak and produce bad results, then one should understand the year to be auspicious. || 36 || 11 ||

**In the Rathoddhata Meter—If the Point of Success is joined with or aspected by benefics, or forms a *Muthashila* <note>A Tajika aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of an event</note> with them, it grants victory. In battle, if it is aspected by or joined with both benefics and malefic planets, the wise say victory comes only after great suffering.** || 37 || 12 ||

If the *Karyasiddhi Saham* <note>Point of Success or Achievement of Work</note> is joined with or aspected by benefic planets, or forms a *Muthashila* yoga with a benefic, it grants victory in battle. If it is both joined/aspected by and forms a *Muthashila* with benefics, it grants an even greater victory. If it is aspected, joined, or in *Muthashila* with both benefics and malefics, it grants victory in battle only after much hardship. The same logic should be applied to the *Sahams* for marriage and other matters. Alternatively, this "Success" can refer to the completion of any task whatsoever. || 37 || 12 ||

**In the Manjubhashini Meter—If the Point of Strife is aspected by or joined with malefic planets, or if it forms a *Muthashila* with a malefic, it signifies death in conflict. However, if it is joined with or aspected by a benefic there, one attains victory; if the aspects are mixed, there is only the pain of the quarrel.** || 38 || 13 ||

If the *Kali Saham* <note>Point of Strife or Quarrel</note> is joined with both malefics and benefics but forms a *Muthashila* with a malefic planet, death occurs in the quarrel. If that same *Kali Saham* is joined with or aspected by a benefic planet, victory is achieved after only a little strife. When the aspects of malefic and benefic planets are equal, or it is joined by both, there is only the distress and exertion of the quarrel, with neither victory nor defeat as a final result. || 38 || 13 ||

**In the Upajati Meter—If the Point of Marriage is aspected by its own lord or a benefic, or joined with benefics, or forms a *Muthashila* with them, it brings the attainment of auspiciousness. If it is aspected by or joined with a mixture of planets, it happens through difficulty; but not if joined with cruel planets or the Lord of Death.** || 39 || 14 ||

If the *Vivaha Saham* <note>Point of Marriage</note> is joined with or aspected by its own planetary lord or a benefic planet, and forms a *Muthashila* with a benefic, it will bring about marriage. If it is simultaneously joined with or aspected by both benefic and malefic planets—and by extension forms an *Itthashala* <note>Another term for the Muthashila configuration, indicating the "mixing" of planetary influences</note> with a mixture of both—then marriage is attained with great difficulty.

<header>Tajika Neelakanthi</header>

If the planet is associated with or aspected by a malefic <note>a naturally harmful planet like Mars or Saturn</note> and forms a <term>Muthashila</term> <note>original: "मुथशिल"; an aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of an event</term>, then it will not allow the attainment of marriage. ॥ 39 ॥ 14 ॥

->**Upajati Meter—If the Lord of the Saham of Fame is in the eighth house, joined or aspected by a malefic, there is an immediate destruction of fame. There is a gain of infamy earned through sins; if the planet is devoid of strength, the glory of the entire lineage is destroyed. 40 ॥ 15 ॥**<-

If the <term>Lord of the Saham of Fame</term> <note>original: "यशसहमधीश"; a calculated point in the horoscope representing reputation</note> is in the eighth house <note>the house of death and transformation</note> and is joined with or aspected by a malefic, then the fame one has earned will be destroyed. Furthermore, one gains infamy related to one of the great sins committed by oneself. When this same Lord of the Saham of Fame is in the eighth house, joined/aspected by a malefic, and is also <term>combust</term> <note>original: "अस्तंगत"; too close to the Sun and thus weakened</term>, it destroys the fame passed down from one's ancestors, such as the father and grandfather; that is, it destroys the glory of one's entire lineage. ॥ 40 ॥ 15 ॥

->**Upajati Meter—If there is an Itthashala with a benefic, or if it is joined/aspected by a benefic and is endowed with strength, there will be an increase in fame, victory in battle, and the gain of vehicles and weapons. If there is a Saraf with a malefic, there is destruction of fame and wealth. ॥ 41 ॥ 16 ॥**<-

If the Lord of the Saham of Fame forms a <term>Muthashila</term> <note>original: "मुथशिली"; a favorable application of aspect</note> with a benefic planet, or is aspected by or joined with a benefic, then fame increases. By implication, there is also an increase in righteousness and gain of wealth, as well as victory in battle and the acquisition of vehicles like horses and weapons like bows. If the Lord of the Saham of Fame forms a <term>Muthashila</term> with malefic planets or an <term>Isarafa</term> <note>original: "ईसराफी"; a separating aspect indicating the passing or failure of an event</note> with a benefic, and is by implication <term>devoid of strength</term> <note>original: "नष्टबली"</note>, then infamy increases and wealth is destroyed. ॥ 41 ॥ 16 ॥

->**Upajati Meter—If the Saham of Hope and its Lord are free from the sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses, and are joined or aspected by benefics, one's desires are fulfilled, and there is gain of gold, wealth, clothes, and vehicles. If the lord of the <term>Disease Saham</term><note>A specific mathematical point in a birth chart used to predict illness</note> is a malefic planet, or is associated with or aspected by malefic planets, it should be known as the cause of disease. # Page 97
### With Language Commentary

In certain instances, the meaning of words can be confusing due to multiple associations—for example: *Guru* (teacher/heavy), *Gaurava* (weight/dignity), *Karma* (action/fate), *Raja-bala* (royal power), *Vapu* (body), and so on. To remove such doubts, it is stated that: *Guru* should be understood as the one who imparts instruction, specifically regarding scientific knowledge and intellect; *Vidya* (knowledge) refers to the Vedas; *Shastra* refers to the scriptures, including *Shruti* (divine revelation) and *Smriti* (traditional laws); *Jadya* refers to ignorance or the forgetting of texts; *Bala* refers to the army, capability, or physical strength; *Deha* refers to the physical body and its limbs; *Jala* refers to luster, like that of a diamond or gem, as well as water; and *Jala-patha* refers to a water route. These are their respective synonyms. || 56 || 31 ||

-> <note>original: "Gurutamandaleshatvam gauravam manashalita / Nigrahanugrahavibhurajachhatradilingabhak"</note>
The state of being a *Guru* implies being the lord of a district or a general king; *Gaurava* implies being eminent or possessing great honor. A King is defined as one who has the power of *Nigraha* <note>punishment or imprisonment</note> and *Anugraha* <note>bestowing favor or gifts</note> over territories large or small, and who bears the royal insignia such as the umbrella and the fly-whisk. || 57 || 32 ||

-> <note>In the Anustup meter</note>
*Mahatmya* is the name for the gravity or depth of counsel; *Dhriti* is the name for wisdom or fortitude. *Samarthya* refers to physical bodily power, and *Shaurya* <note>valor</note> refers to the heroic effort or capability used in the subduing of enemies. || 58 || 33 ||

-> <note>In the Anustup meter</note>
*Asha* is a name for desire, and also a name for a direction; *Shraddha* refers to a mind inclined toward righteous deeds, though here the primary meaning to be taken is "faith" or "trust." *Vanda* is the name for seeking refuge in others. *Paniya-patana* refers to rain or water falling from above, and it also carries the meaning of drowning in water. || 59 || 34 ||

-> <note>In the Anustup meter</note>
*Adhi* refers to mental anguish; *Vyadhi* refers to disease; *Tapa* refers to distress or heat. All of these are synonyms for *Mandhya* <note>sluggishness or affliction</note>. *Sapinda* refers to kinsmen or relatives. *Satyanrita* <note>the mixture of truth and falsehood</note> refers to the profession of trade or commerce. *Adhana* is remembered as the act of procreation or conception. || 60 || 35 ||

*Adhi* (mental pain), *Vyadhi* (physical disease), *Tapa* (torment), and *Santapa* (remorse/heat) are all synonyms for affliction—
