The term *Bandhava* <note>Relating to the Saham of Kinship</note> refers to relatives up to seven generations (*Sapinda*); *Satyalika* is a synonym for the commercial disposition of a merchant; *Prasava* is the name for conception and the production of offspring. || 60 || 35 ||

<term>Anustubh</term> <note>A poetic meter consisting of four quarters of eight syllables each</note>—The state of servitude is called *Parakarma* <note>literally "another's work"</note>; others are clear from their own names. ||
->One should determine the results appropriately, according to the lineage, caste, and nature of the person. || 61 || 36 ||<-

*Parakarma* is a synonym for servitude. The names of these many *Sahams* <note>Arabic Parts/Sensitive Points</note> are called synonyms because they have dual meanings; the remaining *Sahams* have clear names (such as Fortune, Marriage, etc.). One should declare the results after considering the family status and caste appropriately. || 61 || 36 ||

<term>Anustubh</term>—Happiness comes from the aspect or conjunction of benefic planets, according to the strength of the lord. ||
->In the Sahams of Poverty, Death, Maancha, Enemies, and Strife, the opposite is said. || 62 || 37 ||<-

All <term>Sahams</term> give auspicious results according to the strength of the Saham-lord and the aspect or conjunction of benefic planets. However, these five <term>Sahams</term>—Poverty, Death, *Maancha* <note>a specific technical point in Tajika astrology</note>, Enemies, and Strife—give the opposite results. That is to say, if there is a benefic aspect/conjunction and the lord is strong, they give inauspicious results consistent with their nature; but if there is a malefic conjunction/aspect and the Saham-lord is weak, they give auspicious results, contrary to their names. || 62 || 37 ||

<term>Anustubh</term>—Even at the time of a query, one should consider the <term>Saham</term> according to the desire of the petitioner. ||
->All of these are useful here, as people ask about various wonderful things. || 63 || 38 ||<-

If a birth chart is available, one should first consider the <term>Sahams</term> of the birth and then the subsequent yearly charts. For one who has no birth chart, one should consider Fortune and other <term>Sahams</term> from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>Lagna</note> of the query. Since petitioners ask many types of questions, one can answer all types using the <term>Sahams</term>. || 63 || 38 ||

<term>Vasantatilaka</term> <note>A Sanskrit meter of 14 syllables</note>—There was a leader of scholars, adorned with boundless virtues, who explained the words of the Lord of Serpents <note>original: "bhujangapa-gavih" referring to Patanjali's Great Commentary on grammar</note>, a knower of the Vedas, of excellent conduct, expert in the methods of literature, and a knower of the tradition of mathematics—Chintamani, the jewel of the vast Garga lineage. || 64 || 39 ||

At the conclusion of this system (*Tantra*), the author states his name and lineage: He was adorned with boundless virtues such as piety, scriptural scholarship, and was foremost among scholars; he was a commentator on the Great Commentary of Patanjali (the speech of Sheshanaga), a knower of Vedic knowledge, possessed of auspicious conduct, and a master of <term>Astrology</term> <note>Jyotish-shastra</note> including mathematics and the literary arts...

->With the Vernacular Commentary.<-

The astrologer named Chintamani, who became highly skilled in these methods, was the jewel of the lineage of the great sage Garga. <note>Garga is one of the legendary founding fathers of Indian astronomy and astrology.</note> || 64 || 39 ||

**Upajati Meter—His son is Ananta, possessed of infinite virtues, who, for the satisfaction of the wise and by casting aside flawed opinions, composed the Jataka Paddhati and interpreted the Kamadhenu, which is like a wish-fulfilling cow of speech. || 65 || 40 ||**

His son is the astrologer named Ananta, possessed of countless virtues, who milked the "Wish-Fulfilling Cow of Mathematics" <note>original: "Kamadhenu-Ganita"</note>—meaning he authored a commentary on the mathematical treatise *Kamadhenu*. **Indravajra Meter—Born of Mother Padma, the learned Sri Neelakantha, devoted to the Vedas and Shastras, composed this Sanjna Viveka, adorned with the Sahams, to please the scholar Shiva. || 66 || 41 ||**

The author, having previously revealed his father Ananta’s name, now declares his own: born of his mother named Padma, the learned Sri Neelakantha—an expert in the Vedas, the Shastras, Grammar, Mimamsa philosophy, Astrology, and Tantra—composed this *Sanjna Viveka*. This is a system of Tajika astrology <note>Tajika astrology is a branch of Indian astrology influenced by Persian and Arabic traditions, focusing on annual horoscopes.</note> adorned with the *Sahams* <note>term: Saham (Arabic: Sahm). These are specific sensitive points or "lots" calculated in a horoscope to predict specific life events.</note>. This work was created to please the scholar and reader named Shiva, a Brahmin of the Maharashtra region; or alternatively, it was composed to please Lord Mahadeva (Shiva), the omniscient Knower of the Three Times (past, present, and future) and the granter of auspiciousness. || 66 || 41 || Thus ends the third chapter, named the Analysis of Sahams, in the Neelakanthi vernacular commentary by Mahidhara. || 3 ||

**In the work composed by Sri Neelakantha, Mahidhara has written this vernacular commentary called 'Mahidhari' on the Sanjna Viveka, which increases the intellect, satisfies virtuous people, and delights the minds of the wise. || 42 ||**

Mahidhara has composed this vernacular commentary named *Mahidhari* on the *Sanjna Viveka*—the first system of the *Tajika Neelakanthi* composed by the astrologer Sri Neelakantha. This commentary is intended to sharpen the intellect, provide satisfaction to virtuous men, and bring joy to the hearts of right-minded readers. || 42 ||

->Thus ends the first section, the Sanjna Tantra, in the vernacular commentary on the Neelakanthi by Mahidhara.<-

## Salutations to the Great Lord Ganesha.
# Here Begins the Second System of the Neelakanthi.

---

> **Upendravajra Meter — Without whose grace even the hosts of gods, led by the Lord of the Universe <note>original: "Ishanmukha," referring to Shiva</note>, are unable to attain their own desires without obstacles; I bow to that Dhundhiraja <note>A name for Ganesha, the elephant-headed deity who removes obstacles</note> for the sake of obtaining great wisdom. || 1 ||**

The author, the learned teacher Neelakantha the Astrologer <note>term: Daivajna (one who knows the divine/fate)</note>, at the commencement of this second system of results in the *Tajika Neelakanthi*, offers salutations to Lord Ganesha for the removal of obstacles. He states: I bow to Dhundhiraja Ganesha for the attainment of true intelligence, for without His grace, even the assembly of gods including Mahadeva <note>Shiva</note> are not capable of achieving their respective desires without hindrance. || 1 ||

> **Rathoddhata Meter — The results of the planetary periods <note>term: Dashaphala (the fruit of time-cycles)</note> mentioned in natal horoscopy provide only a general or coarse timing for men. In that system, the astrologer’s intellect does not shine with precision; therefore, I shall speak of the annual results according to the ancient Tajika <note>term: Tajika (a system of Indian astrology incorporating Perso-Arabic techniques like solar returns)</note>. || 2 ||**

In natal astrology, the results of planetary periods are said to give the same result to humans over a very long duration. Here, the astrologer's intellect is not fully stimulated because, for example, the period of Venus is said to last for 20 years. No one experiences the exact same conditions for such a long duration. Therefore, I provide a subtle consideration of results based on the duration of a single solar year <note>term: Saura Varsha (the time it takes the Sun to return to its exact natal position)</note>, following the tradition of the ancient Tajika. || 2 ||

> **(Gatha Meter) When the Sun at that moment becomes equal to the Sun at the time of birth, that is the moment of the "Year Entry" <note>term: Varshapravesha (Solar Return)</note>. There is no rule regarding the lunar date <note>term: Tithi</note> and so on being the same. By adding one sign at a time, when the Sun is equal in degrees and so on, that is the "Month Entry." If the minutes are equal, it is the "Day Entry." || 3 ||**

When the calculated position of the Sun <note>term: Suryaspashta (true longitude of the sun)</note> in signs and degrees matches the Sun’s position at the time of birth, that is the exact time of the Year Entry. In determining the Year Entry, it is not a rule that the lunar date or other calendar elements must be identical, as discrepancies often occur. By adding exactly one sign <note>30 degrees</note> to that same clear position while keeping the degrees and minutes the same, the Sun's position for the "Month Entry" is established. Furthermore, by adding one degree at a time to this position for whichever month's "Day Entry" one wishes to calculate—keeping the sign of that month and the minutes and seconds as they were before—the Day Entry is determined. <meta>This page continues the technical instructions for calculating astrological timing, specifically focusing on deriving the "Ishtakala" (desired time of birth or event) from the "Lagnaspashta" (calculated ascendant).</meta>

<page-num>101</page-num>
->**"Example"** of calculating the Desired Time from the Calculated Ascendant<-

The calculated Sun at the time of birth is 0 signs, 18 degrees, 42 minutes, and 31 seconds <note>0|18|42|31</note>. On Saturday, the 12th day of the dark fortnight of the month of Vaishakha in the year 1943 <term>Samyat: a traditional Hindu calendar era</term>, the desired time <term>Ishtaghati: time elapsed since sunrise measured in ghatis</term> is 13:54. In the 38th year of life, the calculated Sun remains the same. Now, from this, we must determine the calculated ascendant, and from that ascendant, find the desired time. The method for finding the ascendant from the Sun is clearly explained with examples in the commentary on verses 21, 22, and 23 of the *Sanjna-Tantra*.

For finding the desired time from the Sun, the half-verse from the *Graha-Laghava* <note>A classic 16th-century astronomical treatise</note> states: "The time remaining for the Sun to cross its sign, added to the time the ascendant has already spent in its sign, plus the rising times of the intervening signs, constitutes the desired time." Following this sequence, the desired time is calculated from the ascendant.

**"Example"**
Precession of the Equinoxes <term>Ayanamsha</term>: 22:44.
Calculated Sun: 0|18|42|31.
Calculated Ascendant <term>Lagnaspashta</term>: 3|10|27|3.
Tropical Sun <term>Sayana: the Sun's position adjusted for precession</term>: 1|11|26|31.
Subtracting the degrees from 30, the remaining portion to be traversed <term>Bhogyansha</term> is 18|33|29. When calculated against the rising time, the "remaining time" is 150|19|9|12.
The Tropical Ascendant is 4|3|11|3. Multiplying this by its specific rising time and dividing by 30, the "elapsed time" <term>Bhuktakala</term> is 37|40|45.
Adding this to the Sun's remaining time (150|19|9|12), we get 187|59|57. Now, we must add the local rising values <term>Swadeshiya Khanda</term> of the signs falling between the Sun and the Tropical Ascendant. Here, we add Gemini (300) and Cancer (346). The total is 833|59|57. Dividing this by 60, the result is 13 *ghatis* and a remainder of 53 *palas* and 59 *vipalas*. By the rule of rounding up (if more than half, add one), this becomes 13:54, which is the desired time. If for any reason the desired time is lost, but the ascendant and Sun positions are known, one can retrieve the time in this manner. This has been written here as a relevant aside. || 3 ||

Having calculated the strength of all planets according to the prescribed methods, I shall now explain the reasoning for determining the Lord of the Year. || 4 ||

The author says that after calculating the true positions of the planets and the houses (ascendant, etc.) as previously described, the intelligent astrologer should determine the strength of the planets and their portions. To facilitate this, I will now explain the logic for appointing the Lord of the Year <term>Varshesha: the planetary ruler of the astrological year</term>. || 4 ||

->**Rathoddhata Meter**<-
> The Lord of the birth ascendant, the Lord of the year ascendant, and the Lord of the Muntha <note>The Muntha is a mathematical point that progresses one sign per year from the birth ascendant</note> are the first three. The Lord of the Tri-Rashi <note>A specific dignity based on the element of the sign and whether the chart is day or night</note> is the fourth. The Lord of the Sun's sign (for a day birth) or the Lord of the Moon's sign (for a night birth) is the fifth. These five should be carefully considered. // 5 //

The five authorities are: 1. The Lord of the birth ascendant <term>Janmalagna-pati: the planet ruling the rising sign at the moment of birth</term>, 2. The Lord of the year ascendant, 3. The Lord of the sign where the Muntha is located, 4. The Lord of the Tri-Rashi (determined by the sequence of Sun, Venus, Saturn, etc.), and 5. The Lord of the Sun's sign if the year begins during the day, or the Lord of the Moon's sign if the year begins at night. The specific methods for these were explained previously in the *Samjna Tantra* <note>The first section of this book dealing with terminology</note>. // 5 //

->**Upajati Meter**<-
> Whichever among these is the strongest and casts an aspect <note>A planetary "glance" or influence</note> upon the ascendant becomes the Year Lord. One who does not aspect the ascendant cannot be the Year Lord, regardless of strength. If strengths are equal, the one with the superior aspect is chosen by the wise. // 6 //

After establishing the five authorities as described, one must examine their aspectual strength <term>Drigbala: strength gained through planetary positioning</term> and their five-fold strength <term>Panchavargi-bala</term>. The planet that possesses the most strength and also "sees" (aspects) the ascendant is designated as the Year Lord <term>Varshesha: the planetary ruler of the year</term>. If a planet is the strongest but does not aspect the ascendant, it cannot be the Year Lord. If the strongest planet's aspect is full, it is chosen; in its absence, one with slightly less strength but a better aspect is selected. If two or more are equally strong, the one with the more powerful aspect on the ascendant wins. Even a very strong planet is disqualified if it lacks an aspect to the ascendant. // 6 //

->**Upajati Meter**<-
> If the aspects and strengths are all equal, or if all are weak, then the Lord of the Muntha becomes the Year Lord. If none of the five aspect the ascendant, then the one with the highest numerical strength is considered the ruler of the year. // 7 //

If all five authorities have an equal aspect on the ascendant and their strengths are also equal, or if all are found to be weak (according to the rules of planetary debility), then the Lord of the Muntha sign is appointed as the Year Lord. If none of the five planets aspect the ascendant, the planet with the highest strength is chosen. If all five have a full aspect, the strongest among them is the Year Lord. Some authorities suggest that if no planet has clear superiority in strength or aspect, the Lord of the Year Ascendant becomes the "King" (Year Lord). Others hold the opinion that in such a case, the planet holding the most minor dignities—such as its exaltation, sign, Navamsha <note>ninth-part division</note>, Drekkana <note>ten-degree division</note>, or Hudda <note>bounds/terms</note>—should be the King. According to the previously mentioned method, whoever becomes the <term>Year Lord</term> <note>original: "Varshasha"</note> should also be known as the first ruler of the periods, since he is the king of all the planets ruling the sub-periods; his influence is felt slightly in all the periods. And the strength of the <term>Year Lord</term> should be calculated according to the <term>Panchavargi</term> <note>A five-fold system of calculating planetary strength</note> method in the birth chart as well as the yearly chart. By combining the strength of the birth and the year, one should determine the <term>Strength-Weakness</term> <note>original: "Balabala"</note>. If it is strong in both, it is called "fully powerful" and gives auspicious results throughout the entire year. In this same order, one should understand the best, middling, and least strength. With low strength, the result is middling; with the least strength, it is inauspicious; and with neutral strength, one should judge the results as neutral for the whole year. The method for <term>Strength-Weakness</term> has been fully described. ॥ 33 ॥

The planet with which the Year Lord forms an <term>Itthashala</term> gives various auspicious results according to its previously mentioned nature. If there is an <term>Isarafa</term> <note>original: "Esaraaf" - a separating aspect where the influence is fading</note> yoga with a benefic planet, it gives a small amount of auspicious fruit. If there is an <term>Itthashala</term> with a malefic planet, it gives undesirable results. One should judge the best, middling, or lowest strength based on the <term>Strength-Weakness</term> analysis. ॥ 34 ॥

**Anustubh Meter**—In whatever *Hadda* <note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as 'Terms' in Western astrology</note> a planet is placed and receives light; if it is in a similar state in the birth and the year-chart, it bestows its own results. || 35 ||

If a planet in the birth chart is in a certain *Hadda* and receives the brilliance of another, and in the year-chart it is also in a similar *Hadda*, then it transfers its results to the related planet. That is to say, if a planet is in the same *Hadda* as it was at birth and forms a *Muthashila* <note>A Tajika aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of an event</note> with any planet, it takes the brilliance of that birth planet. For example, if in the birth chart Mars, the lord of the house of kingdom <note>The 10th house</note>, is at 20 degrees of Aries in its own *Hadda*, and a planet like Venus, the lord of the house of happiness <note>The 4th house</note>, is at 17 degrees and forms a *Muthashila* to receive the brilliance; and if in the year-chart Mars is again in its own *Hadda* and forms a *Muthashila* with Venus, then Venus, in its period, will give results equal to the nature of Mars and also results related to the tenth house. || 35 ||

**Anustubh Meter**—If the planet capable of giving results in the birth chart forms a *Musaripha* <note>Also known as Ithasala-Mussaripha; a separating aspect where the faster planet has passed the slower one, often indicating a missed opportunity or cancellation</note> with the year-ascendant lord or the year-lord, then that result does not manifest in that year. || 36 ||

The planet which is capable of giving auspicious or inauspicious results from the birth chart—if in the year-chart it forms a *Musaripha* yoga with the lord of the year-ascendant or the year-lord, then the results mentioned at the time of birth do not occur in that year. If there is an *Isarapha* <note>Another term for the separating Musaripha aspect</note> with these, the birth results manifest in the year. If there is neither *Isarapha* nor *Musaripha*, then the birth results remain in the birth chart and the year results in the year chart. An example of this is in the next verse. || 36 ||

**Indravajra Meter**—If the lord of the house of children beholds the house of children in the birth chart, it is capable of giving a son. But if in the year-chart, it forms a *Musaripha* with the year-lord of children, then there is the loss of a son in that year. || 37 ||

If at the time of birth the lord of the house of children <note>The 5th house</note> aspects the house of children—by implication, or is situated in the house of children—it has the power to grant a son during its period. In the year-chart, if that same birth-lord of children forms a *Musaripha* yoga with the year-ascendant lord, the year-lord, or the fifth-house lord, then in this year, it will certainly cause the loss of a son. This is the example of the previous verse. All other houses should be considered in this same manner. || 37 ||

**Anustubh Meter**—If the year-lord Jupiter is in the *Hadda* of a friend, and the Moon is seen with a friendly aspect, then the year is auspicious for the person intended. || 38 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi

If <term>Jupiter</term> <note>Sanskrit: Brihaspati; the planet of wisdom and expansion</note> is the Lord of the Year, and in the birth chart <term>the Moon</term> <note>Sanskrit: Chandra</note> forms an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>A Tajika aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of an event</note> with Jupiter, and if Jupiter is in its own <term>Hadda</term> <note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign, similar to 'terms' in Western astrology</note> and aspects the Moon during that year, then the Moon transferring its light to Jupiter from the birth position will make this year yield auspicious results. || 38 ||

In this same way, scholars should deliberate by observing the relationship between the strengths and weaknesses of the birth and annual charts, as well as the three yogas: the future <term>Muthashila</term> <note>An applying aspect</note>, the current <term>Muthashila</term>, and the <term>Isarafa</term> <note>A separating aspect, usually indicating the fading of an influence</note>. These are merely the primary characteristics; all other considerations should be made in a similar fashion. || 39 ||

-> Thus ends the first chapter titled "Description of the Results of the Year Lord" in the vernacular commentary of the Nilakanthi, composed by Mahidhar, within the Varshatantra. || 1 || <-

### Now, the Description of the Muntha.

> <term>Upajati Meter</term>—From one's birth ascendant, the <term>Muntha</term> <note>A mathematical point that progresses exactly one zodiac sign per year</note> moves by traveling through one sign every year. By adding the number of elapsed years to the birth ascendant and dividing by twelve, the resulting sign is the Muntha for humans. || 1 ||

The name of the birth <term>Ascendant</term> <note>Sanskrit: Lagna; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> is Muntha; it rotates in sequence by occupying one <term>Zodiac Sign</term> <note>Sanskrit: Rashi</note> each year. For example, if the birth Ascendant is Leo, then in the second year it will be in Virgo, in the third year in Libra, and so on. Again, in the thirteenth year, it returns to the birth Ascendant of Leo, and in the fourteenth year, it is in Virgo—this is the sequence. By adding the elapsed years to the birth Ascendant and dividing by twelve, the remainder indicates the sign the Muntha occupies for that year. The exact degree of the birth Ascendant remains the exact degree of the Muntha; only the sign increases by one each year. || 1 ||

> <term>Anushtubh Meter</term>—Every day it increases by five minutes of arc through proportional calculation. Some sages say it moves two and a half degrees in a month. || 2 ||

For the commencement of the month or the day, the calculation for the Muntha is done by the <term>Rule of Three</term> <note>Sanskrit: Trairashika; a mathematical proportion</note>: if it traverses one sign (30 degrees) in one solar year, then how much does it move in one month? One sign is 30...

<header>Including the Commentary in Common Language.</header>

One degree is known to consist of 60 minutes. By applying the <term>Rule of Three</term> <note>a mathematical method to find a fourth value from three known values</note>, we find that in one month the Muntha moves 2 degrees and 30 minutes, and in one day it moves 5 minutes. To find the precise position of the Muntha for a monthly chart, add 2 degrees and 30 minutes to the Muntha of the yearly chart; continue adding 2 degrees and 30 minutes for each subsequent month. For a daily chart, simply add 5 minutes for every passing day. || 2 ||

> <note>original: "Anu." - Anushtubh meter</note>—Happiness comes from the aspect of its lord or a benefic planet; fear and disease come from the aspect of an enemy. The results are described based on the aspects and conjunctions of the houses. || 3 ||

The results of the Muntha are as follows: the lord of the sign in which the Muntha is located is called the <term>Munthesh</term> <note>Lord of the Muntha</note>. The Muntha grants happiness if it is aspected by its own lord or by a benefic <note>auspicious</note> planet. However, if it is aspected by an enemy planet or a weak malefic <note>inconstant</note> planet, it brings fear and illness. Its effects are determined by the aspects and conjunctions it forms within the houses. || 3 ||

> <note>original: "Anu." - Anushtubh meter</note>—It is inauspicious in the 4th, 7th, 12th, 6th, and 8th houses from the Year-Ascendant. In the 9th, 10th, and 11th houses, it grants happiness; elsewhere, it gives wealth through effort. || 4 ||

The Muntha is not considered auspicious if located in the 4th (Happiness), 7th (Setting/Partnership), 12th (Final), 6th (Enemy), or 8th (Death/Vulnerability) houses from the <term>Varshalagna</term> <note>the Ascendant of the solar return or yearly chart</note>. It provides happiness when placed in the 9th (Virtue), 10th (Action), or 11th (Gain) houses. In the remaining houses—the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th—it grants wealth, but only through personal effort and enterprise. || 4 ||

> <note>original: "Upaja." - Upajati meter</note>—Destruction of enemies, mental satisfaction, increase in glory, favor from the king, physical health, and various enterprises; the Muntha in the first house bestows wealth. || 5 ||

Regarding the results of the Muntha by house: If the Muntha is in the 1st house (Ascendant), enemies are destroyed, the mind remains satisfied, and one's influence increases. One receives favors from the government or authorities, the body remains healthy and robust, various new ventures are undertaken, and wealth is gained. || 5 ||

> <note>original: "Upaja." - Upajati meter</note>—Wealth through enthusiasm, fame, respect among kin, shelter from the king, enjoyment of sweet foods, strength, nourishment, and happiness occur when the Muntha is in the house of wealth during the year. || 6 ||

If the Muntha is in the 2nd house, wealth comes through enthusiastic effort and fame increases. One receives honor among their kinsmen and community, finds patronage from the authorities, enjoys fine and sweet foods, and experiences physical strength, vitality, and general happiness. || 6 ||

> If the *Muntha* is in the tenth house, one receives grace from the king and performs favors for one's own people. Success in noble deeds and devotion to gods and Brahmins are achieved; fame increases, it grants many kinds of financial gain, and it also grants high position <note>original: padāptim; meaning a promotion or attainment of a high post</note>. || 14 ||

---

**Upajati Meter—** If the *Muntha* reaches the Eleventh House, there are sensual pleasures, good fortune, freedom from disease, and mental clarity. Wealth comes through the patronage of the king, and the attainment of good friends, sons, and desired goals occurs. || 15 ||
> If the *Muntha* is in the eleventh house, there is enjoyment of the eight types of luxury, good fortune, health, and a happy mind. Wealth is gained through royal support, good friends and sons are acquired, and one's heart's desires are fulfilled. || 15 ||

---

**Upajati Meter—** Excessive expenditure, association with wicked people, diseases in the body, and lack of success despite great effort; loss of religion and wealth occurs when the *Muntha* is in the Twelfth House, and there is even enmity with one's own people. || 16 ||
> If the *Muntha* is in the twelfth house, expenses will be very high, one falls into the company of evil men, disease enters the body, and efforts in valor go to waste. There is a loss of religious merit and wealth, and enmity arises with virtuous people. || 16 ||

---

**Anushtup Meter—** If the house where the *Muntha* is placed is aspected by <note>term: drishti; the "glance" or astrological aspect of a planet</note> or joined with cruel planets, the good results of that house are destroyed and the inauspicious results increase. || 17 ||

Regarding the specific results of the **Muntha** <note>A sensitive point in the yearly chart that moves one sign per year from its position at birth</note>, it is said that if the **house** <term>Bhava: a specific area of life, such as wealth or health</term> is occupied by a malefic planet, or if a cruel planet casts a hostile aspect upon it, then even if the Muntha is placed in a generally auspicious position, it will not grant the good results of that house. On the contrary, the inauspicious results will increase. || 17 ||

**In the Bhujangaprayata meter—**
If the Muntha is joined with or aspected by its own lord or a benefic planet, or if its lord is powerful, or if it forms an **Itthashala** <term>A favorable aspect or "link" in Tajika astrology, similar to a planetary application</term> with its lord or a benefic planet, it increases the auspicious results of the house it occupies. If the opposite is true, one should carefully deliberate and conclude that the results will be otherwise. || 18 ||

If the Muntha is joined with or aspected by its own lord or a benefic planet, and the lord is strong, or if it is in an Itthashala yoga with its lord or a benefic, then it enhances the good fortune related to that house. Otherwise, it does not increase the good results. Furthermore, if it is weak—meaning it is not aspected by its lord or a benefic—or if it forms a **Musaripha** <term>A "separation" or unfavorable aspect where the faster planet has passed the slower one</term> with a malefic planet, then it destroys the good results of that house and increases the bad. One should predict the auspicious or inauspicious results of a house by thus evaluating the strength of the Muntha. || 18 ||

**In the Bhujangaprayata meter—**
If the Muntha is situated in the 6th, 8th, 7th, 12th, or 4th house from the **birth ascendant** <term>Janma-lagna: the rising sign at the moment of birth</term>, and in the yearly chart it is joined with or afflicted by malefic planets, it destroys the house it occupies. For example, if in the 2nd house it destroys wealth, in the 3rd house it destroys brothers, and so on. However, if in the yearly chart it is joined with or aspected by its own lord or a benefic planet, this destruction does not occur; instead, it yields auspicious results. || 19 ||

**In the Anushtup meter—**
When the Muntha is afflicted in both ways, the house is destroyed entirely.
When it is auspicious in both ways, that house flourishes greatly. || 20 ||

If the Muntha is in an auspicious position relative to both the birth ascendant and the **yearly ascendant** <term>Varsha-lagna: the rising sign at the moment the sun returns to its birth position</term>, and is not afflicted by malefic planets, then the auspicious results of that house—meaning the growth of that house—will manifest. For example, from the birth ascendant...

If the <term>Muntha</term><note>A mathematical point in a yearly chart that moves one sign per year from the birth ascendant</note> is in the fifth house from the <term>Varshalagna</term><note>The ascendant or rising sign of the annual solar return chart</note> and is associated with or aspected by its own lord or a benefic planet, it brings about an increase in progeny. Conversely, if it is situated in an inauspicious house relative to both the birth and annual charts, or if it is associated with, aspected by, or in an <term>Itthashala</term><note>A specific planetary aspect or configuration in Tajika astrology indicating the fulfillment of an event</note> with malefic planets, that particular house's significance will certainly be destroyed. || 20 ||

> <note>original: "Anushtup" (a poetic meter)</note>--If the Muntha is placed in an inauspicious house in the annual chart, or occupies the same house it held at birth, ||
> and is afflicted by cruel planets, it destroys that house; if joined with benefics, it brings auspicious results. || 21 ||

If the Muntha is in the 4th, 6th, 8th, or 12th houses (considered "dusthana" or difficult houses) from the <term>Janmalagna</term><note>The ascendant at the time of birth</note>, and similarly placed in inauspicious houses in the annual chart, and is further weakened by the association or aspect of malefic planets or the combustion of its lord, it destroys the fruits of that house. However, if it is associated with or aspected by its own lord or forms a favorable Itthashala, it yields auspicious results. || 21 ||

> <note>original: "Bhujangaprayata" (a poetic meter)</note>--If the Muntha is in the fourth house from the birth ascendant and is joined with a benefic planet, it ensures the gain of wealth and land from the father. If joined with malefic planets, it causes fear from the government and great hardships in life. Similarly, one should deliberate on its placement in the eighth house; if joined with benefics, it is auspicious, and if with malefics, it is inauspicious. The same logic should be applied to the sixth and other houses by using one's intelligence to judge the relative strength of the Muntha. || 22 ||

> <note>original: "Shalini" (a poetic meter)</note>--In whichever house the Muntha is aspected by its lord or a benefic, the corresponding house from the birth chart will see growth. ||
> Likewise, destruction is said to occur through malefics; however, if the <term>Varshesha</term><note>The planetary ruler of the year</note> is powerful, happiness prevails. || 23 ||

If the Muntha in the annual chart is aspected by or associated with its own lord or a benefic planet, it increases the prosperity of whichever house it represents in the birth chart. For example: if the Muntha is in the 4th house of the annual chart and is joined with a benefic or its lord, and this same position corresponds to the 3rd house from the birth ascendant, then there will be auspicious results regarding siblings this year. Conversely, if it is associated with or aspected by malefic planets, the house corresponding to its position from the birth ascendant will suffer loss. However, if the Lord of the Year is strong and is a benefic planet, the aforementioned negative effects of a malefic-associated Muntha will not come to pass. || 23 ||

# Now, the Results of the Muntha Associated with or Aspected by Planets

->**Upajati Meter**<-
*If the Muntha is in the Sun's sign, or joined with the Sun, or aspected by the Sun, it grants kingdom and association with kings. It bestows the highest attainment of virtues and changes in residence; such are the results of the aspect as well. || 24 ||*

The results of the Muntha <note>The Muntha is a mathematical point in a yearly horoscope that moves one sign per year; its position is crucial for annual predictions.</note> associated with each planet are now described: If the Muntha is in the Sun's sign (Leo, the 5th sign), or is with the Sun, or is aspected <note>In astrology, an 'aspect' is a geometric relationship between planets that influences their effects.</note> by the Sun, the person gains a kingdom (or status) according to their family lineage, enjoys the company of rulers, and obtains excellent comforts such as women, fine clothes, and ornaments. || 24 ||

->**Upajati Meter**<-
*Joined with Mars, in a sign of Mars, or aspected by Mars, it causes diseases of bile and heat, injury by weapons, and aggravation of the blood; especially so if aspected by Saturn or in a sign of Saturn. || 25 ||*

If the Muntha is joined with or aspected by Mars, or is in the signs of Mars (Aries or Scorpio, the 1st and 8th signs), it causes disorders of the bile <term>Pitta: one of the three humors in traditional medicine, associated with fire and heat</term> and heat-related illnesses. It also brings suffering through weapon injuries and blood disorders. If such a Muntha is also joined with or aspected by Saturn, or is in a sign of Saturn while influenced by Mars, the aforementioned ill effects are greatly increased. Regarding the Muntha, Saturn and Mars produce similarly harsh results. || 25 ||

->**Upajati Meter**<-
*Joined with the Moon, in the Moon's sign, or aspected by the Moon, it gives an increase in righteousness and fame, health, and great satisfaction; but from the aspect of malefic planets, it brings great sorrow. || 26 ||*

If the Muntha is joined with the Moon, in the Moon's sign (Cancer, the 4th sign), or aspected by the Moon, it increases one's fortitude and fame. It brings a great increase in health and happiness. However, if there is also an aspect from a malefic planet <note>Malefics typically include Mars, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu.</note>, it causes great sorrow. || 26 ||

->**Upajati Meter**<-
*Joined or aspected by Mercury or Venus, or in their signs, it brings gain of women, intelligence, and happiness. It bestows incomparable righteousness and fame, though suffering arises from the aspect or association of malefic planets. || 27 ||*

If the Muntha is joined with or aspected by Mercury or Venus, or is in their signs (Taurus, Gemini, Virgo, or Libra—the 2nd, 3rd, 6th, and 7th signs), the person gains happiness through women and the exercise of intelligence. It also grants peerless virtue and reputation. If there is an aspect or conjunction with a malefic planet in this configuration, suffering occurs. || 27 ||

->**Upajati Meter**<-
*If the Muntha is joined or aspected by Jupiter, or is in a sign of Jupiter, it gives happiness through sons and wife. It bestows gems, clothing, and the joy of righteousness; through a favorable Ithashala <note>original: "इत्थशाल" (Itthashala) — a specific Tajika astrological aspect indicating the coming together of two planets' influences</note> and other factors, it brings the gain of a kingdom. || 28 ||*

->**Commentary with Translation**<-

If the <term>Muntha</term><note>A sensitive point in a yearly horoscope that moves one sign per year</note> is joined with or aspected by <term>Jupiter</term><note>Sanskrit: Brihaspati</note>, or if it is located in the signs of Jupiter (Sagittarius or Pisces), it grants the happiness of a wife and children, as well as the joy of possessing gems, fine clothing, and performing <term>Dharma</term><note>Righteous duties or religious merit</note>. If it also forms an <term>Itthashala</term><note>A specific astrological aspect or "link" between planets in Persian-Arabic influenced Vedic astrology</note> with a benefic planet, the person attains a high status or kingdom according to their family lineage. || 28 ||

**If the Muntha is in the house of Saturn, or joined/aspected by him, it causes wind-related ailments (Vata). It brings the loss of vehicles and fear of fire, along with loss of wealth; however, if Jupiter aspects it, auspicious results are obtained. || 29 ||**

If the Muntha is in the signs of <term>Saturn</term><note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, or is joined with or aspected by Saturn, it produces diseases related to <term>Vata</term><note>The "wind" humor in Ayurvedic medicine, often relating to joints or nerves</note>. It also causes the loss of vehicles. However, if there is also an aspect from Jupiter upon it, then it yields auspicious results as well. || 29 ||

**If the Muntha is in the "Face" of the North Node (Rahu), there is gain of wealth, fame, happiness, and the elevation of Dharma. If joined or aspected by Venus and Jupiter, one gains a position of authority and acquisitions of gold, gems, and garments. || 30 ||**

If the Muntha is located in the degrees designated as the "Face" of <term>Rahu</term><note>The North Node of the Moon</note>, then wealth is acquired, and there is an increase in fame, happiness, and religious merit. If it is joined with or aspected by <term>Venus</term><note>Sanskrit: Shukra</note> and Jupiter, then one attains a position of power <gloss>infantry/authority</gloss> and gains of gold, precious stones, and clothing. || 30 ||

**The degrees yet to be traversed by Rahu are its "Face," and the degrees already passed are the "Back." The "Tail" is in the seventh sign from there; having reflected on this, one should declare the results. || 31 ||**

The characteristics of Rahu's Face and Tail are now described. Rahu's <term>retrograde motion</term><note>Moving backward through the zodiac</note> is well known. The degrees remaining for Rahu to cover in a sign are called the "Face," and the degrees already traversed are called the "Back." Some authorities hold the opinion that the 15 degrees before and after Rahu's position constitute the Face and Back. <term>Ketu</term><note>The South Node of the Moon</note>, which resides in the seventh sign from Rahu, is called the "Tail." One should predict results after careful consideration of these distinctions. || 31 ||

**In the "Back" portion, it is not a giver of auspiciousness; from the "Tail" portion, there is fear of enemies and suffering. From the aspect of malefic planets, there is loss of wealth and happiness; if the Muntha is thus situated at birth, it causes the destruction of home and wealth. || 32 ||**

If the Muntha is in the "Back" of Rahu—meaning within the 15 degrees behind Rahu's position or until the end of the previous sign—it does not give auspicious results. If it is in the "Tail" <insert>joined with Ketu</insert>, it brings fear from enemies and physical distress. Furthermore, if aspected by malefic planets, it causes the loss of wealth and happiness. Similarly, if the Muntha is so placed at the time of birth, it leads to the ruin of one's house and finances. || 32 ||

# Page 120
## Tajaka Nilakanthi

**Upajati Meter — Those planets which are strong at the time of birth but weak at the time of the annual revolution grant auspicious results at the end of the year.**
**In the opposite case, misfortune is said to occur earlier; if they are equal in both charts, the results are balanced throughout. || 33 ||**

Those planets which are strong in the birth chart <note>the natal horoscope</note> and weak in the annual chart <note>the Varshaphala</note> give auspicious results in the first half of the year and inauspicious results in the second half due to their weakness. Opposite to this, those which are weak at birth but strong in the annual chart give inauspicious results in the first half and auspicious results in the second half. If they are of equal strength in both charts, they provide consistent results throughout the entire year. || 33 ||

**Upajati Meter — If the Lord of the Muntha is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or in the fourth; or if it is combust, retrograde, or joined/aspected by malefic planets;**
**Or if it is in the fourth or seventh house from a cruel planet, it will not be auspicious and will cause disease and loss of wealth. || 34 ||**

If the lord of the <term>Muntha</term> <note>Muntha: A specific point in Tajaka astrology that moves one sign per year from its natal position</note> is located in the 6th, 8th, 12th, or 4th houses, or if it is "combust" <note>hidden by the sun's glare</note>, or in retrograde motion, or associated with/aspected by "malefic" <note>harmful</note> planets, or if it sits in the 4th or 7th house from a "cruel" <note>natural malefic like Mars or Saturn</note> planet (meaning it is under an inimical gaze), then it does not grant auspicious results. Instead, it creates the onset of disease and the destruction of wealth. || 34 ||

**Upajati Meter — If it is joined with or aspected by the Lord of the Eighth House, or seen by the "Kshuta" aspect, it is even then not auspicious.**
**If both these yogas are present, death occurs; if only one yoga is present, they say it is a pain equal to death. || 35 ||**

If the <term>Munthesh</term> <note>The planetary ruler of the Muntha sign</note>, the Lord of the Year, and the Lord of the Eighth House are joined, or if they are seen by the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th "Kshuta" aspect <note>a specific Tajaka aspect</note>, it does not give good results. One "yoga" <note>planetary combination</note> is this, and the other was mentioned in the previous verse (starting with "In the sixth, eighth..."). In a year where both these combinations occur, they result in death. If only one is present, it causes suffering equivalent to death. || 35 ||

**Anushtubh Meter — If the Muntha or its Lord is associated with or aspected by benefics in the birth chart,**
**It brings auspiciousness at the start of the year; if in the annual chart, then at the end; otherwise, it is inauspicious. || 36 ||**

### Now, the Consideration of Misfortunes in the Year.

> In the Anustubh meter — If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the eighth house, or the Lord of the eighth house is in the Ascendant and aspected by Mars; or if Mercury and Jupiter are set <note>set: 'astangata' or combust, meaning too close to the sun to be seen</note>, there will be wounds from weapons, calamity, or death. || 1 ||

In grammar, the word *Rishta* is derived from the root *Rish*, meaning 'to injure' or 'to harm.' Through the application of the 'Anit' and 'Kta' suffixes, the term *Rishta* is established. While the term *Arishta* (formed with a negative prefix) might seem to mean the opposite, in all astrological texts, the terms *Rishta* and *Arishta* are used synonymously to mean 'misfortune.' 

Now, describing the combinations for misfortune: if the Lord of the Year's Ascendant is in the eighth house <note>the house of death and longevity</note> and is aspected by Mars; or if the Lord of the eighth house is in the Ascendant and aspected by Mars (or by extension, any malefic planet); or if Mercury and Jupiter are combust—then one suffers wounds from weapons, faces great adversity, or meets death. These three outcomes are determined by the degree of planetary weakness: ordinary weakness leads to wounds, greater weakness to adversity, and extreme weakness to death. There are three distinct astrological combinations in this verse. || 1 ||

> In the Anustubh meter — If the Lord of the Year's Ascendant and the Lord of the eighth house are in the twelfth, eighth, or fourth houses combined with the Muntha, they cause death through the aggravation of the humors associated with those planets. || 2 ||

If the Lord of the Year's Ascendant or the Lord of the eighth house is joined with the *Muntha* in the twelfth, eighth, or fourth houses, there will be death-like suffering caused by the bodily humors <note>humors: 'dhatus' such as bile, phlegm, or wind</note> governed by that planet. If both the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the eighth house are joined with the *Muntha* in those specific houses, they bring about death. || 2 ||

> In the Anustubh meter — When the Lord of the Birth Ascendant is powerless and the Lord of the eighth house becomes the Lord of the Year's Ascendant, if he is aspected by the Sun, he brings death, leprosy, itching, or similar calamities. || 3 ||

# Tajika Neelakanthi

Page 122

If the Lord of the Ascendant at birth <note>Janmalagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign at the time of birth</note> is weak in both the birth chart and the annual chart, and if the Lord of the Eighth House <note>the house associated with death and longevity</note> is in the Ascendant of the annual chart while being aspected by the Sun, it brings death, leprosy, scabies (itching), or great calamity. || 3 ||

->Anushtubh Meter: If the Lord of the Year forms a Musaripha yoga with a malefic planet, and the Lord of the Birth Ascendant is afflicted by malefics, even if there is a Kamboola yoga with benefics, it results in disaster or death due to the influence of other authorities. || 4 ||<-

If there is a *Musaripha* <note>a Tajika aspect where a faster planet moves away from a slower one, indicating fading influence</note> between the Lord of the Year and a malefic planet, and the Lord of the Birth Ascendant has become malefic—for example, Mercury joined with a malefic or a waning Moon—then even if the Moon and other benefics form a *Kamboola* yoga <note>a configuration where the Moon transfers power between two planets</note>, calamity or death may occur. Similarly, this same yoga applies to the five authorities <note>Panchadhikari: the five planets with primary influence over the year</note> such as the Lord of the Birth Ascendant, the Lord of the Year Ascendant, and the Lord of the Muntha. Just as the *Musaripha* was described here for the Lord of the Year, it should be considered for the Lord of the Muntha and others; and while *Kamboola* was previously described only for the Moon, here it should be considered for all benefic planets in the same manner. || 4 ||

->Anushtubh Meter: When the Lord of the Muntha and the Lord of the Ascendant are combust and aspected by Saturn, total ruin, death, suffering, mental anxiety, and fear of disease occur. || 5 ||<-

If the Lord of the Muntha <note>Munthesh: the ruler of a sensitive point that progresses one sign per year</note> and the Lord of the Ascendant are combust <note>Astangata: too close to the Sun to be seen</note> and are also aspected by Saturn, there will be total ruin of wife, children, etc., or suffering equal to death, or leprosy, and fear arising from mental anxiety and physical pain. || 5 ||

->Anushtubh Meter: When malefic planets are high in strength and benefics are weak and placed in the houses of enemies or the eighth house, then there will be fear of mental anxiety and disease, as well as quarrels, loss, and calamity. || 6 ||<-

If malefic planets are strong—meaning they have more than 15 units of strength in the *Panchavargiya* <note>a five-fold system of calculating planetary strength</note>—and are placed in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, while benefic planets are weak—meaning they have less than 5 units of strength—and are placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, then mental agony and fear of disease will occur, along with quarrels, loss of wealth, and disaster. || 6 ||

->Anushtubh Meter: If Venus is in its sign of debilitation and Jupiter is in the division of an enemy, there is not even a fragment of happiness. If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th house or the Lord of the 8th is in the Ascendant, death should be predicted. || 7 ||<-

If Venus is in its debilitation sign (Virgo/6) and Jupiter is in the *Amshaka* <note>divisional chart portion</note> of an enemy, there will not be even a trace of happiness in that year. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th house, or the Lord of the 8th house is in the Ascendant, death occurs. These are two distinct yogas. || 7 ||

# Commentary with Translation

<term>Anushtup</term> <note>A poetic meter consisting of four quarters of eight syllables each.</note>—If the lords of the <term>Dharma-sthana</term> <note>The 9th house, representing fortune and righteousness</note> and the <term>Dhana-sthana</term> <note>The 2nd house, representing wealth</note> are weak, and malefic planets are situated in the ascendant:
->Even if Indra <note>The king of the gods</note> himself were the protector, wealth accumulated over a long time would be destroyed. || 8 ||<-

If the lord of the 9th house and the lord of the 2nd house are devoid of strength, and malefic planets are in the first house, then even if the king of gods comes to protect it, the wealth gathered over many days will be lost. || 8 ||

---

<term>Anushtup</term>—If the Moon is in its sign of debilitation and the benefic planets are combust:
->Separation from one's own kin occurs, along with bodily pain, death, or the immediate fear of mental anguish and disease. || 9 ||<-

If the Moon is in its debilitated sign <note>Scorpio, the 8th sign of the zodiac</note> and the auspicious planets are set <note>combust by the sun</note>, then there will be separation from one's people, as well as physical suffering, death, or mental distress and fear of illness occurring rapidly one after another. || 9 ||

---

<term>Anushtup</term>—When the <term>Varsha-lagna</term> <note>The ascendant of the annual chart</note> is in the eighth house from the <term>Janma-lagna</term> <note>The ascendant at birth</note> or the birth Moon-sign:
->There is suffering and fear of great disease; if aspected by or joined with malefic planets, death occurs. || 10 ||<-

If the annual ascendant is the eighth house from the birth ascendant or the birth Moon-sign, there will be distress and fear of great diseases like consumption <note>tuberculosis</note>. If such an eighth-house ascendant is aspected by or joined with malefic planets, death occurs. || 10 ||

---

<term>Anushtup</term>—A malefic planet situated in the eighth house at birth, if it becomes the ascendant of the year, causes disease and mental anguish:
->If the Moon and the lord of the annual ascendant are both devoid of strength, then death occurs. || 11 ||<-

The planet which is in the eighth house at the time of birth, if it is the ascendant in the annual chart, gives disease and mental agony; if both the Moon and the lord of the ascendant are "lost of strength" <note>original: "nashtabala"</note> and lack the five sources of power, then death occurs. || 11 ||

---

<term>Anushtup</term>—If the lords of the birth and annual ascendants are joined with malefics and situated in the eighth house:
->They cause disease and mental anguish; if they are combust and not aspected by benefics, they cause death. || 12 ||<-

If the lord of the birth ascendant and the lord of the annual ascendant are joined with malefic planets and situated in the eighth house <note>Likely a typo for "हो तो" (if it is so)</note>, they give disease and mental agony. If they are also combust and lack the gaze of auspicious planets, they cause death. || 12 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi

->Anushtubh Meter<-
If the Lord of the Ascendant at birth, the Lord of the Year, and the Muntha <note>a mathematical point in Tajika astrology that moves one sign per year</note> are all located in the twelfth, fourth, eighth, or sixth houses, and are in the same zodiac sign, then death is certain if they are also under the "Kshuta" aspect <note>original: "Kshutarvya drishti," a specific Tajika aspect</note> of malefic planets. || 13 ||

If the Lord of the Birth Ascendant, the Lord of the Year, and the Muntha are all together in the 12th, 4th, 8th, or 6th houses, there will be suffering equal to death; if these are also under the "Kshuta" aspect of malefic planets, then death will surely occur. || 13 ||

->Anushtubh Meter<-
The Moon joined with Saturn in the twelfth house, and Venus in the sixth, causes the destruction of wealth. Mental distress arises from an "Isarafa" <note>original: "Isarafa," a Tajika aspect where a faster planet separates from a slower one</note> with malefic planets, unless there is an aspect from a benefic. || 14 ||

If the Moon is in the twelfth house with Saturn and Venus is in the sixth, it causes the destruction of wealth. If there is an Isarafa yoga of any malefic planet with Saturn or Venus, the mind will remain distressed. If there is no aspect from a benefic planet upon them, then both wealth destruction and mental distress will result. || 14 ||

->Anushtubh Meter<-
If the Moon is within the orb of the Sun <note>combust</note> and situated in the sixth, twelfth, eighth, or fourth houses, disease arises from the three humors. If aspected by Jupiter, there is a favorable outcome. || 15 ||

If the Moon is set <note>combust/hidden by the Sun's light</note> and is in the 6th, 12th, 8th, or 4th house, then diseases such as delirium will occur due to the disorder of the three humors <note>original: "Tridosha" - Vata (air), Pitta (bile), and Kapha (phlegm)</note>. If Jupiter aspects this combination, the person will eventually become free from disease. || 15 ||

->Anushtubh Meter<-
If the Lord of the "Hadda" <note>original: "Hadda," a specific degree-based division or 'term' in Tajika astrology</note> of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Year's Ascendant are in the seventh, eighth, or twelfth houses joined with malefics, they grant death during their period. With a benefic aspect, one should predict a good outcome. || 16 ||

Whichever planet owns the Hadda of the Ascendant at that time, along with the Lord of the Ascendant, if they are in the 7th, 8th, or 12th houses joined with malefics, they bring death during their planetary period <note>Dasha</note>. If there is also an aspect from a benefic planet on them, one should say that there will be happiness after experiencing the suffering. || 16 ||

->Anushtubh Meter<-
From the Year Ascendant, if a direct planet is in the twelfth and a retrograde planet is in the second, disease occurs. Similarly, imprisonment is predicted via the Lords of the Birth and Year Ascendants. || 17 ||

If there is a direct-moving planet in the 12th house from the Year Ascendant and a retrograde planet in the 2nd house, disease occurs; this is called "Kartari Yoga" <note>the 'Scissor' combination where a house is hemmed in</note>. Similarly, if the Lord of the Birth Ascendant or the Lord of the Year Ascendant is hemmed in by a Kartari Yoga from the Lord of the Year, imprisonment should be predicted. A Kartari Yoga on the 7th house also gives imprisonment through disease or wicked disturbances. || 17 ||

**Anushtubh Meter—If the Lord of the Three Signs <note>original: "Trirashipati"; a specific planetary ruler in Tajika astrology</note> is in its sign of debilitation and aspected by malefic planets, the intended work is destroyed. If the Lord of the Muntha <note>original: "Munthesha"; the ruler of the progressed annual point</note> and the Lord of the Year <note>original: "Varshesha"</note> are in the sixth house, or by implication the eighth, and are combust <note>original: "astangata"; rendered invisible by the sun's proximity</note>, then calamity occurs through disease. || 18 ||**

If the Lord of the Three Signs is in a debilitated sign and is viewed by malefic planets, the desired task is ruined (1). And if the Lord of the Muntha and the Lord of the Year are in the sixth or, by extension, the eighth house and are combust, then distress from diseases arises (2). These are the two planetary combinations (Yogas) described. || 18 ||

**Shardulavikridita Meter—If the Moon is situated in the twelfth, sixth, eighth, first, or seventh house and is aspected by malefic planets but not by benefics, it causes misfortune or even death. Specifically, if such a Moon is aspected by Mars, there is fear of fire or weapons. If aspected by Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu, there is fear of enemies, suffering from wind-based diseases <note>original: "vataroga"; ailments like rheumatism or neurological issues in Ayurvedic thought</note>, and poverty if aspected by the Sun. If there is also an aspect from a benefic planet, especially Jupiter, then after the aforementioned suffering, one should predict well-being. || 19 ||**

If the Moon is in the 12th, 6th, 8th, 1st, or 7th house and malefic planets look upon it while benefic planets do not, it grants misfortune or death itself. The specific results based on planetary aspects are: if Mars looks upon the aforementioned Moon, it gives fear of fire or weapons; if Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu look upon it, it gives fear of enemies, pain from wind-diseases, and if the Sun looks upon it, it gives poverty. If a benefic planet, particularly Jupiter, also casts its gaze, then after the removal of said pains, it grants welfare. || 19 ||

**Vasantatilaka Meter—If the Muntha is joined with or aspected by a malefic and is also seen by Saturn while placed in the inauspicious 6th, 12th, 8th, or 4th houses, it grants mental anguish and physical disease. If this same Muntha was in the 12th, 4th, 6th, 8th, or 7th house at the time of birth (relative to the birth ascendant) and is in the 8th house in the yearly chart, joined with or seen by a malefic, it grants death. Thus should the wise deliberate. || 20 ||**

> Thus ends the Chapter on Misfortune in the Phalatantra of the Neelkanthi. || 3 ||

If the Muntha is joined with a malefic planet and Saturn sees it, and it is in the inauspicious houses (6, 12, 8, or 4), it causes mental agony and disease in the body (1). If this same Muntha was in the 12th, 4th, 6th, 8th, or 7th house at the time of birth—that is, from the birth ascendant—and in the year chart it is in the eighth house and joined with or seen by a malefic planet, it causes death. In this manner, scholars should analyze the chart. || 20 ||

->Thus in the commentary by Mahidhara on the Neelkanthi,<-
->The Third Chapter on the Consideration of Misfortune in the Phalatantra ends.<-

# Chapter on the Cancellation of Malefic Combinations

<note>The text transitions here to the "Arishta-Bhanga-Adhyaya," a crucial section in Vedic astrology that explains how strong planetary positions can neutralize bad omens or predicted misfortunes.</note>

Anushtubh Meter — If the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength, or is associated with or aspected by benefic planets, and is situated in a Quadrant or a Trine, it destroys the malefic influence and bestows happiness and wealth. || 1 ||

To remedy the previously mentioned malefic combinations <term>Arishta: planetary configurations signifying misfortune or death</term>, the "Arishta-Bhanga" (cancellation of misfortune) combinations are stated: If the Lord of the Yearly Ascendant <term>Varsha-Lagna: the rising sign at the moment of the solar return</term> is strong—specifically having more than 15 points in the Five-Fold Strength <term>Pancha-Vargiya: a specific Tajika system for calculating planetary potency</term>—and is joined with or aspected by benefic planets, and is placed in the Quadrants (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses) or Trines (5th or 9th houses), then it destroys the evil effects of the previously mentioned bad yogas and grants happiness and wealth. || 1 ||

Anushtubh Meter — If Jupiter is in a Quadrant or a Trine, aspected by benefics and not aspected by malefics, it destroys the misfortunes arising from the Ascendant or the Moon and grants wealth and happiness. || 2 ||

If Jupiter is in a Quadrant or a Trine and is aspected by benefic planets without any aspect from malefic planets, one should predict the destruction of misfortunes arising from the Ascendant, the Moon, or the Muntha <term>Muntha: a sensitive point in the yearly chart that progresses one sign per year</term>, and the attainment of happiness. || 2 ||

Anushtubh Meter — If the fourth house is joined with its own Lord and aspected by benefics, it gives happiness, fame, and wealth. If Jupiter is in the Ascendant or the third house, and the Birth Ascendant Lord is in the fourth, it gives wealth and happiness. || 3 ||

If the fourth house <note>The house of comforts and the home</note> is joined by its own Lord and is aspected by or joined with benefic planets, it grants fame and wealth. Furthermore, if Jupiter is in the Ascendant or the third house, and the Lord of the Birth Ascendant <note>The ruler of the rising sign from the original time of birth, rather than the yearly chart</note> is in the fourth house, it grants wealth with ease. || 3 ||

Upajati Meter — If the Lord of the seventh house is in the Ascendant with Jupiter, not aspected by malefics but aspected by benefics and friends, it destroys misfortune and grants fame and happiness; in its own period, it grants the favor of the King. || 4 ||

If the Lord of the seventh house is in the Ascendant along with Jupiter, and cruel planets <note>Malefics like Mars or Saturn</note> do not aspect them, but they are aspected by (or joined with) benefic and friendly planets, then it destroys misfortune and gives wealth, fame, and happiness. One should also predict that during the planetary period <term>Dasha: a time-block ruled by a specific planet</term> of that planet, the person will receive royal favor <term>Rajaprasada: literally "the grace of the King," implying success in high-level career or government</term>. || 4 ||

Upajati Meter — When the Lords of the ninth and second houses are endowed with strength and situated in the Ascendant, not aspected by malefics, there is the gain of a kingdom full of elephants, horses, clothes, and gems, the destruction of misfortune, and incomparable fame. || 5 ||

If the Lord of the ninth house <note>The house of fortune and destiny</note> and the Lord of the second house <note>The house of wealth</note> are strong and placed in the Ascendant, and malefic planets do not aspect them, the person gains a kingdom filled with elephants, horses, clothing, and jewels; misfortune is destroyed, and the person achieves incomparable fame. || 5 ||

<summary>This page outlines specific planetary configurations that cancel out "Arishta" (misfortunes) in a yearly horoscope, emphasizing the protective roles of Jupiter and the Ascendant Lord. It promises that strong placements in the Quadrants and Trines can transform potential disaster into wealth, royal favor, and fame.</summary>

**Upajati Meter—If malefic planets are situated in the third, sixth, or eleventh houses, and benefic planets are located in the center <note>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> or trine <note>Trikona: the 5th or 9th houses</note> positions, then the person attains gems, clothing, gold, fame, and happiness. Even the previously mentioned misfortunes are destroyed, and the body gains strength and nourishment. || 6 ||**

If malefic planets <note>original: "Asaumya" or "Papa-graha"</note> are in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, and benefic planets are in the centers or trines, then one receives jewels, garments, gold, fame, and happiness; the aforementioned ill-fortune is negated, and the body becomes healthy and robust. || 6 ||

A strong Mars in the house of wealth grants fame, riches, glory, and sudden happiness. || 8 ||**

If Saturn, Venus, or Jupiter are in their signs of exaltation and form an *Itthashala* with a benefic planet, wealth is obtained from a distinguished foreigner <note>The term "Yavana" historically referred to Greeks/Ionians, but in this context, it implies foreign rulers or those outside the traditional Vedic social structure</note>. Specifically, through a Saturn yoga, wealth comes from such foreigners; through a Venus yoga, from a woman; and through a Jupiter yoga, from a priest <note>Brahmin</note>. If all three are exalted and in auspicious aspects, great wealth is obtained from a foreign king; otherwise, the gains are moderate. If a powerful Mars is in the second house <note>the house of wealth</note>, one attains fame, money, splendor, and sudden joy. || 8 ||

If the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus create a mutual *Itthashala* aspect, the person attains sovereign power, fame, happiness, and wealth. Furthermore, if the Sun or Mars are in the *Upachaya* positions (the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses) relative to the *Muntha*, they bestow well-being and great prosperity. || 9 ||

If Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are situated in their own *Hadda* divisions, and malefic planets are placed in the 3rd or 11th houses, the individual attains gold, comfort, and renown through their own personal effort and bravery. || 10 ||

<note>Anushtup meter</note>—If Mercury and Venus form a *Musaripha* <note>original: "मूसरिफौ" - a Tajika aspect where a faster planet moves past a slower one, indicating the fading of an effect</note> yoga, and Jupiter is situated in the third house <note>the house of courage and siblings</note>, then the native attains kingdom, fame, gold, pearls, and coral. || 11 ||

<note>Anushtup meter</note>—If Mars is the Lord of the Year <note>the planet ruling the specific year in the Tajika system</note> and is placed in a friend's sign, and forms a *Kambuli* yoga <note>a configuration involving the Moon</note> with planets in their own signs or other dignities, it grants the gain of elephants, horses, gold, garments, and land, along with great happiness. || 12 ||
If Mars becomes the Lord of the Year and resides in a friendly sign, and forms a *Muthashila* <note>an applying aspect</note> with a planet in its own sign and a *Kambuli* yoga with the Moon, then it bestows the gain of elephants, horses, gold, clothes, and land, and provides much happiness. || 12 ||

<note>Anushtup meter</note>—In this manner, having deliberated upon the strength and weakness of the yoga-forming planets in both the birth chart and the annual chart, one should predict *Rajayoga* <note>combinations for royal success or high status</note> and its components. || 13 ||
In this way, by considering the strength and weakness of the planets creating yogas in the birth and year charts, one should declare the presence of *Rajayoga* or the cancellation of *Rajayoga*. For instance, if the yoga-forming planet is in its sign of exaltation or is fully strong, there is the attainment of a kingdom; if it is weak, there is the loss of kingdom and status. || 13 ||

<note>Upajati meter</note>—If the Lord of the *Muntha* <note>a sensitive mathematical point in the yearly chart</note> and other planets are associated with or aspected by malefics, or are combust <note>too close to the sun</note> or in their signs of debilitation, and the benefics are devoid of strength, then even an existing *Rajayoga* is cancelled, and there is a loss of wealth and happiness. || 14 ||
In the yearly chart, if planets like the Lord of the *Muntha* are joined with or seen by malefic planets, or are set (combust) or in debilitation, and the auspicious planets are powerless, then even if a *Rajayoga* is present, it will be broken, and one should predict the destruction of wealth and happiness. || 14 ||

<note>Shardulavikridita meter</note>—The jewel of the lineage of Sri Garga was the mathematician Chintamani; his son Ananta, to destroy the opinions of the wicked, composed the *Janu-Paddhati*. His son, the wise Nilakantha, by the command of the learned Shiva, has spoken here of the Lord of the Year, the results of the *Muntha*, misfortunes, and auspicious yogas. || 15 ||
The meaning of this verse is as previously stated; the specific detail is that in this chapter, the author has described the Lord of the Year, the fruits of the *Muntha*, misfortunes (*Arishta*), yogas, the cancellation of misfortunes, and *Rajayoga*. || 15 ||

# Now, the Analysis of the First House among the Analysis of the Houses.

> <note>Metre: Anushtubh</note>—Whichever house is aspected by or associated with its own lord or with benefic planets, that house prospers. If it is aspected by or associated with malefic planets, it suffers destruction. If the influences are mixed, one should predict mixed results. ॥ 1 ॥

Whichever house <note>Bhava</note> is joined with or aspected by its own lord or a benefic planet <note>favorable planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, that house experiences growth. Conversely, whichever house is joined with or aspected by a malefic planet <note>unfavorable planets like Mars or Saturn</note> suffers loss. If a house is influenced by both benefics and malefics—for instance, joined by one and aspected by the other—then the results should be described as mixed, being partly auspicious and partly inauspicious. This principle applies to the analysis of all houses. ॥ 1 ॥

---

> <note>Metre: Indravajra</note>—When the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength, there is happiness, freedom from disease, the arrival of wealth, and pleasures. If it possesses medium strength, there is little happiness and financial gain. If it possesses little strength, there is an excess of distress and misfortune. ॥ 2 ॥

If the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnashesh</term><note>The planet ruling the first house of the zodiac at the time of birth or the start of the year</note> is powerful according to the previously mentioned methods, the person enjoys happiness, good health, the acquisition of wealth, and joys such as laughter and luxury. If the planet has moderate strength, then happiness and financial gains are limited. If the planet has little or no strength, there is great suffering and calamity. ॥ 2 ॥

---

> <note>Metre: Shardulavikridita</note>—If the Sun, acting as the Lord of the Birth Year, the Ascendant, or the Muntha, is devoid of strength, it causes loss of vision and skin diseases, and a lack of enthusiasm. It leads to base actions and humiliation even from parents. If the Moon is similarly weak, it causes loss of work, poverty, defeat, domestic strife, and fear of disease. ॥ 3 ॥

The specific results of the ruling planets being weak are now described. If the Lord of the Birth Ascendant, the Lord of the Year Ascendant, the <term>Munthesh</term><note>The lord of a specific sensitive point in a yearly progressed chart</note>, or the Lord of the Year is weak—meaning it scores less than 5 in the <term>Panchavargi</term><note>A five-fold system used in Tajika astrology to calculate planetary strength</note>—the following results occur: If it is the Sun, there is loss of sight due to eye disease, skin diseases like leprosy or ringworm, and a loss of motivation. One may have to perform lowly tasks and face "estrangement" or humiliation from parents, along with a loss of authority. If it is the Moon, there is deterioration of vision, failure in undertakings, poverty, insult, quarrels within the home, mental anguish, and fear of illness. ॥ 3 ॥

---

> <note>Metre: Anushtubh</note>—If Mars is weak, there is cowardice; if Mercury, there is delusion and defeat. If Jupiter, there is a decline in righteousness and a life of hardship. ॥ 4 ॥

If Mars is the ruling planet and is weak in the manner described above, there is physical weakness...

**In the Anustubh meter—If Venus is present, there is a destruction of pleasures and comforts, and strife with women. If Saturn is present, there is sorrow caused by servants or diseases arising from an imbalance of the wind humor.** || 5 ||

Similarly, if Venus is present, there will be the destruction of laughter, luxury, and happiness, and quarrels with women will occur. If Saturn is present, there will be suffering caused by servants and diseases will arise from the aggravation of the wind <note>original: "vatakopa"; referring to the Vata dosha in Ayurvedic medicine</note>. || 5 ||

**In the Anustubh meter—If the Ascendant is joined with malefic planets and is neither aspected by nor joined with benefics, men experience disputes, deception, and the eating of wicked food.** || 6 ||

If the Ascendant <note>the rising sign or 'Lagna'</note> is occupied by malefic planets and is not aspected by or associated with auspicious planets, then men will face quarrels, someone may cheat them, and they will receive bad food to eat. These are the results. || 6 ||

**In the Shardulavikridita meter—If the Lord of the Birth Ascendant, the Lord of the Year Ascendant, the Lord of the Eighth House, the Lord of the Year, and the <term>Muntha-Lord</term><note>The ruler of the Muntha, a mathematical point that moves one sign per year in Tajika astrology</note> are strong, then the year is said to be beautiful, bringing incomparable happiness, fame, and the arrival of wealth. If these are not placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, but are weak, then this year is said to be inauspicious and productive of grief and fear, unless there is an aspect from a benefic.** || 7 ||

If the <term>Lord of the Birth Ascendant</term>, the <term>Lord of the Year Ascendant</term>, the <term>Lord of the Eighth House</term>, the <term>Lord of the Year</term>, and the <term>Muntha-Lord</term> are powerful and are not located in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses <note>the 'Dusthanas' or difficult houses</note>, then astrologers declare only auspicious results for the entire year; there will be immeasurable happiness, fame, and the arrival of wealth. If the aforementioned planets are devoid of strength and lack the aspect of auspicious planets, then grief and fear occur, and they give entirely inauspicious results. If they are weak, under malefic influence, and situated in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, the said planets may even cause death. || 7 ||

**In the Anustubh meter—If the planet that bestows wealth in the birth chart and the Lord of the Wealth House are destroyed in the year, they cause loss of wealth and accusations regarding deposits.** || 8 ||

If the planet that grants wealth in the birth chart and the <term>Lord of the Wealth House</term><note>The ruler of the 2nd house of the birth chart</note> from the birth itself are weak in the annual chart, then there will be loss of wealth and "Apavada"—which means a scandal or stigma (such as being accused: "I had entrusted him with some money and he stole it"). If both of these are strong, they grant wealth. || 8 ||
