### Now, the Inquiry into the House of Wealth.

Verse: When the lord of wealth from the birth chart is situated in the house of wealth during the year, and Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva"</note> forms an *Itthashala* <term>Itthashala: a favorable aspect or planetary link in Tajika astrology</term> with the Lord of the Ascendant, then wealth is acquired throughout the entire year. If the aforementioned Jupiter forms an *Isarafa* <term>Isarafa: a separating or unfavorable aspect</term> with malefic planets, there is a loss of wealth and grain. || 1 ||

If the Jupiter who rules the house of wealth in the birth chart is placed in the second house <note>the house of finances</note> during the yearly revolution and forms an *Itthashala* yoga with the Lord of the Ascendant, then wealth is obtained throughout the year. If that Jupiter forms an *Isarafa* yoga with a malefic planet, it causes the destruction of wealth and food supplies. || 1 ||

Verse: When Jupiter looks upon the house of wealth in the birth chart and becomes the Lord of the Year <note>the dominant planet for that specific year</note> with full strength, then great wealth is acquired without any effort. || 2 ||

If Jupiter aspects <note>casts its astrological gaze upon</note> the house of wealth in the birth chart and becomes the "Lord of the Year" in the yearly chart while remaining strong, then one receives abundant wealth without hard labor. || 2 ||

Verse: In this same way, whatever house Jupiter rules in the birth chart, if he is situated in that same house during the year and forms an *Itthashala* with the Lord of the Ascendant, there will be happiness related to that house. || 3 ||

Similarly, whatever house Jupiter owns in the birth chart, if he is placed in that same house during the year—and by implication becomes the Lord of the Year—and forms an *Itthashala* with the Lord of the Ascendant, then the person experiences the joys of that house. For example, if Jupiter is the lord of the third house in the birth chart and in the yearly chart he is in the third house or becomes the Lord of the Year and links with the Ascendant Lord, there will be happiness regarding siblings. One should analyze all houses in this manner. || 3 ||

Verse: Furthermore, whatever house Jupiter aspects in the birth chart, if he becomes the Lord of the Year, then the experts in *Tajika* <note>a system of Indian astrology with Persian-Arabic influences</note> say he grants happiness related to that house. || 4 ||

As stated previously, if Jupiter is the Lord of the Year and he aspects a particular house in the birth chart, he provides happiness derived from that house. This is the opinion of those who know the *Tajika* scriptures. || 4 ||

**Anustubh Meter—If Mercury is the lord of the sixth house at birth and is in the sixth house during the year, it yields little profit. If Jupiter is afflicted by malefic planets in the eighth or second house, a fine from the king will surely fall upon the person. || 5 ||**

**Anustubh Meter—Similarly, if Venus is the lord of the year, much wealth and grain are produced. The conjunction of the lord of wealth and the lord of the ascendant destroys the happiness of wealth. || 7 ||**

Just as with Jupiter, if Venus is in the second house associated with or aspected by benefics, and if Venus is also the <term>Varshesha</term> <note>the ruler of the year</note>, then great wealth and an abundance of grain are acquired. If the lord of the second house and the <term>Lagnesha</term> <note>the lord of the ascendant or first house</note> are in the same position, they destroy the happiness derived from wealth. However, there is a specific consideration here: if they form an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>a favorable aspect or "yoga" in Tajika astrology indicating the fulfillment of a task</note>, then wealth and happiness occur. If they form an <term>Ishrafa</term> <note>a separating aspect indicating the failure or loss of an objective</note>, then the happiness of wealth is destroyed. If there is neither an Itthashala nor an Ishrafa, but merely a conjunction, wealth and happiness still occur; this interpretation is widely accepted. || 7 ||

**Anustubh Meter—Likewise, if Mercury is strong, wealth comes through writing, knowledge, and effort. Benefics that were in the birth ascendant give wealth when in the annual second house. || 8 ||**

Similarly, if a strong Mercury is the ruler of the year and is in the second house with benefic aspects, wealth is gained through writing, intellectual pursuits, the sciences, and industrious efforts. Furthermore, those benefic planets that were in the ascendant at the time of birth will grant wealth if they are positioned in the second house during the annual progression. || 8 ||

**Anustubh Meter—If Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are in the house of wealth or the Maal Saham, or if they aspect them, one gains much wealth and the sovereignty of their family. || 9 ||**

In the Persian language, "Maal" refers to wealth. If Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are located in the <term>Maal-sthana</term> <note>the second house of wealth</note> or the <term>Maal-Saham</term> <note>the Arabic Part of Fortune or specifically the Lot of Wealth</note>, or if these three planets aspect those points, the person will obtain great riches and may attain the leadership or "kingdom" of their own family line. || 9 ||

# Now, the Consideration of the House of Siblings.

**Translation: When the Lord of the Year, or the Sun and Venus, are strong and free from malefic influence,**
**there is mutual happiness among siblings; if the opposite, one should predict the opposite. || 1 ||**

If the Lord of the Year <term>Abdesha: the planetary ruler of the specific year in a Tajika chart</term>, the Sun, or Venus is powerful and not joined by malefic planets, there will be mutual happiness among brothers. If they are joined by malefic planets, the opposite result should be predicted—meaning mutual quarrels and disturbances will occur among the brothers. || 1 ||

->**Vasantatilaka Meter**<-
If the Lord of the Third House <note>original: "Sahajapa"</note> or the Lord of the Year <note>original: "Abdapati"</note> is "burnt" <note>term: Dagdha; refers to a planet being combust by the sun or placed in an inauspicious house</note>, or if Jupiter is devoid of strength in the third house, there will be strife with one's siblings. If there is an Isarafa Yoga <note>term: Isarafa; an astrological configuration where two planets are moving away from an aspect, indicating separation or loss</note> with the Lord of the Third House, one should expect illness or sluggishness among one's own people and brothers. || 2 ||

If the Lord of the Third House becomes the Lord of the Year and is "burnt" (afflicted by being in a bad house or combust), there will be quarrels with brothers; the same result occurs if Venus or the Sun are "burnt." If Jupiter is in the third house without strength, the same result follows, and they will experience distress (whereas a strong Jupiter in the third house grants happiness from brothers). Furthermore, if there is an Isarafa Yoga between the Lord of the Year and the Lord of the Third House, one should recognize both quarrels with brothers and kin, as well as physical suffering in their bodies. || 2 ||

->**Upajati Meter**<-
If Jupiter is in the third house and forms an Itthashala <note>term: Itthashala; a favorable aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of a task</note> with the Lord of the Third House, one obtains happiness from siblings. If Mars and the Moon are in the third house, there will be strife, provided they are not joined or aspected by Jupiter. || 3 ||

Even if Jupiter is weak in the third house, if it forms a favorable Itthashala with the Lord of the Third House, one should predict happiness from brothers. It is already established that if Jupiter is strong in the third house, it grants brotherly happiness even without an Itthashala. If the Moon is with Mars in the third house, there will be quarrels with brothers, but this result only holds if Jupiter does not aspect them; if Jupiter aspects them, the result becomes auspicious. || 3 ||

->**Anushtubh Meter**<-
When the Lord of the Third House is in the third house with authority, or if it forms a Muthashila <note>term: Muthashila; another term for the favorable Itthashala aspect</note> with the Lord of the Ascendant, there is mutual happiness between siblings. || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Third House is placed in the third house and possesses planetary authority, and if the Lord of the Year and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagnapa"</note> are in a Muthashila configuration, there will be mutual happiness among the brothers. || 4 ||

->**Anushtubh Meter**<-
If there is an Isarafa Yoga with malefic planets, there is a quarrel; if Saturn is in the signs of Mars, there is disease. If Mars is in the signs of Mercury in the third house, one should clearly predict illness for the younger brother. || 5 ||

If there is an Isarafa Yoga between the Lord of the Third House and malefic planets, there will be quarrels with brothers. If Saturn is in the third house in the signs of Mars (Aries or Scorpio), then brothers will suffer from disease. Likewise, if Mars is in the third house in the signs of Mercury (Gemini or Virgo), one should predict distress for the brothers. || 5 ||

->There will be mutual happiness and great joy among siblings. (6)<-

If Mars is in the third house in a sign of Saturn (Capricorn or Aquarius), or if Mercury is in the third house in a sign of Mars (Aries or Scorpio), and is joined with or aspected by <term>benefic planets</term>(<note>planets like Jupiter, Venus, or a strong Moon that bring positive influence</note>), then there is great mutual happiness among brothers. (6)

<note>Written in Vasantatilaka meter</note>—If Mercury and Venus, as lords of the birth or year, are strong in the third house, they bring happiness to the circle of siblings and kin; Jupiter does the same. If Venus is the <term>officer of the year</term>(<note>the ruling planet for that specific year in the Tajika system</note>), is powerful, and is placed in the sign of the Moon (Cancer), it leads to the increase of siblings and relatives in the birth and year charts. (7)

If the Lord of the Year or the Lord of the Ascendant, Mercury or Venus, is strong and placed in the third house, they provide happiness to uterine brothers and other relatives; Jupiter also gives the same result. Furthermore, if the <term>Adhikari</term> (ruling officer) Venus is powerful in the birth or year chart and is placed in the fourth sign (Cancer, the sign of the Moon), it causes an increase in the number of brothers and kinsmen. (7)

<note>Written in Vasantatilaka meter</note>—If the third house is occupied by malefic planets and is devoid of the aspect of the Lord of the Third House or the Lord of the <term>Sahaja Saham</term>(<note>a specific Arabic Part or sensitive point relating to siblings</note>), there is suffering for the siblings. The same should be said for the Sahaja Saham itself; if its lords are <term>combust</term>(<note>original: "dagdha" - meaning burnt by the sun's proximity or placed in evil houses</note>), they should be known as destroyers of siblings. (8)

If the third house is joined by malefic planets and the Lord of the Third House or the Lord of the Sahaja Saham does not cast an aspect upon it, the brother will experience sorrow. The same should be predicted regarding the Sahaja Saham; if the Lord of the Third House and the Lord of the Sahaja Saham are <term>combust</term>(<note>afflicted by being too close to the sun or placed in unfavorable positions</note>), they should be understood as causing the loss of siblings. If they are joined or aspected by benefics, consider it auspicious for the siblings. (8)

<note>Written in Upajati meter</note>—If the Lord of the Year or the Lord of the Ascendant is in the seventh house from the Lord of the Third House, there will be disputes with siblings. If the Lord of the Third House is in the third house in both the birth and year charts and is aspected by benefics, it brings joy to the siblings. (9)

### Thus ends the consideration of the Third House.

If the Lord of the Year or the Lord of the Year's Ascendant is in the seventh position from the Lord of the Third House, there will be quarrels with brothers. If the Lord of the Third House is placed in the third house in both the birth and year charts and is aspected by benefic planets, it brings mutual joy to the brothers. (9)

# Now, the Consideration of the House of Happiness.

<note>The "House of Happiness" or Sukha Bhava refers to the fourth house in a natal or annual horoscope.</note>

*Upajati Meter*—If the Sun and Moon are in the fourth house, joined with or aspected by malefic planets, there is suffering for the father and mother respectively. If Saturn, in the solar return year, occupies the same sign that the Sun occupied at birth, the individual faces dishonor and experiences strife and enmity with the father. || 1 ||

If the Sun is in the fourth house joined with or aspected by malefic planets <note>original: "papayukta" or "papadrishta"</note>, it causes suffering to the father; similarly, the Moon in such a state causes suffering to the mother. If the Sun and Moon are together in the fourth house, or if both are aspected by malefics, they bring distress to the father. Furthermore, if Saturn in the annual chart is in the same zodiac sign where the Sun was placed at birth, it results in humiliation and conflict with the father. || 1 ||

*Upajati Meter*—Similarly, if Saturn is in the sign of the natal Moon, it brings distress to the mother. If the Lord of the Fourth is in the fourth house, there is affection and happiness from the parents. If the powerful Lord of the Fourth forms an *Itthashala* yoga with the Lord of the Ascendant, the sages declare happiness regarding the parents. || 2 ||

If Saturn in the annual chart is in the same sign as the natal Moon, there will be enmity and quarrels with the mother. If the Lord of the Fourth House is situated within the fourth house itself, it indicates love for the parents and receiving happiness from them. By extension, if the *Saham* <note>An Arabic-derived sensitive point or "lot" used in Tajika astrology</note> for the father or mother is in the fourth house, it yields the same result. If the Lord of the Fourth aspects the fourth house, it grants parental happiness. If the powerful Lord of the Fourth forms an *Itthashala* <note>term: Itthashala (a favorable aspect or "application" between two planets where the faster planet approaches the slower one)</note> with the Lord of the Ascendant, parental bliss is assured. By extension, a simple conjunction between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Fourth also grants these results. || 2 ||

*Vasantatilaka Meter*—If the Lord of the Fourth is weak in both the birth and annual charts, it causes harm to the parents; the same should be considered for the Lords of the parental *Sahams*. If a "burnt" <note>combust or severely afflicted</note> malefic planet is in the fourth house from the *Muntha*, there is destruction for them; the same occurs if the *Sahams* themselves are "burnt." || 3 ||

If the Lord of the Fourth House from the birth chart is powerless in the annual transit, it produces inauspicious results for the parents. The same logic applies to the Father-Saham and Mother-Saham. If these *Sahams* contain "burnt" <note>original: "dagdha," referring to planets weakened by proximity to the Sun</note> malefic planets and fall in the fourth house from the *Muntha* <note>term: Muntha (a progressed point in the annual chart that moves one sign per year)</note>, it signifies the loss of the parents. Likewise, if the Lords of the parental *Sahams* are weak, attacked by malefics, or combust, they yield the same ill effects. Conversely, if the Lord of the Fourth or the Lords of the said *Sahams* are strong, they bring auspicious results to the parents. || 3 ||

If it lacks a *Kamboola* yoga <note>A yoga formed when the Moon connects two planets</note>, then wind-related diseases like rheumatism and eye ailments may also occur. ॥ 1 ॥

# Tajik Nilakanthi

If the sign of the year <note>The Ascendant of the solar return chart</note> is occupied by Mars, or if Mars casts its aspect upon it, then the aforementioned diseases will be only slight.

### In the Vasantatilaka meter:
When the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Year forms an *Itthashala* <term>Itthashala: A favorable aspect or "application" between two planets in Tajik astrology</term> with the Lord of the Sixth House, disease arises according to the specific bodily humor <note>The three doshas: Vata, Pitta, and Kapha</note> associated with that planet as defined in the chapter on planetary substances. If the Sun in the year-chart occupies the same sign that Venus occupied at birth, disease arises from humoral imbalance. 

<margin>Note: The text questions the logic of the Sun occupying Venus's sign, as the Sun returns to its natal position annually; it suggests this refers to the specific house or "Bhava" instead.</margin>

Regarding the verse's meaning: it appears to say the Sun should be in the natal sign of Venus. However, since the Sun returns to the same sign every year at the time of the solar return, how can it be in Venus's sign unless they were together at birth? If they were together, this yoga would occur every year, which is improbable. Therefore, it is more authoritative to interpret this as the Sun being in the *house* (Bhava) occupied by Venus. If the Sun and Venus were in the same sign at birth, and in the year-chart Venus falls in the sixth house, then <term>Smara-roga</term> <note>literally "memory disease," but here interpreted as disorders of desire or reproductive ailments</note> occurs. If the *Roga-Sahama* <term>Sahama: An Arabic Part or sensitive point; here, the Point of Disease</term> is associated with a malefic planet, this should be predicted with certainty.

### From the Bhuvanapradipa:
If a malefic-associated Jupiter is in the eighth house and Mars is in the Ascendant, the native suffers from <term>Tandra</term> <note>A state of exhaustion, lethargy, or fainting</note>. If the Moon is also with Jupiter in the eighth while Mars is in the Ascendant, there may be the loss or severe affliction of a limb due to disease. If malefic planets are in the "angles" (quadrants) of the birth chart and also in the Ascendant of the year-chart, they produce sickness. For instance, if Venus is aspected by malefic planets situated in human signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Aquarius, and the first half of Sagittarius</note>, then <term>Kapha-roga</term> <note>Phlegm-based illnesses or respiratory issues</note> occurs during that year.

### From the Bhuvanapradipa:
If at the time of the solar return, the Ascendant of the year or the birth chart falls in the *Hadda* <term>Hadda: A subdivision of a sign similar to "Terms" in Western astrology</term> of the Sun or Mars, there will be suffering from fever. However, if the period (Dasha) of a benefic planet is active, happiness and recovery will be attained.

# Now, the Analysis of the Seventh House

->**Upajati Meter**<-
If Venus, as the Lord of the Year <note>The planet designated as the ruler of the current year in a Tajika solar return chart</note>, is strong and situated in the seventh house, one should expect happiness from the wife's side. If it is aspected by Jupiter, there is extreme happiness; if it is aspected by Mars, acting as an official <note>A planet with specific functional authority in the chart</note>, it creates mutual affection between the couple. || 1 ||

If the Year Lord Venus is strong and placed in the seventh house, it brings happiness from the wife's side. If the aspect of Jupiter also falls upon it, it brings immense marital bliss. If such a Venus is aspected by Mars (as an official), it increases the mutual love between husband and wife. <insert>If Venus in the seventh is weak, destroyed, or combust, it causes distress from the wife.</insert> || 1 ||

->**Anushtubh Meter**<-
If aspected by Mercury, there is adultery with a younger woman; if by Saturn, with an older woman. By the aspect of Jupiter, there is a new wife and then swift offspring. || 2 ||

If that same Year Lord Venus is aspected by Mercury (as an official), there is adultery with a young woman of another or a courtesan. If the said Venus is aspected by Saturn (as a non-official), there is adultery with an elderly woman of another. If the said Venus is aspected by Jupiter (whether official or non-official), there is union with a newly wedded wife and rapid birth of children. In this verse, the phrase "by the aspect of Jupiter" <note>original: "गुरुदृष्ट्या" (gurudṛṣṭyā)</note> is a clerical error because it was already mentioned in the previous verse; here the reading should be "by conjunction with Jupiter." This is also stated in the <term>Tajika Sudhanidhi</term> <note>A classical Sanskrit treatise on Tajika astrology</note>: "Even when in conjunction with Jupiter, there is a new beloved and children are born quickly there." || 2 ||

->**Anushtubh Meter**<-
When the Lord of the Birth Ascendant is in the seventh house and endowed with strength, there is marital happiness. When the sign occupied by Venus at birth is in the seventh house of the year and Venus is the Year Lord, it leads to the gain of a wife. || 3 ||

If the Lord of the Birth Ascendant is strong in the seventh house during the year, there is marital happiness. If the sign where Venus was located at birth becomes the seventh house in the annual chart, and Venus itself is the Year Lord, one obtains a wife. || 3 ||

->**Anushtubh Meter**<-
When the Lord of the Birth Ascendant is in the seventh house from the Year Ascendant, and is risen and strong, marital happiness is produced. || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Birth Ascendant is in the seventh house of the year and is visible <note>not combust by the sun</note> and strong, marital bliss occurs. || 4 ||

**Anustubh Meter—If the Lord of the Year is in the same sign occupied by Venus at birth, or if that sign is in the seventh house, then a man’s marriage occurs. || 5 ||**

If the Lord of the Year <note>The planet ruling the specific year in the 12-year cycle</note> is in the same zodiac sign that Venus occupied at the time of birth, or if that birth-Venus sign is in the seventh house <note>The house of marriage and partnerships</note> during the year, the man will marry in that year. This yoga <note>astrological combination</note> is also supported by the text *Tajika Sara*, which states "**The marriage of the Lord of the Ascendant and Venus**"—meaning the Lord of the Ascendant being in the sign of Venus is also considered authoritative proof. || 5 ||

**Anustubh Meter—With a waning Moon in the place of Venus, predict minimal sexual intercourse. Mars in the birth-sign of Venus, if strong, creates a celebration of feminine pleasure. || 6 ||**

If the Moon is waning <note>original: "nashtendu", literally 'lost' or 'diminished' Moon</note> during the year while positioned in the sign occupied by Venus at birth, there will be little sexual pleasure this year. However, if a strong Mars is positioned in the birth-sign of Venus during the year, there will be a festive abundance of pleasure with women. || 6 ||

**Vasantatilaka Meter—If the birth seventh-lord is joined with or aspected by the Year-Lord Venus, there will be union with women characterized by great playfulness and happiness. If Jupiter is in a center or trine from the birth-Venus sign, happiness from women is said; likewise for the Lord of the Term and the Marriage Lot. || 7 ||**

1. If the Lord of the Seventh House at birth is joined with or aspected by <note>aspected: a 'drishti' or planetary gaze/influence</note> Venus during the year in any house, there will be union with women full of playfulness, laughter, and joy. 
2. If Jupiter is in a Center <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> or a Trine <note>houses 1, 5, or 9</note> from the sign occupied by Venus at birth, there will be happiness from women. 
3. If the Lord of the *Hadda* <note>term/bounds; a specific sub-division of a zodiac sign</note> of the Year-Ascendant is in the birth-sign of Venus and located in a Center or Trine from the Year-Ascendant, there will be happiness from women. 
4. Similarly, if the Lord of the Marriage *Saham* <note>Marriage Lot; a calculated mathematical point for marriage</note> is in the birth-sign of Venus and located in a Center or Trine from the Year-Ascendant, one attains a wife. These are the four yogas. || 7 ||

**Anustubh Meter—When the Sun is in the place of the Officials, there is constant anxiety from women. In the place of the Muntha-lord, Jupiter’s aspect brings marriage. || 8 ||**

If the Sun is in the sign of any of the Five Officials <note>Pancha-adhikari: the five planets holding specific administrative strength for the year</note>, there will be constant anxiety or distress caused by women. Furthermore, if Jupiter is in the sign of the Lord of the *Muntha* <note>a sensitive point that moves one sign per year</note>, or if Jupiter is in the sign of the *Muntha* itself, or if Jupiter aspects the *Muntha* sign, the "Yoga of Marriage" is declared. || 8 ||

# Now, the Consideration of the Eighth House

If Mars is the Lord of the Year <term>Varshasvami: the planet ruling the specific year of life</term> and is afflicted by malefic planets and devoid of strength, there will be injury to a limb caused by iron weapons. The specific limb affected should be determined by the *Drekkana* <note>A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> as explained in the Chapter on Definitions. Furthermore, if this Mars is in a Fire sign (Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius), there is danger from fire. If this same Mars is in a "human" or "two-footed" sign (Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or the first half of Sagittarius), death or danger may come from thieves or wicked men. || 1 ||

Similarly, if Mars is the Lord of the Year, weak and afflicted by malefics, and is placed in the tenth house, there will be fear or danger from the King, a government minister, enemies, or thieves. If such a Mars is in the fourth house, there will be fear or danger from the mother, paternal uncles, maternal uncles, or the father. || 2 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant, the Lord of the *Muntha*, and the Lord of the Year are in an *Itthashala* yoga <term>Itthashala: a specific aspect/configuration in Tajika astrology indicating the coming together of two planetary influences</term> with the Lord of the Eighth House, it is said to result in death. If this occurs during an unfavorable planetary period, death is certain. If the Sun and Mars are involved and the Lord of the Year is strong, there is fear from the government during the day. || 3 ||

The Lord of the Ascendant, the Lord of the *Muntha*, and the Lord of the Year, if forming an *Itthashala* with the Lord of the Eighth House, indicate the result of death...

### With Commentary ###

**In the Rathoddhata meter: If the Moon is in the House of Merit <note>Punya Saham: a specific Arabic part or sensitive point in Tajika astrology representing fortune and virtue</note> and a malefic planet is in the seventh house from it, or if malefic planets occupy the second and twelfth houses from the ascendant, it brings death-like suffering. Similarly, if malefic planets are in the second and twelfth houses from the House of Merit or the Moon's sign, the same result occurs. This is specifically known as the "Malefic Scissor" yoga <note>Papakatari Yoga: when a house or planet is hemmed in by malefic planets on both sides</note>. One should apply this analysis to the birth ascendant, the year ascendant, the House of Merit, and the Moon's sign. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Year or the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth House are situated in the eighth house, it yields these results. || 24 ||**

# Now begins the analysis of the Ninth House. #

**In the Anustubh meter: If Mars is the Lord of the Year, is positioned in the third or ninth house, is powerful, and is not joined by malefic planets, then travel will be beneficial. In such a case, even unstable or moving tasks will become stable; that is, work related to water or canals will bring auspicious results. || 1 ||**

**If the Sun is the Lord of the Year, is positioned in the third or ninth house, and forms a Kambuli Yoga <note>Kambuli: a Tajika aspect similar to Ithasala involving the Moon, indicating the completion of a task</note> with the Moon, it grants happiness during travel. If the Sun is in its own sign or exaltation, the travel occurs by one's own will. However, if the Sun lacks such dignity, the journey occurs at the command or sending of another, and there may be no happiness on the way. || 2 ||**

**If Venus is the Lord of the Year and is in the third or ninth house, there is happiness in travel. If it is retrograde or combust, the journey is difficult or bad. If a benefic planet is so situated, it indicates a pilgrimage or a divine journey. || 3 ||**

# Tajika Nilakanthi

Page 154

If the Lord of the Year <note>The planet ruling the specific year in the individual's life cycle</note>, Venus, is in the third or ninth house, is free from the influence of cruel planets <note>Malefics like Mars or Saturn</note>, is strong, and is in retrograde motion, there will be happiness on the journey. If Venus is combust <note>Too close to the sun to be seen</note> while in these positions, the journey will be difficult or contrary to one's desires. If the Lord of the Year, Mercury, is free from sin <note>unafflicted by malefic planets</note>, strong, and retrograde in the third or ninth house, there will be a pilgrimage to a holy site or a journey related to the deities.

> *If afflicted by cruel planets, there is a bad journey; one should consider it a difficult path. If there is an Itthashala <term>Itthashala: an aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</term> between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Ninth, there is an unexpected journey.*

Just like the aforementioned Mercury, if Jupiter is the Lord of the Year, free from malefic planets, and situated in the 3rd or 9th houses, it grants a pilgrimage to holy places or temples. If it is weak or afflicted by cruel planets, it results in a "bad vehicle" <note>an uncomfortable or ill-fated journey</note>. If there is an *Itthashala* between the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnashesh</note> and the Lord of the Ninth House <note>Dharmesh</note>, an unexpected journey occurs—one that was not even in one's thoughts or possibilities.

> *When the Lord of the Ascendant gives its light to the Lord of the Ninth, it grants a journey that was previously planned. The same applies to the connection between the Ascendant and the Year Lord, or the Munthaha and the Lord of the Ascendant.*

If the Lord of the Ascendant gives its "Tejas" <note>light or power</note> to the Lord of the Ninth—meaning the Lord of the Ascendant is faster with fewer degrees and the Lord of the Ninth is slower with more degrees, and both are within their orb of influence—it indicates a pre-planned journey. If the Lord of the Ninth gives its light to the Lord of the Ascendant, the journey is unexpected. The same results apply to the yoga <note>conjunction or aspect</note> between the Lord of the Year-Ascendant and the Lord of the Year, or between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Munthaha <term>Munthaha: a sensitive point in Tajika astrology that progresses one sign per year</term>.

> *When Mars is in the house occupied by Jupiter and in the ninth house, it gives a good journey with servants and wealth. When Mars is in the house of Mercury and is aspected by the Lord of the Ascendant, it gives happiness in travel.*

If Mars, in the yearly chart, is in the same zodiac sign that Jupiter occupied at the time of birth, and this occurs in the ninth house, one gains servants and wealth during the journey. If Mars is in the same sign that Mercury occupied at birth, and the Lord of the Ascendant aspects <note>looks at</note> it, there will be comfort and happiness in travel.

> *The Lord of the Ascendant, if in its own place or strong and aspecting the Ascendant, gives a good journey. When Mercury, the ruler of the birth, is in the house of Saturn and joined with a cruel planet...*

# Now begins the consideration of the Tenth House.

> <term>Translation</term><note>original: "Anu." abbreviation for Anuvada/Translation</note>: When the Lord of the Year is strong and situated in the tenth house, there is kingdom, wealth, happiness, and fame. If it is in another <term>Kendra</term>, there is the attainment of a house and happiness. || 1 ||

If the strong <term>Varshesha</term><note>The planetary ruler of the specific year in a Tajika solar return chart</note> is in the tenth house, one receives a kingdom (status) according to their family lineage, as well as wealth, happiness, and fame. If it is in another center—the first, fourth, or seventh houses—one receives happiness related to the home. || 1 ||

> <term>Translation</term>: Likewise, a strong Sun situated in the fourth house brings the attainment of a position earned by one's ancestors. If this same Sun is in the eleventh house, there will be friendship with the best of the King's <term>Amatyas</term>. || 2 ||

If the <term>Varshesha</term> is the Sun and it is strong in the fourth house, one receives the kingdom or some authority earned by their father or grandfathers. If such a Sun is in the eleventh house, there will be friendship with the King's high-ranking <term>Amatyas</term><note>Ministers or high-level counselors; often translated as Viziers in this period</note> and others. || 2 ||

> <term>Translation</term>: If the Sun's position is in the <term>Ithasala</term><note>A specific Tajika aspect where a faster planet approaches a slower one</note> with the Ascendant or the tenth house, it grants the attainment of a kingdom and happiness. If the Sun is in its sign of debilitation and joined with malefic planets, it indicates imprisonment or death at the hands of the King. || 3 ||

**Verse: If the Sun is strong and well-placed in Leo, there is gain of position and shelter from a king. If the Moon is strong in the place of Mars, there is the acquisition of a different or higher position. ॥ 4 ॥**

If the Sun of the birth chart is in the sign of Leo and is strong in the tenth house of the yearly chart, then a new position and the patronage of a king are obtained. **Verse: If such a Mars is in the third or ninth house and is 'burnt' or 'destroyed,' there is an accumulation of sin. If Saturn is the Lord of the Year, holds authority, and is in the third or ninth house, it increases righteousness. ॥ 7 ॥**

If the yearly Mars is in the sign occupied by Saturn at birth, but is placed in the third or ninth house and is 'burnt' <note>combust, or too close to the Sun</note> or 'destroyed' (lacking strength), then there is an increase in sin through the destruction of merit. Conversely, if Saturn is the Lord of the Year, possesses planetary strength, and is in the third or ninth house, it increases righteousness through the destruction of sins. ॥ 7 ॥

Likewise, if the Year-lord <term>Varsh-esh; the planet ruling the specific year in a chart</term> Saturn is the authority and is "combust" <note>original: "dagdh"; a planet too close to the sun, losing its power</note> or destroyed, then in this year the person becomes a sinner and a slanderer of religion. > Verse: If the Muntha is situated there, there is an arrival of merit; if associated with malefics, there is sin. If the Sun is the lord of the tenth house in the birth chart and is in the tenth house in the year-chart, and there is an Itthashala... || 9 ||

The <term>Muntha; a sensitive mathematical point in Tajika astrology that moves one sign per year</term> brings the arrival of merit and religious deeds if placed in the third or ninth house. If the Muntha is associated with malefic planets in these same houses, it brings about sinful results. If the Sun, being the lord of the tenth house at birth, is also in the tenth house during the year and is strong, and also forms an <term>Itthashala; a favorable aspect or "link" between two planets</term> with the (slow-moving) Lord of the Ascendant, then the person attains a kingdom or high status according to their strength. || 9 ||

> Verse: The attainment of a kingdom is spoken of through the Lord of the Ascendant according to its strength. If the lords of the ninth and tenth houses are combust, they bring the destruction of religion and the kingdom. || 10 ||

### Thus ends the consideration of the Tenth House (Karma).

When the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, one attains a kingdom according to that strength. If the Lord of the Ninth <note>the house of religion and fortune</note> and the Lord of the Tenth <note>the house of career and action</note> are combust or afflicted by malefic planets, they cause the decay of religion and the state. Here, the specific consideration is that the Tenth House, the <term>Rajya Saham; a specific Arabic Part or lot signifying power</term>, the <term>Karma Saham; the lot signifying action</term>, the Ascendant, and their respective lords give auspicious results if they are strong and associated with benefic planets. If they are retrograde, combust, weak, or associated with malefics, they give inauspicious results. || 10 ||

# Now, the Consideration of the Twelfth House (House of Loss)

**Vasantatilaka Meter**—If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnesha</note> and the Lord of the Year <note>Varshasvami</note> are devoid of strength and situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, one should predict results according to the nature of the signs they occupy. If the Lord of the Year is Venus, is lacking in strength, is aspected by malefic planets with a cruel gaze, and is situated in the sixth house in a human sign... || 1 || ...there will be loss of servants. If Venus is in a quadruped <note>four-legged</note> sign, there is loss of horses and similar animals. This same result is spoken of for other Year Lords as well. If Mars is well-placed and joined with the Moon, there is loss of horses and such; if Mars is afflicted by malefics, there is great mental distress. || 2 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Year are weak and placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, they give results according to the nature of the sign (such as quadruped signs). If a quadruped sign is in the aforementioned houses, there will be destruction of or by four-legged animals; this is the general consideration of this house. Specifically, if Venus is powerless in the sixth house, aspected by malefics with a cruel vision, and is in a human sign <note>e.g., Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius</note>, there will be loss of servants. If such a Venus is in a quadruped sign <note>e.g., Aries, Taurus, Leo</note>, it causes the loss of elephants, horses, and other livestock. The same should be predicted if the Lord of the Year is in the eighth or twelfth houses. If the Lord of the Year is Mars and is with the Moon in the tenth house, it causes the loss of horses etc., and also causes agitation in the mind. Furthermore, Mars in the sixth house afflicted by malefics gives this same result. || 1 || 2 ||

**Vasantatilaka Meter**—If the Sun is in the sixth house, afflicted by malefics and placed in a quadruped sign, there will be quarrels with one's servants; the same result occurs if the Sun is in the eighth or twelfth houses. If Saturn is the Lord of the Year, possesses strength, and is placed in the sixth or twelfth house, there will be the establishment of a residence on abandoned land and the construction of gardens and reservoirs. || 3 ||

If the Sun as Year Lord is in the sixth house, oppressed by malefics and in a quadruped sign, there will be strife with one's own employees; this also applies to the eighth and twelfth houses. If Saturn is the Year Lord, is strong, and is in the sixth or twelfth house, one gains a livelihood by settling new colonies on abandoned land, and there is the construction of plantations, water-works, wells, ponds, and streams. || 3 ||

**Upajati Meter**—If the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in his own sign or sign of exaltation in the tenth house, there is freedom from disease. If Jupiter is so placed, there is acquisition of wealth. If the Sun is so placed, wealth comes from the King; if Mars, through the strength of one's arms; if Mercury, through medicine, astrology, poetry, and crafts. || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Year, <term>Saturn</term> <note>Shani</note>, is in its own signs (Capricorn or Aquarius) or in its sign of exaltation (Libra) and is placed in the tenth house, the body remains free from disease and there is an influx of wealth. If <term>Jupiter</term> <note>Brihaspati</note>, as the Lord of the Year, is in its own signs (射手座 Sagittarius or Pisces) or its sign of exaltation (Cancer) in the tenth house, it gives the same auspicious results. If the Lord of the Year, the <term>Sun</term> <note>Surya</note>, is in its own sign (Leo) or its sign of exaltation (Aries) in the tenth house, one receives wealth from the government or authorities. If the Lord of the Year, <term>Mars</term> <note>Mangal</note>, is in its own signs (Aries or Scorpio) or its sign of exaltation (Capricorn) in the tenth house, wealth is acquired through one's own physical strength and valor. If the Lord of the Year, <term>Mercury</term> <note>Budha</note>, is in its own signs (Gemini or Virgo) or its sign of exaltation in the tenth house, profit is gained through medicine, astrology, and craftsmanship <note>shilpa</note>. || 4 ||

> <note>original: "मंदेडब्दे गतबले नैराश्यं दौस्थ्यमादिशेत् ॥ सूर्येडब्देशे शशिस्थाने मंदेडब्दजनुषोर्हते ॥ ५ ॥"</note>

If the Lord of the Year, Saturn, is weak and <term>afflicted by malefics</term> <note>papakranta; influenced by naturally "cruel" planets like Mars or Rahu</note>, there is despair (loss of gains) and a lack of stability in one's position. If the Sun is the Lord of the Year, and Saturn occupies the sign of the natal Moon during the year, and if Saturn is weak and afflicted by malefics in both the birth chart and the annual chart, then there is failure and frustration in all auspicious works. Similarly, if Saturn is <term>retrograde</term> <note>vakra; appearing to move backward</note> or <term>combust</term> <note>astangata; too close to the Sun</note>, the same negative results occur. || 5 ||

> <note>original: "सर्वकर्मसु वैकल्यं वक्रेऽस्ते च तथा पुनः ॥ कर्मकर्मेशसह्मनाथाः शनियुतेक्षिताः ॥ ६ ॥"</note>

The meaning of the first half of this verse was explained in the previous 5th verse. The meaning of the second half is: if the tenth house, the <term>Lord of the Tenth</term> <note>Dashamesha</note>, the <term>Lord of Action</term> <note>Karmesha</note>, and the Lord of the <term>Saham of Action</term> <note>Sahamesha; a specific sensitive point in the chart related to career</note> are joined with or aspected by Saturn, then there is failure in actions and useless exertion. || 6 ||

> <note>original: "षडष्टव्ययगेऽब्देशे कर्मेशे च बलोज्झिते ॥ सूतावब्दे च न शुभं तत्राब्दे मृतिपे तथा ॥ ७ ॥"</note>

If the Lord of the Year is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house <note>the "Dusthanas" or difficult houses</note>, and the Lord of the Tenth from both the birth and annual charts is weak, and if the Lord of the Eighth House of the year is also in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, then there will be no auspicious results in this year. || 7 ||

> <note>original: "यत्र भावे शुभफलो दृष्टो वा जन्मनि ग्रहः ॥ वर्षे तद्भावगस्तादृक्तत्फलं यच्छति ध्रुवम् ॥ ८ ॥"</note>

In whichever house a planet gave auspicious results or was aspected favorably at birth, if that planet occupies the same house in the annual chart, it will certainly grant similar auspicious results. || 8 ||

Whichever planet is designated to give auspicious or inauspicious results in a particular house at the time of birth, if that same planet occupies the same position during the solar return year, it will certainly provide those results with even greater intensity. || 8 ||

<term>Indravajra</term> <note>A classical Sanskrit poetic meter used here for the astrological verse.</note>—Those planets which are strong at birth but weak in the yearly chart grant happiness in the first half of the year and distress in the latter half. Conversely, those weak at birth but strong in the year grant distress first and happiness later. If they are equally strong in both charts, the results remain consistent throughout. || 9 ||

->Thus ends the consideration of the Twelfth House (House of Expenditure).<-

A planet that is powerful at birth but lacks strength in the yearly transition provides good results in the first half of the year and unfavorable results in the second half. Those that are weak at birth but gain strength in the year provide unfavorable results in the first half and favorable results in the second half. If they are equally powerful in both instances, they provide uniform results. || 9 ||

->Thus ends the chapter on the results of the Twelfth House by the illustrious Mahidhara. || 12 ||<-

---

<term>Shardulavikridita</term> <note>A complex Sanskrit meter often used for concluding or celebratory verses.</note>—The ornament of the lineage of Sage Garga was the mathematician Chintamani; his son Ananta, possessed of infinite intellect, composed a system of birth horoscopy to destroy the opinions of the wicked. His son, the wise Neelakantha, by the command of the learned Shiva, composed this analysis of the houses from the <term>Tajika</term> <note>A system of Sanskrit astrology influenced by Persian/Arabic traditions</note> scriptures for the satisfaction of the learned. || 10 ||

->Thus ends the consideration of the twelve houses in the Tajika Neelakanthi.<-

This verse belongs to the chapter's conclusion; its meaning is as stated previously. The specific detail here is that the analysis of the house results has been compiled in this chapter according to the opinions of the finest <term>Tajika texts</term>. || 10 ||

->Thus ends the fifth section on the strength of the houses in the vernacular commentary of Neelakanthi by the illustrious Mahidhara. || 5 ||<-

### Now, the consideration of the sequence of the Yearly Periods.

<term>Upajati</term> <note>A Sanskrit meter formed by combining Indravajra and Upendravajra.</note>—Having calculated the precise positions of the planets along with the Ascendant, and disregarding the signs, place the one with the lowest degrees first. Then, place the others in increasing order of their degrees; this shall be the sequence of the <term>Dashas</term> <note>Planetary periods or "timings" of events</note> for the year. || 1 ||

The sequence of the <term>Patyanshi Dasha</term> <note>A specific method of calculating planetary periods based on the degrees a planet has traveled within a sign</note> is now described. First, after calculating the exact positions of all planets including the Ascendant, one should ignore the zodiac signs and arrange them according to their degrees and minutes. The order is as follows:

> *Upajati Meter* — Subtract the lower value from the higher value in sequence. The sum of these individual differences <note>original: "vishu-dhansha-sheshakaikyam"</note> will be exactly equal to the value of the planet with the highest degrees. This total is then used to divide the measure of the year. || 2 ||

The planet with the lowest degrees of all is subtracted from the one with the next highest degrees. Then, that higher one is subtracted from the one even higher than it. After subtracting all in this manner, the sum of all these "reduced portions" <note><term>Patyansha</term>: The net value remaining after subtracting the previous planet's degrees from the current one.</note> will be equal to the planet with the highest degrees <note>the Moon in this example</note>. If they match, the calculation is correct.

**Example:** The lowest degrees belong to Mercury: 2 | 18 | 28. This remains as it is. Next is the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> at 8 | 57 | 2. Subtracting Mercury from this gives 6 | 38 | 34; these are the "reduced portions" for the Ascendant. Next is the Sun at 9 | 36 | 57. Subtracting the Ascendant's degrees (8 | 57 | 2) leaves 0 | 39 | 55 for the Sun. Continuing this for all, the final planet with the highest degrees is the Moon at 28 | 16 | 31. The sum of all reduced portions also equals this same value. This is for the purpose of verification <note>original: "nishchayarth"</note>.

### Portions of the Nodes (Patayansha)

The reasoning is—even with reduced degrees, the Moon remains the one with the highest degrees. By using the "Portions of the Nodes" <note>Patayansha: a specific calculation in Tajika astrology used to determine the duration of planetary periods</note> and summing all the degrees and their subunits, the maximum value is obtained. Divide the total duration of the year—either the Solar year of 360 days or the Savana <note>terrestrial/civil</note> year of 365 days, 15 minutes, 31 seconds, and 30 thirds—by this final maximum degree. The resulting quotient will be the "Constant Multiplier" (Dhruvanka) for the year. || 2 ||

->*Upajati Meter—Multiply those purified degrees by this obtained Constant Multiplier; the result will truly be the measure of that planet's period (Dasha) in days and subunits. One should then declare the results according to the scriptures.* || 3 ||<-

Using the "Constant Multiplier" obtained as described, multiply each planet's "Portion of the Node" (Patayansha) using the <term>Gomutrika</term> <note>literally "cow's urine track"; a zigzag method of multiplication used in ancient Indian mathematics</note> sequence or by reducing them to a single denomination. Keep the three resulting figures in the form of days, Ghatis, and Palas <note>traditional units of time: 1 Ghati = 24 minutes; 1 Pala = 24 seconds</note>. Place these under each respective planet; this constitutes the "Dasha" (period) of that planet. After determining the periods for all planets in days and subunits, add the first planet's period to the Sun's degrees at the start of the year, then add the subsequent planets in order, writing them below. At the end, the calculated position will match the Sun's exact position for the following year. Alternatively, add the first period to the day and time of the year's commencement; by adding them all in sequence, the day and time of the next year's commencement will be accurately found. Similarly, by adding the Savana lunar dates (Tithis), the dates for the next year are found.

**Example:** The sum of all Portions of the Nodes is 28 | 16 | 31; this is the final value for the Moon. Now, the year's duration must be divided by this. First, reduce the sum to a single denomination: multiply 28 by 60 to get 1680 <term>Kala</term> <note>minutes of arc</note>, add 16 to get 1696. Multiply this by 60 to get 101760, and add 31 <term>Vikala</term> <note>seconds of arc</note> to get 101791. This is the converted divisor. Similarly, multiply the dividend of 360 days twice by 60 to get 1296000. Dividing this by the divisor gives 12; the remainder 74508 multiplied by 60 and divided gives 43; repeating this gives 55. Thus, 12 | 43 | 55 is the Constant Multiplier. With this, for all planets...

By following the *Gomutrika* <note>original: "Gomutrika" - a zigzag mathematical method used in Vedic arithmetic</note> sequence of degrees and other units, the days and other time-measures of each planetary period are determined. First, add the days and units of the first period-holder to the longitude of the Sun at the exact moment of the year's commencement. Then, add the subsequent period to that sum. By adding all periods in this sequence, you will ultimately arrive at the Sun's longitude for the commencement of the following year. Alternatively, one may add the elapsed days, *ghatis*, and *palas* <note>traditional units of time: 1 ghati = 24 minutes; 1 pala = 24 seconds</note> of the first period-holder to the entry date and time of the current year, then continue adding the others in sequence; the final result will be the day and time of the next year's commencement. For example—at the start of the year, the Sun's longitude was 3 signs, 9 degrees, 36 minutes, and 57 seconds. At this moment, the period of Mercury began. Mercury's period, calculated by the previous method, is 29 days, 22 *ghatis*, and 6 *palas*. Adding this to the Sun's longitude, we find that Mercury's period lasts until the Sun reaches 4 signs, 8 degrees, 59 minutes, and 3 seconds. After this, the period of the next sign begins. For a detailed example, the planetary ripening periods and the Sun's longitude are written in the table. By adding the values of the Sun's transit in this way, the sequence of the solar entry dates is obtained. || 3 ||

->Tajika Neelakanthi<-

The order of the major periods (Dashas) is determined by the degrees: the one with the fewest degrees is written first, followed by the one with more, and so on. If the degrees and minutes of two planets are exactly equal, then the one that is more powerful <note>referring to Shadbala or positional strength</note> shall be the first period-lord. Here, the reading "equality of pure degrees" <note>original: "shuddhansha-samye"</note> is improper; rather, the reading "equality of lesser degrees" <note>original: "hinansha-samye"</note> is more appropriate. When the strength is also equal, the planet with the slower motion is written first, and the one with faster motion follows. In the case of equality between a planet and the Ascendant (Lagna), one must consider the strength of the Ascendant-lord; whoever is stronger takes precedence. This is the established order. || 4 ||

Regarding the sub-periods (Antardashas), there is a verse from another text: "Divide the product of one's own period days and their own degrees by the sum of the pure degrees... the sub-periods and even the minor sub-periods are found in sequence." || 1 ||

That is to say, to find the sub-period of a specific planet, first multiply its "pure degrees" by its own degrees, then multiply by the degrees of whichever planets' sub-periods are being calculated, and divide by the total sum of degrees. The resulting quotient gives the value of the sub-period according to its category. Alternatively (another method): multiply the days of the major period by the days of the planet whose sub-period is desired, and divide by the sum of the "lesser degrees" (the total sum); the quotient in days and minutes becomes the sub-period. In this manner, every planet has a sub-period within the major period of every other planet.

**Example:** The Ascendant's period is 83 days, 44 minutes, and 28 seconds. We wish to find the sub-periods within this. The first is Mercury, whose period is 29 days and 22 minutes. The total sum of all planetary periods is 360 days, 0 minutes, and 0 seconds. By applying the <term>Zig-zag Method</term> <note>original: "Gomutrika-krama," literally "the path of cow's urine," a mathematical term for a specific multiplication layout</note> and multiplying the Ascendant by Mercury, we get 2509:20:13. Dividing this by 360, we get 6 days, 58 minutes, and 13 seconds as Mercury's sub-period within the Ascendant's major period. One should calculate the sub-periods of other planets in the same way. If the sum of all sub-periods matches the total days of the major period-lord, consider the calculation accurate. This same sequence of periods applies to the Solar Return (Monthly Entrance) as well, as stated:

"By the sum of the degrees to be fallen, one should divide the product of the elapsed and remaining months..."

"The periods are multiplied in the stated order for the monthly results of the planetary periods." <note>original Sanskrit: "saṃguṇitādaśāḥ syuruktakramānmāsaphale daśānām"</note> To find the monthly period, multiply the planetary strength units <term>Patyansha: a specific numerical value assigned to planets in Tajika astrology to determine the duration of their influence</term> by 30 and divide by the total sum of all planetary strength units. By this method, the period for each planet is determined. According to the school of Gauri <note>A traditional authority in astrological calculation</note>, for the first lord of the period, one looks at the lunar mansion <term>Nakshatra: one of the 27 sectors of the sky through which the moon passes</term> on the day the month begins. Starting from the mansions of Krittika, Uttara Phalguni, and Uttara Ashadha, the sequence of lords follows: Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, and Venus in three cycles. This determines the first ruler of the period. Their values in days are as follows:

| Sun | Moon | Mars | Rahu | Jup | Sat | Merc | Ketu | Ven |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 2 | 5 |

<note>The table values represent the proportional weight or days assigned to each planet under this specific calculation method.</note>

One should know this from the day's lunar mansion at the start of the month. Just as there are ten main types of periods in a natal horoscope, there are also ten types for the yearly chart: 1. Patyanshi, 2. Tasir, 3. Bhava-Tasir, 4. Sthala-Bhava-Tasir, 5. Kala-Hora, 6. Hadda, 7. Naisargika, 8. Tanu-Bhava, 9. Muda, and 10. Balarama-mata. Out of fear of making the book too voluminous, the author has primarily established the Patyanshi system here. However, just as the Great Periods <term>Mahadasha</term> are used in natal astrology, the Muda Dasha system is commonly practiced and experienced in results for yearly charts. Therefore, I am writing the sequence of this period system:

> "Add the number of the birth mansion to the elapsed years of life, subtract two, and divide the remainder by nine. The remainder indicates the lords of the periods in the order of Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, and Venus for that year." <note>original Sanskrit: "janmarkṣasaṃkhyāsahitā gatābdā dvigunitānandahatāvaśeṣāḥ..."</note>

Add the elapsed years to the birth mansion number, subtract two, and divide the remainder by 9. The remaining number indicates the period lord in the sequence of Sun, Moon, Mars, etc. For example: if the birth mansion is Rohini (the 4th mansion) and the elapsed years are 8, the sum is 12. Subtracting 2 leaves 10. Dividing by 9 leaves a remainder of 1. Thus, the Sun's period is first. If the remainder is 2, it is the Moon; 3 is Mars; 4 is Rahu; 5 is Jupiter; 6 is Saturn; 7 is Mercury; 8 is Ketu; and 9 (or 0) is Venus. Furthermore, the standard natal period years for the planets—Sun 6, Moon 10, Mars 7, Rahu 18, Jupiter 16, Saturn 19, Mercury 17, Ketu 7, and Venus 20—are multiplied by three to find the days in a year...

This is the Sun's sub-period within the Sun's major period. Next, the Moon's multiplier is 8; multiplying the Sun's 18 days by 8 gives 144. Dividing by 60 gives 2 days and 24 units. This is the Moon's sub-period within the Sun's period. All other planets should be understood in this way, as clearly shown in the chart.

-># Tajika Nilakanthi<-
<note>The Tajika Nilakanthi is a classic 16th-century Sanskrit treatise on Tajika astrology, which incorporates Persian astrological influences into the Indian tradition.</note>

By fate (fortune), the gain of wealth and the service of those without honor causes further distress to the mind. <note>original: "दिष्टं दैवं भागधेयम्" - "Fate, destiny, and fortune are synonymous," quoting the Amarakosha lexicon.</note> || 6 ||

> Traveling abroad, distress, loss of intellect, and bad expenditures;
> It causes loss of honor; such is the result of the period of a troubled Ascendant. || 7 ||

The result of the period of a troubled Ascendant <term>Kashta-Lagna-Dasha: a period ruled by a rising sign that is weakened or afflicted</term>—Going to foreign lands, suffering, destruction of wisdom, wasteful spending, and loss of prestige are caused by the troubled Ascendant period. The period of a cruel Ascendant <term>Krura-Lagna: an Ascendant ruled by a malefic planet like Mars or Saturn</term> remains mediocre. It brings little happiness, spending of wealth, pain in the limbs, physical weakness, death, and quarrels. || 8 ||

### The Results of the Sun’s Period

> <note>original: "Upajati" - a specific Sanskrit poetic meter.</note> The period of a Sun with full strength gives gains of elephants, horses, gold, garments, and jewels;
> It grants rise in status from the king, and fame through the worship of gods and Brahmins. || 9 ||

Now the results of the planetary periods are described—If the Sun's period is in effect and the Sun is at full strength <term>Purna-Bali: possessing maximum directional, positional, and temporal strength</term>, there will be great profit in elephants, horses, gold, and gems. It also grants an increase in honor from the sovereign and brings fame through the worship of deities and the learned. || 9 ||

> The period of a Sun with medium strength gives all these results in a moderate way;
> Gain of happiness comes through village authority, business, courage, and according to the status of one's lineage. || 10 ||

If the Sun has medium strength, then in its period, the previously mentioned results are moderate; it grants happiness and gains through administrative rights over villages, business ventures, fortitude, and honors consistent with one's family standing. || 10 ||

> The period of a Sun with little strength gives men sorrow through disputes with their own kin;
> Confusion of mind, bile-related illnesses, loss of one's luster, and humiliation by enemies. || 11 ||

A Sun with little strength <term>Alpa-Bali: weak in the birth chart</term> gives various types of sorrow during its period, as well as disputes with one's own people, clouded judgment, illnesses caused by "pitta" <note>Pitta refers to the fire/bile humor in Ayurvedic medicine, often causing fever or inflammation.</note>, loss of wealth, and even defeat at the hands of enemies. || 11 ||

> The period of a Sun with no strength gives men fear from the king and others, and loss of wealth;
> It causes disputes with wife, son, friends, and others, as well as mental confusion and disease. || 12 ||

**Upendravajra Meter—The period of the body (the Ascendant) gives results equal to the strength of its lord; this is another specific rule. ||**
**In a Moveable sign, the results are auspicious, middling, and poor; in a Dual sign, the opposite is said to be true. || 44 ||**

The period of the Ascendant <note>Lagna-dasha</note> gives results according to the strength of its lord. For example, if the Lord of the Ascendant is rising or situated in its own house, it gives the full auspicious results described for that period; if it is set <note>combust</note> or in its sign of debilitation, it gives the results of a weak period. There is a specific detail here: in a Moveable sign <note>Chara-rashi: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, if the first Decan <note>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</note> is rising, the period is auspicious; in the second Decan, the results are middling; and in the third Decan, the results are poor. In a Dual sign <note>Dvisvabhava-rashi: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, it is the opposite of the Moveable sign—meaning the first Decan gives poor results, the second middling, and the third gives the results of a strong, auspicious period. || 44 ||

**Upendravajra Meter—In a Fixed sign, the results are poor, auspicious, and middling respectively by the Decans, as stated by the ancients. ||**
**Happiness comes from the association or aspect of a benefic lord; suffering should be predicted from the aspect of a malefic. || 45 ||**

In a Fixed sign <note>Sthira-rashi: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, if the first Decan is rising, it gives the results of a weak period; the second gives the results of a strong period; and the third gives middling results. In this manner, the ancient teachers have described the third type of result for the Ascendant period based on the Decans. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Ascendant aspects the Ascendant or is placed within it, happiness is predicted; if there is association with or aspect from malefic planets, then suffering must be predicted. || 45 ||

### Now, the Method for Sub-periods.

**Anushtubh Meter—Taking the total span of the period as the measure, and following the previously mentioned path, ||**
**The sub-periods should be calculated according to the previously established fractional shares. || 46 ||**

Regarding the method for sub-periods <note>Antardasha</note>: the same method used previously to calculate the fractional share periods <note>Patyanshi-dasha</note> applies here as well. The only difference is that where the measure of a civil year was used, one should now use the days and minutes of the specific major period lord. For instance, just as the fractional shares were previously taken based on the lowest degrees, and the solar or civil days were divided by the sum of those shares to find a constant, that same constant <note>Dhruvak</note> should be recognized for the sub-periods. By multiplying all the fractional shares by that constant, each sub-period—

# Tajika Nilakanthi

### Example of Venus Sub-period Calculations

| Ven. | Jup. | Mar. | Sat. | Mon. | Mer. | Asc. | Sun | Total | Planets |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 18 | 29 | 50 | 57 | 41 | 33 | 48 | 24 | 00 | |
| 7 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 9 | 9 | 10 | 10 | <insert>Solar Entry Figures</insert> |
| 12 | 4 | 12 | 14 | 20 | 11 | 18 | 9 | 12 | |

| 5 | 21 | 58 | 29 | 9 | 24 | 33 | 4 | 22 | |
| 0 | 18 | 47 | 37 | 34 | 15 | 48 | 36 | 00 | |

The period is obtained. Example: The days of the Venus period etc. are 90 | 42 | 17. Having performed <term>Savarna</term> <note>original: "सवर्ण" - the process of reducing fractions to a common denominator for mathematical operations</note> and dividing by the sum of the previously calculated <term>Patyansha</term> <note>original: "पात्यांश" - specific fractional portions or degrees assigned to planets in the Tajika system</note>, the resulting <term>Dhruvaka</term> <note>original: "ध्रुवक" - a constant or multiplier used in astronomical tables</note> is 3 | 12 | 28. By multiplying each planet's Patyansha by this constant, the <term>Antardasha</term> <note>sub-period of a planet</note> for each is found. Afterward, additions should be made as before based on the Sun's position or the days of the solar transit. || 46 ||

<margin>Anushtubh Meter</margin> 
> **At the beginning is the sub-period of the Lord of the Period, followed by the others in their specific order. ||**
> **One should determine the results based on the aspects or associations of auspicious planets and their friendships. || 47 ||**

In the <term>Antardasha</term> <note>sub-period</note>, first is the <term>Dashapati</term> <note>Lord of the major period</note>, meaning the one whose sub-period it is. Thereafter, all planets should be written in the order prescribed for that period. One should declare the results after observing the four-fold strength of the sub-period lord. For instance, if there is an aspect or conjunction of auspicious planets with the sub-period lord, the results should be declared as auspicious or inauspicious according to its position in exaltation, debilitation, setting, or rising. Similarly, the results of the sub-period should be known through conjunctions or aspects with malefic planets. || 47 ||

<margin>Anushtubh Meter</margin> 
> **Moon, Mars, and Jupiter; Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus; Sun, Moon, and Mars; Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus; || 48 ||**
> **Sun, Moon, and Mars; Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn; Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus—these are the auspicious sub-periods starting from the Sun. ||**
> **The others should be known as inauspicious; thus it was spoken by Vamana. || 49 ||**

In the period of the Sun: Moon, Mars, and Jupiter [are auspicious]. In the period of the Moon: Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus. In the period of Mars: Sun and Moon. In the period of Mercury: Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus. In the period of Jupiter: Sun, Moon—

->**The Results of Planetary Periods**<-

### Calculation of the Lord of the Year

Multiply the elapsed years by the constants 15, 31, 31, and 24. Add the factors 0, 24, and 23. Divide the result by 7; the remainder determines the Lord of the Year, starting from the Sun. || 1 ||

The method for determining the Lord of the Year <term>Varshapati; the planet ruling the specific astrological year</term> is described as follows:
For example, if the Shaka era year of birth is 1512 and the desired Shaka year for calculation is 1550, the difference is 38 elapsed years. Multiply these 38 elapsed years by the additive constants <term>Kshepaka; specific numerical values used to align astronomical cycles</term> 0, 15, 31, 31, and 24. This results in 47, 49, 57, 53, and 12. To this, add the factors 0, 24, and 23, which gives 48, 14, 20, 53, and 12. Dividing this by 7 leaves a remainder of 6, 14, and 21. This identifies the Lord of the Year.

Now, regarding the corrections: if the calculation has been adjusted for the equation of time, the equation of the center, or the ascensional difference <note>original: "Udayantara, Bhujaphala, Charaphala"</note>, it should be rendered free of these corrections to find the true Lord of the Year. It must be remembered that in this specific example, the corrections have already been applied. Therefore, one must subtract the three corrections to find the Lord of the Year. However, in relation to the planetary positions, one must apply the inverse correction to the Lord of the Year to arrive at the uncorrected value. || 1 ||

Multiply the total elapsed years by 207, then multiply the group of elapsed years by 14. Divide by 45 to find the result in Ghatikas <term>Ghatika; a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term>. Add 320 and divide by 800. Add the elapsed years to the days and divide by seven; the remainder indicates the Lord of the Year starting from Aries. || 2 ||

Alternatively, another method for bringing forth the Lord of the Year <term>Abdadhipa; another term for the Year Lord</term> is stated:
For example, the difference between the birth Shaka 1512 and the desired Shaka 1550 is 38 elapsed years. Multiply this 38 by the constant 207, which equals 7866. Then... <note>The text breaks off here; the catchword indicates the next page begins with "Phiragata-" (Then the elapsed...)</note>

For year 38, multiply the <term>kshepaka</term> <note>a constant additive factor used in Hindu calendrical calculations</note> by 14, resulting in 532. Dividing by 45, the quotient obtained is 11 <term>ghatis</term> and 49 <term>palas</term> <note>traditional units of time: 1 ghati is 24 minutes; 1 pala is 24 seconds</note>. Adding the constant 320 to this gives 320:11:49. This was added to the previously calculated 7866, resulting in 8186:11:49. Dividing by 800, the resulting days and time units are 10:13:58. Adding the 38 elapsed years results in 48:13:58. After subtracting multiples of 7 <note>to find the day of the week</note>, the Lord of the Year (Varshapati) is determined as 6:13:58. Since the Sun at the time of birth was adjusted for <term>chara</term> <note>ascensional difference</note> and <term>deshantara</term> <note>terrestrial longitude</note>, one must apply those corrections here in reverse relative to the planets to obtain the uncorrected Lord of the Year. || 2 ||

### Now, the Fruits of the Planets in the Houses

> **<term>Upajati Meter</term> — If the Sun, Mars, or Saturn are in the first house, they cause suffering from fever and loss of wealth; the Moon joined with malefic planets acts likewise. ||**
> **If joined with benefics and possessing a full body <note>a waxing or full moon</note>, it brings happiness. Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus bring wealth and gains from the state. || 50 ||**

Now the effects of the planets in the various houses are described: If the Sun, Mars, or Saturn—either individually or together—are in the <term>Lagna</term> <note>the Ascendant or First House</note>, they cause pain related to fever and loss of wealth. The <term>malefic-associated</term> Moon in the first house gives the same result. However, if the Moon is full and associated with benefics, it grants happiness; one should understand through intellect that a lesser moon gives less, and a greater moon gives more. Furthermore, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus in the first house grant wealth and royal pleasures according to the status of one's lineage. Mercury in the first house, whether alone or with benefics, brings joy. || 50 ||

> **<term>Upajati Meter</term> — The Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus in the second house grant the arrival of wealth and royal happiness. ||**
> **Malefics in the second house cause loss of wealth; Saturn specifically causes fear from the sovereign and the destruction of one's work. || 51 ||**

In the second house <note>the house of wealth</note>, the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus grant the arrival of riches and state-related comforts. A full Moon <term>associated with benefics</term> also gives this result. Conversely, a Moon <term>associated with malefic planets</term> in the second house causes loss of wealth. Saturn, in particular, causes fear of the King and the failure of one's undertakings. || 51 ||

> **<term>Vasantatilaka Meter</term> — Malefic planets in the third house grant wealth, righteousness, and gains from the state; if strong, they grant gains of land. Benefics there bring happiness, wealth, fame, and luxury; the Moon there surely brings incomparable joy. || 52 ||**

### Now, the Calculation of Monthly and Daily Commencements and Their Results.

->**In the Anushtubh Meter**<-
When the difference between the Sun of the month and the Sun of the nearest row is converted into minutes and divided by the Sun's daily motion, the resulting days and other units are added or subtracted. 1.
This is applied to the day of the week found in that row; if the Sun of the month is greater or lesser, the monthly commencement occurs on that day and time. The daily commencement is found in the same way. 2.

Now the method for <term>Monthly Commencement</term> <note>Varshaphal/Tajika system: the exact moment the Sun returns to the same degree it held at birth, adjusted for the month</note> and <term>Daily Commencement</term> is explained. The precise longitude of the Sun at the time of birth remains the same for every yearly commencement. To find the commencement of a specific month, subtract 1 from the number of the desired month and add that to the sign of the yearly commencement. For example, add 1 for the second month's commencement, 2 for the third, and so on, to find the <term>Sun of the Month</term> <note>original: "Masarka"</note>. Similarly, for the daily commencement, add 1 degree. 

Look in the almanac for the solar longitude nearest to this calculated Sun; that longitude is the <term>Row-Sun</term> <note>original: "Panktyarka"</note>. Find the difference between the Sun of the Month and the Row-Sun. Convert this difference into minutes of arc and divide by the daily motion. This yields three units: day, ghatis, and palas <note>traditional units of time: 1 ghati = 24 minutes</note>. Add or subtract this result from the day and time associated with the Row-Sun. If the Row-Sun was subtracted from the Sun of the Month, add the result; if the Sun of the Month was subtracted from the Row-Sun, subtract it. This gives the day, ghati, and pala of the Monthly Commencement. The Daily Commencement is understood in the same way. The logic for this was also provided in the commentary on the third verse of the first chapter of this system.

# Tajika Nilakanthi

<page-num>184</page-num>

->**Tajika Nilakanthi**<-

It is written, for example: the previously recorded Sun's longitude at the time of birth is 0s 18° 42' 31" <note>Signs, degrees, minutes, seconds</note>. In the year 1943 <note>Vikram Samvat calendar, approx. 1886 CE</note>, on the 12th day of the dark fortnight of the month of Vaishakha, a Saturday, at the desired time of 13 ghatis and 54 palas <note>approx. 5 hours and 34 minutes after sunrise</note>, the 38th annual return occurs. At this moment, the Sun's longitude is also 0s 18° 42' 31". To find the monthly return <term>Masapravesha: the moment the Sun enters the same degree of the next sign</term>, add one sign to this, resulting in 1s 18° 42' 31". This is called the **Monthly Sun** <term>Masarka</term>. 

For the second month, Jyeshtha, near the 12th of the dark fortnight, on Monday the 6th of the dark fortnight of Jyeshtha, the almanac <term>Panchang</term> shows the sunrise data. This is known as the weekday-base 2 | 0 | 0 <note>Monday at sunrise</note>. On this day, the Sun's longitude at sunrise is 1s 10° 35' 3" and its daily motion is 57' 27". This is the **Almanac Sun** <term>Panktyarka</term>. 

One must find the difference between these. Since the Monthly Sun (1s 18° 42' 31") is greater, subtract the Almanac Sun (1s 10° 35' 3") from it, leaving 0s 8° 7' 28". This equals 487 minutes and 28 seconds. The daily motion is 57' 27". Multiply 57 by 60 and add 27 to get 3447 (the motion-sum). Multiply the 487 minutes by 60 and add 28 to get 29248 (the minute-sum). Dividing the minute-sum 29248 by the motion-sum 3447 gives a result of 8 days. Multiply the remainder 1672 by 60 to get 100320; dividing by 3447 gives 29 ghatis. Multiply the remainder 357 by 60 to get 21420; dividing by the divisor gives 6 palas. 

This result of 8 days, 29 ghatis, and 6 palas must be added to or subtracted from the Almanac Sun's weekday-base of 2 | 0 | 0. Since the Almanac Sun was subtracted from the Monthly Sun, add the 8 days (reduced by 7 to leave a remainder of 1), 29 ghatis, and 6 palas to the weekday-base. This results in a weekday-base of 3 | 29 | 6. Thus, the second monthly return occurs on Tuesday <note>the 3rd day of the week</note>, the 14th of the dark fortnight of Jyeshtha, at 29 ghatis and 6 palas. The method for calculating the daily return <term>Dinapravesha</term> should be understood in the same way. An imaginary calculation with examples is written in the commentary of the third verse of the first chapter of this system. Both methods are proven. For specific understanding, it is written in various places. || 1 || : 2 ||

> **Translation of Verse:** At the time of the monthly return, one should also calculate the planets and the houses. In that monthly chart, there is the Lord of the Ascendant, the Lord of the Muntha <note>a mathematical point that progresses one sign per year</note>, and the Lord of the Birth chart. || 3 ||
> The Lord of the Triplicity, the Lords of the Day and Night, the Lords of the Sun and Moon signs, and the Lord of the Ascendant of the Annual Return—whichever among these is the strongest becomes the Lord of the Year <insert>or Month</insert> for the physical body. || 4 ||
