> The Lord of the Month is known by his aspect <note>The astrological gaze or influence</note>; from this, one should declare the good or bad results. Others have stated that the Lord of the Month-Ascendant is the Lord of the Month. || 5 ||

Just as there are five office-bearers <term>Panchadhikari: five planets with specific jurisdictional strengths</term> for the Lord of the Year at the time of the solar return, there are six office-bearers <term>Shadadhikari: six jurisdictional authorities</term> for the Lord of the Month at the time of the lunar return. These are as follows: First, calculate the precise positions of the planets at the moment of the month's commencement. 1. The Lord of the Month-Ascendant. 2. The Lord of the *Muntha* <note>A sensitive mathematical point in Tajika astrology that progresses one sign per year</note> for the month; this is found by multiplying the month number by 2 degrees and 30 minutes and adding it to the yearly *Muntha*. 3. The Lord of the Birth Sign. 4. The Lord of the Trine <term>Trirashisha: the ruler of a specific three-sign division</term>, determined as previously mentioned by the rule "The lords of the trines are Sun, Venus, Saturn, and Venus..." etc. 5. The Lord of the Sun's sign during the day, or the Lord of the Moon's sign during the night. 6. The Lord of the Year-Ascendant. These are the six office-bearers. Among these six, whichever is the strongest and casts an aspect on the Ascendant is the Lord of the Month. Some teachers consider only the Lord of the Month-Ascendant to be the Lord of the Month; according to their view, there is no need for the six office-bearers. The determination of the Lord is made as before. || 3 || 4 || 5 ||

### In the Anushtubh Meter — The wise have likewise spoken of the Lord of the Day and the Lord of the Day-Ascendant.

> The wise should declare the results for the Lord of the Month and the Lord of the Day in the same manner as the Lord of the Year. || 6 ||

The intelligent call the Lord of the Day-Ascendant at the time of the day's commencement the Lord of the Day. Its results—whether auspicious or inauspicious—should be declared by the wise based on the consideration of strength and weakness, just as one does for the Lord of the Year. || 6 ||

### In the Shardulavikridita Meter — If the Lord of the Ascendant's Navamsha is aspected by or joined with the Lord of the Ascendant...

> ...and if the Moon also views them both with a friendly aspect, then in that month there will be many kinds of happiness and freedom from disease. This result lasts as long as these conditions remain; one should declare the results by calculating the movements of the planets. || 7 ||

If the Lord of the *Navamsha* <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign</term> of the Month-Ascendant has a friendly aspect with the Lord of the Ascendant (or the Lord of the *Navamsha* where the Ascendant Lord is placed), or if they are both in the same position, and if the Moon views them both with a friendly aspect, then during that month, the person will experience various types of physical happiness and health for as long as this monthly influence lasts. In this way, one should declare the results by considering the strength, weakness, and aspects of the planets through mathematical calculation. || 7 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi
<note>original: "ताजिकनीलकण्ठी" - A classic 16th-century treatise on Tajika astrology, which incorporates Perso-Arabic influences into Sanskrit traditions.</note>

->**In the Shardulavikridita meter**<-

If the Lord of the Ascendant's degree and the Lord of the degree occupied by the Ascendant Lord view each other with a hostile aspect, and are also viewed by the Moon with a hostile aspect, they cause mental anguish and an increase in disease. If one of these two is in debilitation <note>original: "नीच" (Nicha) - the sign where a planet is at its weakest</note> or combust <note>original: "अस्तंगत" (Astangata) - rendered invisible by proximity to the Sun</note>, then happiness is only obtained after great suffering. If both are debilitated and combust, it signifies death. If there is an affliction <term>Arishta: a combination indicating misfortune or death</term> arising from the birth chart and the yearly chart, death occurs; otherwise, authorities say it results in suffering equal to death. || 8 ||

If the aforementioned Lord of the Ascendant's degree and the Lord of the degree occupied by the Ascendant Lord look at each other with a hostile aspect, or if the Moon also looks with a hostile aspect, they grant mental sorrow. If one among the Ascendant Lord and the Lord of the Ascendant Lord's degree is debilitated or combust, one finds happiness only after enduring great hardship. If both the Lord of the Ascendant's degree and the Lord of the Ascendant Lord's degree are debilitated and combust, and the Moon looks with a hostile aspect, they cause death. However, death occurs only if there is an affliction in both the birth and the yearly charts during that month; otherwise, the suffering is merely equivalent to death. Some teachers say that if the birth affliction occurs in a month but the yearly chart is clear, the death-like suffering occurs in the first half of the month; if the yearly chart has the affliction but the birth chart does not, the misfortune occurs in the latter half of the month. || 8 ||

->**In the Shardulavikridita meter**<-

If the Lord of a house's degree is viewed by or joined with the Lord of the degree occupied by that house's lord with a friendly aspect, and if the Moon also views them with a friendly aspect, then happiness related to that house <term>Bhava: an astrological house representing specific life areas like wealth or family</term> is attained. If the opposite occurs, the result is said to be reversed. The effects of debilitation and combustion should be deduced by the wise for all houses just as they were for the Ascendant. || 9 ||

The same logic applies to all houses: if the Lord of the Navamsha <note>original: "नवांश" - a 1/9th division of a sign used for fine-tuning predictions</note> of a house and the Lord of the degree occupied by that house's lord view each other with a friendly aspect, and the Moon also views them with a friendly aspect, then auspicious results related to that house are obtained in that month. If they view each other with a hostile aspect or are conjoined, and the Moon etc. views them with a hostile aspect, then suffering related to that house is certain. Similarly, if one or both are debilitated or combust, suffering is the result. The wise should apply this reasoning to all houses just as it was applied to the Ascendant. || 9 ||

->**In the Indravajra meter**<-

If the Lord of the Ascendant, the Lord of the Month, and the Lord of the degree occupied by the Year Lord are viewed by or conjoined with the Lord of their respective degrees with a friendly aspect, and are also supported by the Moon, it leads to happiness regarding that house; if not, it is inauspicious. || 10 ||

It explains that while severe planetary alignments can suggest death, the overall birth and yearly charts must confirm such a fate, otherwise the result is merely intense hardship.</summary>

# Tajika Neelakanthi

The <term>Shakri Dasha</term> <note>A specific system of planetary periods used in Tajika astrology</note> has its detailed explanation written previously in the section on period methodology. In the same manner, the sub-periods (Antardashas) should be calculated. According to these, the results should be predicted by discerning the strength or weakness of planets, such as their exaltation or debilitation. There are many types of periods, such as: 1. <term>Patyanshi</term>, 2. <term>Mudda</term>, 3. <term>Haddasha</term> according to the opinion of Devakirti, 4. <term>Tasir Dasha</term> with its many divisions, 5. <term>Nisarga Dasha</term>, 6. <term>Kalahora</term>, 7. Periods based on the Ascendant and other signs, 8. Bhogyansha Dasha, 9. The system of Mahadeva, 10. The system of Balabhadra, 11. The system of Gauri, and 12. The system of Rama. A detailed expansion of these is found in the <term>Tajika Muktavali</term> <note>A classical reference text on Tajika astrology</note>. Here, out of fear of making the book too voluminous, the Teacher has only described the primary fractional periods (Ansha Dasha).

The method for knowing the monthly and daily periods is as follows: between the <term>Muntha</term> <note>A sensitive mathematical point in a yearly chart that progresses one sign per year</note> and the <term>Monthly Ascendant</term>, whichever is stronger—the lords of the "Hadda" <note>Terms or bounds; specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note> in that sign (Mars, etc.) receive days equal to their respective degrees. For example, one should look at the precise <term>Yearly Ascendant</term> (Varshalagna). Following the rule "In Aries, the degrees are..." and so on, the lord of the Hadda is the first period lord, followed by the others in sequence. For instance, a sign has 30 degrees; multiplying these by 12 equals 360, which are the solar period days. Similarly, however many Hadda degrees there are, multiply them by 12 to get the period days for Mars and the other planets. For the first Hadda lord, multiply the elapsed degrees and the remaining degrees separately by 12 to find the elapsed and remaining period days. The elapsed days will come at the end of the period. This is the method of Hadda periods according to the opinion of Devakirti. The same method should be applied to the Daily Entrance (Dinapravesha). The Patyanshi period follows its own stated method. || 14 ||

> Verse (Anustubh meter)—Because of the non-inclusion of the Sun and Moon <note>original: "ravīndvorasamāveśān"</note>, others have said this is constant. The results of the periods and sub-periods are suitable for the year. || 15 ||

The opinion held by some that the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant are excluded is not authoritative. Since the results of the periods and sub-periods are as stated for the years, they must certainly occur within the period. Therefore, the Patyanshi and <term>Mudda</term> <note>A system of short-term planetary periods used for yearly and monthly predictions</note> are primary. || 15 ||

->**Tajika Nilakanthi**<-

In the Indra-vajra meter — **The Navamsha <note>The ninth-part division of a zodiac sign, crucial for determining the true strength of a planet</note> which is associated with or aspected by a benefic planet, or viewed with a friendly glance by the Moon, brings happiness related to that house. If the opposite occurs, it is said to bring sorrow. This same principle should be applied to all houses.** || 21 ||

Here, the consideration of the Navamsha is equal for all houses. Whichever house the specific degree of the house-cusp falls into in the Navamsha, if that Navamsha is occupied or aspected by benefic planets or friendly planets, and is also viewed by the Moon with a friendly aspect, then there will be happiness regarding that house. If it is occupied or aspected by malefic planets and viewed by the Moon with a hostile aspect, it causes distress regarding that house. This is the method for all houses. || 21 ||

In the Anushtubh meter — **The Navamsha of the sixth house, if joined by a benefic, causes disease; if joined by a malefic, it is auspicious. If the Navamsha of the twelfth house is joined or aspected by a benefic, there is "good expenditure"; if by a malefic, the expenditure is "bad."** || 22 ||

In certain houses, the interpretation differs. For example, if the Navamsha of the sixth house <note>The house of illness and enemies</note> is joined or aspected by benefic planets, it actually produces disease. If it is joined or aspected by malefic planets, it is auspicious, meaning it grants freedom from disease. Similarly, if the degree of the twelfth house <note>The house of loss and expenditure</note> is joined or aspected by a benefic, there is <term>Sadvayaya</term> <note>Virtuous spending, such as on charity, deities, or priests</note>. If it is joined or aspected by a malefic, expenditure occurs through theft, fines, or legal penalties. || 22 ||

In the Anushtubh meter — **The Navamsha of the seventh house, if joined or aspected by benefics, brings pleasure and happiness from one's own wife. With malefic planets, there is strife and sorrow; if placed between malefics, it indicates death.** || 23 ||

If the Navamsha of the seventh house <note>The house of marriage and partnerships</note> is joined or aspected by benefic planets, it brings pleasure and enjoyment with one's own wife. If joined or aspected by malefic planets, there will be quarrels with women and sorrow related to them. If that Navamsha is hemmed in between malefic planets, it indicates the death of the wife. If malefic planets are in the seventh house itself, there may be unions with other women; with many benefic planets, there is great happiness from women. || 23 ||

In the Anushtubh meter — **If the Navamsha is situated between benefics, there is abundant pleasure from women. With Jupiter, there is passion for one's own wife; with other planets, one may speak of passion for other women.** || 24 ||

If the Navamsha of the seventh house is hemmed in between benefic planets, there will be much sensual happiness. If it is joined or aspected by Jupiter, the person is devoted to his own wife; if influenced by other benefic planets, there may be passion for other women. || 24 ||

In the <term>Dinapravesha</term><note>The moment the Sun enters a new solar day in the annual chart.</note>, the Moon yields results corresponding to its specific state, such as "Travel" and others. Without a doubt, one should consider the same for the <term>Masapravesha</term><note>The commencement of a solar month.</note>. || 30 ||

<term>Anushtup Meter</term>--Discarding the signs, multiply the Moon's degrees by two and divide by five. The resulting quotient indicates the "elapsed" states; one should predict the results based on the "remaining" state to be experienced. || 31 ||

To determine the state, take the Moon's current longitude, discard the signs, and multiply the remaining degrees and minutes by two, then divide by five. The quotient represents the states already passed; the next state is the one currently being experienced, and its results should be declared. The twelve states are: **Travel, Destruction, Death, Victory, Laughter, Pleasure, Play, Sleep, Enjoyment, Fever, Trembling, and Stability.** The sequence begins with "Travel" for Aries, "Destruction" for Taurus, "Death" for Gemini, and so on, ending with "Stability" for Pisces. There are only twelve states, and here, five degrees are allotted to each state within a sign. Some practitioners calculate starting from "Travel" for all signs; that is an alternative school of thought. || 31 ||

<term>Bhujangaprayata Meter</term>--When the Lord of the Night <note>The Moon</note> is in the state of **Travel**, there is a journey; in **Destruction**, there is loss of wealth; in **Death**, there is fear of death; in **Victory**, there is triumph; and in **Laughter**, there is dalliance with beautiful women. || 32 ||

The results of the Moon's states are described: in the **Travel** state, the Moon indeed causes travel; in **Destruction**, loss of wealth; in **Death**, fear of death; in **Victory**, success; and in **Laughter**, it grants pleasure with women. || 32 ||

<term>Bhujangaprayata Meter</term>--In **Pleasure**, there is delight; **Play** is a giver of happiness; **Sleep** brings sleep, strife, and bodily pain; **Enjoyment** brings fear; **Fever** brings distress; **Trembling** brings loss; and **Stability** brings happiness. These are the results of the states in order. || 33 ||

In **Pleasure** (affection), there is joy; in **Play**, happiness; in **Sleep**, sleep, quarrels, and physical pain; in **Enjoyment**, fear; in **Fever**, agony; in **Trembling**, loss; and in **Stability**, happiness. These are the results of the states in sequence. They occur truly as described, but if the Moon is in the eighth house, it gives the opposite results. || 33 ||

# Now, the Consideration of Hunting.

<margin>From the *Bhuvanapradipa*:</margin> When Mars and Mercury are endowed with strength, they bring success in the King’s hunt; if they are devoid of strength, success is not achieved. A hunt in the water is predicted when the planets and signs designated as "watery" are strong; a hunt in the mountains is predicted when those designated as "mountainous" are strong. || 34 ||

If, from the Ascendant <note>The *Lagna*, or the zodiacal sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the query</note> of the day's commencement, Mars and Mercury are strong and situated in prescribed houses, then the King (the querent) will achieve his goal in hunting on that day. If these planets are weak, the hunt will not be successful. In the earlier chapter on terminology, the "water-dwelling" and "mountain-dwelling" signs and planets were described; the results should be declared according to them. For instance, if water-dwelling signs and planets are powerful, the hunt will involve aquatic creatures. If mountain-dwelling signs and planets are powerful, it will be a forest hunt. Specifically, the nature of the hunt corresponds to the nature of the daily Ascendant—such as being a water-dwelling sign—and the nature of the planets occupying or aspecting it. In mixed cases, the results should be declared as mixed. || 34 ||

<margin>From the *Anupama*:</margin> If the lords of the Ascendant and the Seventh House are situated in the Quadrants <note>The *Kendras*, or the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the pillars of a horoscope</note> but are weak, the hunt is said to bring distress. If those two are endowed with strength, the hunt yields auspicious results. || 35 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh House are in the Quadrants and are strong, the hunt will be pleasant; if these planets are weak, the hunt will cause hardship. || 35 ||

# Now, the Consideration of Food.

<margin>From the *Anupama*:</margin> The Lord of the Ascendant is the giver of food; the Lord of the Fourth House is the food itself. The Lord of the Seventh House is the hunger, and the Lord of the Tenth House should be considered the eater. || 36 ||

From the Ascendant of the day's commencement or the Ascendant of the query: the Lord of the First House represents the person providing the meal; the Lord of the Fourth House represents the food or grain fit for consumption; the Lord of the Seventh House represents the desire for food—that is, hunger or appetite; and the Lord of the Tenth House represents the person eating. One should predict the attainment or non-attainment of these things based on the strength or weakness of these planets. For example, if the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and placed in an auspicious house, the provider will give food with great devotion; if weak, they may provide it with anger or lack of faith. Similarly, if the Lord of the Fourth House is strong, one will receive excellent food; if weak, one may not receive food at all, or it may be of a contemptible quality. If the Lord of the Seventh House is strong, there will be a good appetite...

->Translation: If Saturn or Rahu is in the Ascendant, joined or aspected by the Sun, ||<-

If Saturn or Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered a shadow planet</note> is in the Ascendant and there is also an aspect from the Sun, then despite one's efforts, a meal will not be obtained that day; moreover, there may be a fear of weapons or injury. || 38 ||

->Translation: If the Ascendant is neither joined nor aspected by the Sun, ||<-
->Then fasting should be predicted, or a tasteless meal at night. || 39 ||<-

If the Ascendant is not joined or aspected by the Sun, then first of all, one may have to go without food entirely, or perhaps receive a tasteless, dry meal at night. || 39 ||

->Translation: If the Moon is in the tenth house, the food is hot; if Mars is in the fourth, it is cold. ||<-
->One should predict the flavor of the food based on the planet situated in the fourth house. || 40 ||<-

If, in the chart of the day or the inquiry, the Moon is in the tenth house, one receives (<term>Ushna</term> <note>Hot/Warm</note>) piping hot food. If Mars is in the tenth house, one receives (<term>Shita</term> <note>Cold</note>) cold or stale food. The flavor of the food should be determined by the planet in the fourth house: for example, the Sun indicates bitter, the Moon indicates salty, Mars indicates pungent/spicy, Mercury indicates mixed flavors, Jupiter indicates sweet, Venus indicates sour, and Saturn indicates (<term>Kashaya</term> <note>Astringent</note>) items like decoctions, fermented gruel, or vinegar that have been prepared many days prior. || 40 ||

->Translation: If Venus is in the fourth, the food is rich/oily; if Saturn, it is prepared with oil. ||<-
->If a planet is in its debilitation, the food is poor, tasteless, and poorly prepared. || 41 ||<-

### Salutations to the Lord Ganesha. <note>original: "Shri Ganeshaya Namah"; a traditional invocation to the elephant-headed deity of wisdom and beginnings.</note>

# Here Begins the Neelakanthi Prashna Tantra.

---

## Introduction

The works of the astrologer Neelakantha <note>original: "Neelakantha Daivagna"</note> follow a system of three "Tantras" <note>technical systems or treatises</note>. However, the third part, the *Prashna Tantra* <note>the system of Horary Astrology, or answering specific questions based on the time they are asked</note> composed by Neelakantha Acharya, has become difficult to obtain in the present day due to the passage of time and various other circumstances. After having already prepared, according to my humble intellect, the vernacular commentaries <note>original: "Bhasha-tika"</note> on the *Brihat Jataka* (concerning natal horoscopy) and the *Tajika Neelakanthi* (concerning annual solar returns) for the pleasure of the general public, I now present this accompanying volume on the subject of "Prashna" <note>Inquiry/Horary astrology</note>. This volume is essential for those who study the natal and annual systems.

Although it is often said in the aforementioned natal and annual texts that the same principles generally apply to horary inquiries—meaning the purpose of a horary text is somewhat covered by them—nevertheless, following the tradition of ancient teachers and for the sake of clarity, many texts have followed the school of Neelakantha, thus earning the name *Neelakanthi*. I am now writing this vernacular commentary on this miraculous horary text to the best of my ability. May the virtuous accept it with their natural kindness.

The Sanskrit sciences are peerless; there is no object or concept devoid of them. That which is not found within them does not exist in the fourteen realms <note>referring to the entire cosmos in Hindu cosmology</note>. However, the primary reason for the decline of knowledge in India <note>original: "Bharatvarsha"</note> is that those who possess unique knowledge, arts, medicinal formulas, or miraculous mantras become envious when it comes to teaching others and do not reveal their secrets. Upon their death, that knowledge vanishes with them; how then can knowledge flourish? Considering this, I have openly revealed the various symbols and secrets of the science of astrology <note>original: "Jyotish-shastra"</note> within the *Brihat Jataka* and all three Tantras of the *Neelakanthi*.

> ->Written in the Anushtup meter:<-
> By the will of Fate, and the desire for good or evil results,
> Every mortal is inevitably brought into the range of the Astrologer. || 1 ||
> <note>original: "Daivagnasya hi daivena sadasatphalavanchaya..."</note>

Past actions are called "Fate" <note>original: "Daiva"</note>. Just as a person has performed actions, so too must they experience the results...

If the practitioner <note>original: "daivajña" - one who knows the divine or fate</note> desires to know the auspicious or inauspicious results of an action, they can explain it entirely through the movement of the planets <note>original: "grahachāra" - planetary transit</note>. || 1 ||

->Having heard the decisive words regarding queries, sounds, and omens from Vishnu, Brahma revealed them to the world through the science of light <note>original: "jyotiṣa" - astrology/astronomy</note>. || 2 ||<-

Vasantatilaka Meter—Therefore, a King <note>the term "King" is used here as a general example for any seeker</note> should approach in the morning with flowers, gems, and fruits in his right hand. After offering salutations and facing East, he should appoint the astrologers. He should gather those beneficial calculators <note>original: "gaṇaka" - mathematicians or astrologers</note> who are experts in the branch of astrology concerning time <note>original: "horā" - natal or horary astrology</note> and ask his question clearly and only once. || 3 ||

Therefore, the seeker—taking auspicious items like flowers, jewels, and fruits in the right hand—should respectfully request the astrologer for a reading in the morning. Then, having gathered the well-wishing calculators who understand the limbs of the *Hora* scriptures, he should ask his question in few words and only once. || 3 ||

Arya Meter—The one who calculates the ten-fold planetary positions and examines the birth chart <note>original: "jātaka"</note> in its entirety—
->When such a person speaks of good or evil fortune, their words never prove false. || 4 ||<-

After the question is asked, the calculator who examines the ten types of planetary strengths, positions, and the entire system of natal astrology before pronouncing the result, will find that his speech is never in error. || 4 ||

### First, the Examination of the Seeker

Arya Meter—The astrologer must first examine the strength of the Ascendant <note>original: "lagna" - the rising sign at the moment of the query</note> to determine if the seeker is honest or deceitful.
->The astrologer should then speak the results, for the divine destiny residing in the seeker's heart will manifest through the astrologer's intuition. || 1 ||<-

Whether the seeker's mind is straightforward or crooked must first be tested by the astrologer using the strength of the Ascendant before giving a prediction. The divine fruit of past actions <note>original: "karmapāka"</note> residing in the seeker's heart will be revealed to the astrologer through this focused consideration. || 1 ||

Arya—If the Moon is in the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>, Saturn is in a Cardinal house <term>Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term>, and Mercury is eclipsed by the Sun's rays;

Furthermore, if the Ascendant and the seventh house are under the gaze of auspicious planets, or if the Moon is viewed by Mercury and Jupiter, the querent should be known as simple-hearted and honest.

If Mercury or Jupiter looks upon the Lord of the Seventh house <term>Saptamesha</term> with the gaze of an enemy, the querent is deceptive. If they look upon it with the gaze of a friend, the querent should be known as a simple-hearted person.

Arya—Having thoroughly considered the Ascendant, one should speak on the question once, according to the scriptures.
->He who speaks on a single matter, his words shall not prove false.<-

An astrologer <term>Jyotishi</term>, after carefully considering the Ascendant, should answer a few questions according to the commands of the scriptures. The one who speaks on a single question, his speech does not become false; that is to say, many questions asked at once in the Ascendant do not yield true answers.

### Now, the States of the Planets

<term>Anu.</term> <note>original: "Anushtubh" - a poetic meter</note>—Radiant, Distressed, Joyful, Healthy, Sleeping, Oppressed, Robbed, Diminished, Strong, and Greatly Powerful. || 1 ||

The ten classifications of the planets are named Radiant <note>Dipta</note>, Distressed <note>Deena</note>, Joyful <note>Mudita</note>, Healthy <note>Svastha</note>, Sleeping <note>Supta</note>, Oppressed <note>Pidita</note>, Robbed <note>Mushita</note>, Diminished <note>Parihina</note>, Strong <note>Suvirya</note>, and Greatly Powerful <note>Adhivirya</note>. These are the ten varieties. || 1 ||

<term>Anu.</term>—A planet in its sign of exaltation is called Radiant; in its sign of debilitation, it is proclaimed Distressed. In a friend's house, it is Joyful; in its own house, it is Healthy. || 2 ||
Situated in an enemy's house, it is Sleeping; defeated by another, it is Oppressed. Moving toward debilitation, it is Diminished; a planet that is combust <note>hidden by the Sun's rays</note> is Robbed. || 3 ||
The wise call a planet Strong when it is moving toward its exaltation; it is declared Greatly Powerful when it possesses many rays and occupies auspicious divisional charts. || 4 ||

A planet in its highest exaltation is Radiant; in its lowest debilitation, Distressed; in a friend's sign, Joyful; in its own sign, Healthy; in an enemy's sign, Sleeping; attacked by another malefic planet, Oppressed; desiring debilitation <note>approaching its sign of fall</note>, Diminished; set or combust, Robbed; desiring exaltation <note>approaching its highest point</note>, Strong; and when it has many rays and a high count of auspicious divisions <note>shubha-varga</note>, it is called Greatly Powerful. || 2 || 3 || 4 ||

<term>Anu.</term>—In the Radiant state, there is success in undertakings; in the Distressed state, the arrival of sorrow. In the Healthy state, there is fame and wealth; in the Joyful state, great happiness. || 5 || In the Sleeping state, there is fear of enemies and sorrow; in the Oppressed state, loss of wealth. In the Robbed and Diminished states, there is destruction of work and depletion of resources. || 6 || Acquisition of elephants, horses, and gold occurs in the Strong state, along with the wealth of gems. In the Greatly Powerful state, one attains kingdom, religious merit, and the company of friends and wealth. || 7 ||

Describing the fruits of these states: a planet in the Radiant state brings success to tasks; in the Distressed state, the onset of grief; in the Healthy state, fame and prosperity; in the Joyful state, great...

In the state of *Ananda* <note>Joyful</note>, there is happiness; in *Supta* <note>Asleep</note>, there is fear of enemies and sorrow; in *Pidita* <note>Afflicted</note>, there is loss of wealth; in *Mushita* <note>Robbed</note> and *Parihina* <note>Diminished</note>, there is destruction of work and loss of wealth; in *Suvirya* <note>Great Prowess</note>, there is the acquisition of elephants, horses, gold, and gems; in *Adhivirya* <note>Supreme Prowess</note>, there is the gain of a kingdom and the meeting of friends and wealth. || 5 || 6 || 7 ||

### Now, the Nature of the Planets.

-> Translation: The Sun is the East, the quality of Purity, the King, and the Father; he is of the Warrior caste, the Summer season, reddish in color, and restless. <-

The Sun's forms and qualities are: Lord of the East, the quality of *Sattva* <note>Purity/Goodness</note>, the status of a King, the representation of the Father, the *Kshatriya* <note>Warrior</note> caste, the Summer season, a blood-red complexion, a restless nature, eyes like the color of honey, a temperament dominated by *Pitta* <note>Bile/Fire</note>, a courageous warrior, and fine, thin hair. || 1 ||

The Moon's forms and qualities are: The *Kapha* <note>Phlegm/Water</note> temperament, the Rainy season, a soft body, the representation of the Mother, the element of Water, a fair complexion, the quality of *Sattva* <note>Purity</note>, the giver of life, the *Vaishya* <note>Merchant</note> caste, a changeable or moving nature, a round shape, Lord of the Northwest direction, and lovely eyes. || 2 ||

# Tajika Neelakanthi

<page-num>204</page-num>

The quality of goodness <note>Sattva guna</note>, yellow color, cool temperament, phlegmatic nature, a tall body, knowledge of sacred chants <note>mantras</note>, the priestly class <note>Brahmin caste</note>, masculine, a fondness for sweets, lord of the Northeast direction, phlegmatic constitution, and eyes the color of honey—these are the qualities of **Jupiter**. || 5 ||

> *Translation—Venus is peaceful, a priest, dressed in feminine attire, a counselor, mobile, white, ruling the Southeast, phlegmatic, sour, with dark curly hair.* || 6 ||

A peaceful temperament, priestly class, wearing feminine attire, a counselor <note>minister</note>, of a mobile nature, white color, lord of the Southeast direction, phlegmatic constitution, sour taste, and dark, curly hair—these are the qualities of **Venus**. || 6 ||

> *Black, of the quality of darkness, thin, old, eunuch, root-based, low-born, lazy, cold, windy, cruel, Western, talkative—this is Saturn.* || 7 ||

Black color, the quality of darkness <note>Tamas guna</note>, a thin body, old age, neuter, associated with roots, of the lowest social standing, lazy, lord of the winter season, of a windy constitution, cruel temperament, lord of the West, and talkative—these are the forms and qualities of **Saturn**. || 7 ||

> *Rahu is elemental, Ketu is root-based, the rest is like Saturn; this should be considered from the Lord of the Ascendant or the strongest planet in the center.* || 8 ||

**Rahu** is primarily elemental <note>Dhatu</note>, wearing matted hair, and associated with roots; his remaining qualities should be known as equal to Saturn. **Ketu** should also be known in this same way. One should describe the characteristics in a query based on the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, the Lord of the Ascendant, or whichever planet is strongest in the cardinal houses <note>Kendras</note>. The specific qualities and the attributes of the zodiac signs have been clearly written with diagrams in the first section on terminology. || 8 ||

Happiness, lifespan, stage of life, caste, freedom from disease, physical marks, qualities, hair, physical shape, form, and color—these many considerations are to be examined by the wise in the **First House** <note>Lagna Bhava</note>. || 1 ||

Pearls, rubies, and other gems; metals such as gold; wealth, clothing, matters concerning horses, and knowledge related to travel—all these matters should be considered from the second <term>Bhava</term> <note>The 'House' or state of being in a horoscope</note>. || 2 ||

**The learned should properly observe sisters, brothers, servants, and those who perform service from the house of 'Duschikya'. || 3 ||**

**The wise should look to 'Patala' for gardens, threshing floors, fields, great medicinal herbs, and treasures, as well as entry into holes or caves. || 4 ||**
<note>original: "पाताल" (Patala) — meaning the 'underworld' or 'bottom,' used here as a name for the Fourth House, which represents the lowest point of the zodiac chart.</note>

Step-wells, threshing floors, farming, medicines, grains, treasures (excellent items or wealth buried underground), and entry into crevices, caves, or tunnels—all these are to be seen from the <term>Fourth Bhava</term>. || 4 ||

Fear of thieves, enemies, warfare, as well as donkeys, camels, cruel actions, the maternal side of the family, illness, and attendants—the consideration of these should be done from the <term>Sixth House</term>. || 6 ||

**The wise should look to the 'House of the Wife' for commerce, transactions, disputes with others, coming and going, and the spouse. || 7 ||**

Trade, the profession of a merchant, disputes or treaties with others, as well as departures, arrivals, and the wife—these considerations are to be made from the <term>Seventh Bhava</term>. || 7 ||

**In the crossing of rivers, in the hardships of the road, in fortresses, and in the danger of weapons; in loss, in wickedness, in battle, in disease, and in vulnerabilities—one should examine the 'Chidra'. || 8 ||**
<note>original: "छिद्र" (Chidra) — meaning a hole, gap, or vulnerability; a traditional name for the Eighth House.</note>

### From the Shatpanchashika
<note>A classical 6th-century work on horary astrology by Prithuyashas</note>

<insert>Indravajra meter</insert>—Whichever house is aspected by or occupied by its own lord or by benefic planets, that house will flourish.
> Conversely, by malefic planets, the destruction of that house is to be predicted for those inquiring or from the birth chart. || 13 ||

Whichever house is joined with or aspected <note>The "aspect" (drishti) refers to the mathematical glance or influence one planet has over another or a specific house</note> by its own lord or by benefic planets, there is an increase in the fruits of those specific houses. Those joined with or aspected by malefic planets suffer loss. This consideration should be applied everywhere, both in "Prashna" <note>Horary astrology, where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</note> and in "Janma" <note>Natal astrology, based on the moment of birth</note>. || 13 ||

### Samarasimha

> <term>Arya meter</term>—When a question is asked, "Tell me, when will this specific task be accomplished?" one should look at the Ascendant, the Lord of the Ascendant, the House of the Task <note>The specific house related to the question, e.g., the 10th for career</note>, and the Lord of the Task. || 22 ||
> If the Lord of the Task is situated in the Ascendant and aspects the Lord of the Ascendant, the matter will be realized. If the Lord of the Ascendant is situated elsewhere, it will not happen quickly. || 23 ||

When someone asks when a specific work will be done, if in that query the Lord of the Task aspects the House of the Task, or the Lord of the Ascendant aspects the Ascendant, say that the work will be done quickly. If the Lord of the Task is in the Ascendant and aspects the Lord of the Ascendant, the work will also be fast. If the Lord of the Ascendant is elsewhere, it will not be immediate. || 22 || 23 ||

> When the Moon aspects the Ascendant, or when the Moon aspects the Lord of the Ascendant, or when there is a connection between the Ascendant and the Task, then success is achieved. || 24 ||
> If the Lord of the Ascendant does not aspect the Lord of the Task or the Ascendant, the destruction of the task is predicted; if the Ascendant is "dead" <note>likely referring to a void-of-course moon or a severely afflicted first house</note>, nothing should be predicted. || 25 ||

## On the General Consideration of the Houses

*In the Anustubh meter:*
The Moon is everywhere like the seed; the Ascendant is like the flower. The Degree <note>Amsha</note> is like the fruit, and the House <note>Bhava</note> is like the taste of that fruit. || 35 ||

In this astrological consideration, the Moon is compared to a seed, the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> to a flower, the specific degree to the resulting fruit, and the House itself to the flavor or experience of that fruit. || 35 ||

*In the Arya meter:*
Take the minutes of the rising sign at the time of the query, multiply them by the fingers of the shadow... <note>The text breaks off here, describing a calculation involving a gnomon shadow</note> || 36 ||

### Having calculated thus as before, the rising of a benefic planet occurs.
### The attainment of the objective should be declared to the inquirer through these planets. || 37 ||

In all inquiries regarding gains and other matters, to determine the timing, one should take the total minutes <note>original: "lipta-pinda"; the sum of the degrees and minutes of the rising sign converted into minutes</note> of the current Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the question</term>. Multiply this by the number of inches <note>original: "angulas"</note> of a twelve-inch shadow cast at that moment, and divide the result by fourteen. The remainder indicates the zodiac sign starting from Aries. If that remainder corresponds to the sign of a benefic planet <note>Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, or a waxing Moon</note>, the work will be accomplished; if it is the sign of a malefic planet <note>Sun, Mars, Saturn, or Rahu/Ketu</note>, loss of the work should be predicted. || 36 || 37 ||

### The multipliers for the planets should be known by the astrologer as: five (5), twenty-one (21), fourteen (14), nine (9), eight (8), three (3), and eleven (11), starting from the Sun. || 38 ||
### Divided by the sum of the multipliers, and then subtracted by the individual multipliers of the Sun and others; the planet whose multiplier cannot be further subtracted determines the time. || 39 ||

The multipliers for the planets are: Sun 5, Moon 21, Mars 14, Mercury 9, Jupiter 8, Venus 3, and Saturn 11. Their sum is 71. One should take the previously mentioned product (the minutes of the Ascendant multiplied by the shadow inches) and divide it by 71. From the remainder, subtract the individual multipliers of the planets one by one, starting with the Sun. Continue subtracting as long as possible. The planet whose multiplier is larger than the remaining value is the one used to determine the time, as explained next. || 38 || 39 ||

### If the remainder belongs to Mars or the Sun, it means days; for Venus or the Moon, fortnights; for Jupiter, months; for Mercury, seasons; and for Saturn, years. || 40 ||
### In matters of conception, attainment of wealth, departures and arrivals, defeat or victory, or the destruction of enemies, one should state the fixed time of the inquiry. || 41 ||

In order: if the multiplier of the Sun or Mars remains, the time is that many days; for Venus or the Moon, it is fortnights <note>original: "paksha"; a 15-day lunar half-month</note>; for Jupiter, months; for Mercury, seasons <note>a two-month period</note>; and for Saturn, years. Whether the question concerns the birth of a child after conception, the acquisition of wealth, going or coming, victory or defeat, or the destruction of an enemy, the timing should be determined and spoken with certainty in this manner. || 40 || 41 ||

### The groups of letters A, Ka, Cha, Ta, Ta, Pa, Ya, and Sha belong to the Sun, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Moon respectively. By the first letters produced from these... || 42 ||
Having known the absorption from that...

> Having understood the auspicious and inauspicious, one should speak. Based on the initial, middle, and final letters of the question, an odd-numbered sign is determined. || 43 || If the ascendant <note>Lagna: the rising sign at the time of inquiry</note> is unknown, one should speak based on the inquiry. For Mars, Mercury, and Jupiter, there are two signs; for Venus and Saturn, there are many; for the Sun and Moon, there is only one sign. || 44 || Therefore, one should first declare all good and bad results at the time of the inquiry. This should be considered when there are many questions, through the knowledge of time. || 45 ||

The lord of the 'A' group <note>Varga: phonetic groupings of the Sanskrit alphabet</note> is the Sun; of the 'Ka' group is Mars; of the 'Cha' group is Venus; of the 'Ta' group is Mercury; of the 'Ta' (dental) group is Jupiter; of the 'Pa' group is Saturn; of the 'Ya' group is the Moon; and of the 'Sha' group is also the Moon. These are the lords of the phonetic groups. Where the knowledge of the ascendant is not possible, or where many questions (such as 3 or 6) are asked during the same ascendant, one should derive the ascendant from the group-lord in this manner: the lord of the group containing the first letter of the question should be known as the ascendant sign. From that ascendant, one should speak of the auspicious or inauspicious results by considering the yogas <note>astrological combinations</note> as previously described. Each planet has two signs; among these, one should choose the odd-numbered sign <note>e.g., Aries instead of Scorpio for Mars</note>. For the Moon, there is only one sign, so that alone is known. Where there are many questions, the ascendant for the first question is known by the first letter of the inquiry, and for the second, by the final letter. Furthermore, if the ascendant signs of Mars, Mercury, or Jupiter are identified, know that there are two questions; from Venus and Saturn, many; and because the Sun and Moon have only one sign, know there is only one question. In the case of many questions, one should speak of all auspicious and inauspicious results from the ascendant in this manner, and by considering the qualities of the group-lord planet according to the previously stated order. || 42 || || 43 || || 44 || || 45 ||

->On the Knowledge of the Question<-

> If the lord of the ascendant is in its own division <note>Amsha: a divisional portion of a sign</note>, or in the ascendant, or in a trine <note>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, and looks upon its own division, it indicates a concern regarding minerals or inanimate objects. If it is in the division of another, it indicates a concern regarding living beings. If it has reached the highest division, it indicates a concern regarding roots or plants. || 46 ||

In a "closed fist" or "silent" question <note>Mooka-Prashna: where the querent does not reveal their question</note>, if the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is in its own division, or in the ascendant, or in a trine (9th or 5th houses), or in any other place but looks at the ascendant while being in its own division, then the concern is about <term>Dhatu-chinta</term> <note>inanimate objects, minerals, or metals</note>. If it is in the division of an enemy or an equal and looks at the ascendant or the Moon, it is <term>Jiva-chinta</term> <note>living beings, humans, or animals</note>. And if it sits in the division of another and looks at the planets of that division, it is <term>Mula-chinta</term> <note>roots, plants, or botanical matters</note>.

## Including the Vernacular Commentary

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnēsha: the planet ruling the rising sign</note> or the Moon are in the final portion of a sign, or if any planet in the Ascendant is in its final portion, then the question relates to "Root" <note>Mula: botanical or vegetable matter</note> substances. || 46 ||

-> Mineral, Root, and Life are determined by the odd signs; in even signs, it is the reverse. The specific division of the Ascendant determines the object; this is a summary of the many detailed variations. || 47 || <-

If an odd-numbered zodiac sign is rising, the first ninth-part <term>Navamsha: a 3°20' subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> indicates Mineral <note>Dhatu: metals or minerals</note>, the second indicates Root, the third indicates Life <note>Jiva: humans or animals</note>, the fourth Mineral, the fifth Root, the sixth Life, the seventh Mineral, the eighth Root, and the ninth Life. -> If the Sun and Mars are strong and positioned in the Angles, they signify Minerals in a query. Mercury and Saturn signify Roots; the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus are known to signify Life. || 48 || <-

If the Sun and Mars are powerful and located in the "Angles" <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope</term>, the question is about Minerals. If Mercury or Saturn are so placed, it is about Roots. If the Moon, Jupiter, or Venus are present, one should understand the query concerns Living Beings. || 48 ||

-> When Aries, Scorpio, or Leo are rising and joined or aspected by Mars or the Sun, speak of Minerals. With Gemini, Aquarius, or Virgo as the Ascendant, joined by Mercury or Saturn, it is Roots. With Taurus, Libra, Leo, Pisces, Sagittarius, or Cancer, joined or aspected by the Moon, Jupiter, or Venus, Life is to be indicated. || 49-50 || <-

If the Ascendant is Aries, Scorpio, or Leo (1, 8, 5) and is occupied or aspected <note>Drishti: the "glance" or astrological influence of one planet upon another</note> by Mars or the Sun, the question is about Minerals. If the signs are Gemini, Aquarius, or Virgo (3, 11, 6) and occupied by Mercury or Saturn, it is about Roots. If the signs are Taurus, Libra, Leo, Pisces, Sagittarius, or Cancer (2, 7, 5, 12, 9, 4) and occupied or aspected by the Moon, Jupiter, or Venus, the question concerns Living Beings. || 49 || 50 ||

## On Queries Regarding the First House (The Ascendant)

> When a person asks, "What was my past, what is my present, and what will be my future?" one must investigate the strength of the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> <note>the planet ruling the rising sign</note> or the Moon. If these lack strength... || 1 || ...then one must look to the strength of the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>the ninth divisional chart, used for fine-tuning strength</note>, as well as the aspects and conjunctions of benefic planets. In all matters, if there is an abundance of strength, one should predict auspiciousness for the petitioner; if the opposite is true, the result is inauspicious. || 2 ||

If someone asks about their past or future—what has happened or what will happen—one must examine the strength of the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> <note>Lagnesha</note> and the Moon in this query. If these are not powerful, then examine the strength of the <term>Navamsha</term>. If there is an excess of strength and conjunctions or aspects from benefic planets, one should declare success in all the petitioner's works. If the situation is reversed, one should declare it inauspicious. || 1 || 2 ||

> One should speak of the past based on the planet with which the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> forms a <term>Musaripha</term> <note>a Persian-derived astrological aspect where a faster planet passes a slower one</note>. From the planet it is joined with, speak of the present; and from the planet that aspects it, speak of the future. || 3 ||

One should describe the past according to which planet the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> forms a <term>Musaripha</term> with. For example, if a <term>Musaripha</term> has occurred and turned into an <term>Isarapha</term> <note>separation of planets</note>, the work is already finished. If there is an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>applying aspect/conjunction</note>, say that the work is currently happening. Future events should be predicted through aspects. The various types of <term>Itthashala</term> have been explained previously. || 3 ||

> If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant, joined with or aspected by benefics, then the petitioner's anxieties and bodily ailments are destroyed. || 4 ||

If the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> is situated in the first house and is conjoined with or aspected by auspicious planets, then the petitioner's mental distress and all physical ailments will be cured. || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</note> is a malefic <note>a "bad" planet like Mars or Saturn</note>, then there will be quarrels, disease, and loss of wealth. ## Now, the Results of the Second House.

In an inquiry regarding the gain of wealth, if the Lord of the Ascendant forms an *Itthashala* <term>Itthashala: a specific planetary aspect in Tajika astrology indicating the fulfillment of a desire</term> with the Lord of the Moon-sign or the Lord of the Second House <note>Dhananatha: the planet ruling the house of wealth</note>, and if they are joined or aspected by benefics, wealth will be gained. || 6 ||
In a question about gaining wealth, if the Lord of the Ascendant forms an *Itthashala* with the Moon's sign or the Lord of the Second House, and is also associated with or viewed by benefic planets, wealth will be obtained. || 6 ||

If malefic planets are placed in the Second House, wealth is gained only after a long time, and other misfortunes may occur. If the Lord of the Second House or the Lord of the Ascendant forms a *Muthashila* <term>Muthashila: a synonym for Itthashala, indicating a favorable configuration</term> with a malefic, the querent <note>Prashta: the person asking the astrological question</note> may face great suffering or even death. || 7 ||
If malefic planets are in the house of wealth, profit comes after a long delay and some inauspiciousness occurs. If the Lord of Wealth or the Lord of the Ascendant forms an *Itthashala* with a malefic, the querent suffers harm. || 7 ||

As the Lord of Wealth forms an *Itthashala* with the slower-moving planet among the various houses—such as the First (Self), Second (Wealth), or Third (Siblings)—the querent will gain wealth through the person or matter related to that specific house. || 8 ||
The Lord of Wealth, being slower-moving, indicates that wealth will be gained through the people associated with whichever house (Body, Wealth, Siblings, etc.) it forms an *Itthashala* with. || 8 ||

<term>Anushtup: a specific poetic meter consisting of 32 syllables</term>—In an inquiry, if the Lord of the Fourth House is situated in the fourth or aspects it, or if the Moon is there, one should say that wealth is certainly present in that place. || 9 ||
In cases of doubt regarding buried or stolen wealth, if the Lord of the Fourth is in the Fourth House, or aspects it, or if the Moon is in the Fourth, one must say that the wealth is definitely located there. || 9 ||

If the Lord of Wealth is in the Second or the Fourth House, there is much wealth there. However, if a malefic is in the Fourth House, the wealth situated there will not be obtained quickly. || 10 ||

# Tajika Neelakanthi
<note>The title refers to a seminal 16th-century Sanskrit treatise on Tajika astrology, a system influenced by Perso-Arabic traditions, written by Neelakantha.</note>

If there is an *Itthashala* <note>original: "इत्थशाल" (Itthashala) — a planetary aspect in Tajika astrology where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of an event</note> between the Lord of the Tenth House and the Lord of the Ascendant, the thief will be caught by the royal family <note>or government authorities</note>. If the Lords of the Third and Ninth Houses form an *Itthashala* with the Lord of the Seventh House, the thief will be caught in another country. || 16.5 ||

-> If the Moon is in the Ascendant and forms an *Itthashala* with a benefic planet, the lost wealth will be recovered. If the Moon is in the Ascendant and is viewed with a friendly aspect by the Sun or a benefic planet, the same result should be predicted. || 17 || <-

If the Moon is in the Ascendant or the Tenth House and forms an *Itthashala* with a benefic planet, the lost wealth is found. If the Sun and benefic planets look upon the Moon situated in the Ascendant with a "friendly sight" <note>a specific planetary aspect</note>, then also one should predict the recovery of the wealth. || 17 ||

## Commentary in the Common Tongue

The direction or sub-direction associated with the zodiac sign <note>the sign occupied by the planet representing the lost object</note>, or the specific element of that sign—whether Fire, Earth, Air, or Water—indicates the location where the lost property is currently situated. || 22 ||

-> **On the Recovery of Lost or Stolen Wealth** <-

In a query regarding the recovery of lost or stolen wealth, the Seventh House represents the thief, the Fourth House represents the recovery of the goods, the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the rising sign at the time of the query</term> represents the property itself, and the Moon represents the owner of the wealth. || 23 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Seventh House and forms a *Muthashila* <term>an aspect in Perso-Arabic astrology where a faster planet approaches a slower one</term> with the Lord of the Seventh House, the lost property will be recovered. If the Lord of the Eighth House is positioned in the Ascendant, the thief will return the wealth of his own accord. || 24 ||

If the Lord of the Second House <note>the house of wealth</note> is within the rays of the Sun or is combust <term>hidden by the Sun's brightness</term>, the thief will be caught. If there is an *Itthashala* <term>a completed favorable aspect</term> between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Tenth House, the thief will be found along with the money. If the Lord of the Ascendant does not cast an eye <note>aspect</note> upon the Seventh House, the thief will return with the wealth. || 25 ||

If the Lord of the Seventh House is "burnt" <note>combust</note> or within the rays of the Sun, the thief is captured. If the Lord of the Seventh House forms an *Itthashala* with the Lord of the Ascendant, the thief will personally return the money out of fear of the King <note>the legal authorities</note>. || 26 ||

If there is no aspect between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh House, and the Lord of the Ascendant is "weak in its arts" <term>Vikala; lacking strength or dignity</term>, then the thief will hand over the stolen goods to the Royal Court with his own hands. || 27 ||

If there is a connection between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Midheaven <note>Tenth House</note>, the stolen goods are recovered after reaching the Royal Court. The Eighth House represents the thief's wealth; if the Lord of Wealth is there or in the Seventh House, the property is not recovered. || 28 ||

### Knowledge of the Thief's Location

> In a query regarding the thief's location, if the Sun and Moon aspect the Ascendant, the thief is within the querent's own house.
> If only one of these aspects the Ascendant, he lives near the house. || 30 ||

In a question of "Where is the thief?", if the Sun and Moon both aspect the Ascendant, the thief is in the house of the <term>querent</term> <note>praṣṭā: the person asking the question</note>. If only one of them aspects it, the thief lives in the neighborhood. || 30 ||

> If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant and joined with the Lord of the Seventh, the thief is in the house.
> If the Lord of the Seventh is in the Twelfth or Third house, this thief is one's own servant. || 31 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the first house joined with the Lord of the Seventh <note>the house of the thief</note>, the thief stays in the querent's house. If the Lord of the Seventh is in the Twelfth or Third house, the thief is the querent's own servant. || 31 ||

> If the Lord of the Seventh is in its sign of exaltation or its own house, the thief is well-known. The first, tenth, and seventh houses should be examined in order regarding their exaltation, etc. || 32 || Whichever planet is strong should be known as the strength of the thief. Whichever planet among the Ascendant and others is strong in its exaltation, etc., the thief is of that caste/type. Without such a yoga, the strength of the Lord of the Seventh alone should be taken. || 33 ||

If the Lord of the Seventh is exalted or in its own sign, one should say the thief is famous. One must examine the 1st, 10th, and 7th houses in sequence; whichever is strongest (in exaltation, etc.) represents the thief's power. The thief will be of the caste or nature of that strongest planet, or that planet will assist the thief. If these specific combinations are not present, then only the strength of the Lord of the Seventh <note>Dyūnēśa</note> should be considered. || 32 || 33 ||

### On Buying and Selling from Other Texts

The buyer is known by the lord of the first house (Ascendant), and the seller is remembered as the lord of the second house. When the question is: "Should I purchase this item?"
If the Ascendant and its lord are strong, the item should be purchased. In such a case, the querent <note>The person asking the astrological question</note> will certainly gain profit from that purchase.

When the question is: "I am selling this item, [what will be the result]?"
If the eleventh house <note>The house of gains</note> or its lord is strong, the item should be sold. In this case, there will be profit; otherwise, there will be loss.

Thus ends the description of the third house in the commentary on the *Prashna Tantra* composed by Shrimad Mahidhara.

### Now, Inquiries Regarding the Fifth House.

> If a questioner asks, "Will this woman of mine have offspring or not?" If the questioner asks whether his wife will give birth or not, and the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the Fifth House are in a mutual <term>Itthashala</term> yoga, then there will be progeny. || 1 ||

> If the Lord of the Fifth is in the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the Fifth, it should be said to happen very quickly; if there is a <term>Nakta Yoga</term>, it will happen with delay. || 2 ||

If the Lord of the Fifth House is in the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the Fifth House, then offspring will be born soon. If they form a <term>Nakta Yoga</term> <note>A configuration where two planets are connected through the mediation of a third, faster planet</note>, then it will happen after a delay. || 2 ||

> If a dual-natured sign is on the Ascendant and the Fifth House is joined by a benefic, there is a combination for two children. If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Fifth are in masculine signs, then a son is in the womb. || 3 ||

->**On the question of life or death for infants, if the Lord of the Twelfth is aspected by benefics...**<-

->**Aspected by malefics, the child dies at birth or in the womb. || 10 ||**<-

In a query to determine the day of delivery, one should look at the degrees already traversed in the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> to represent the months of pregnancy already passed; the remaining degrees to be traversed should be used to estimate the remaining days until birth. || 11 ||

->**The month of pregnancy corresponds to the house position of Venus from the Ascendant...**<-

The number of months the woman has been pregnant corresponds to the number of houses Venus <term>Shukra</term> is removed from the Ascendant. If Venus is positioned beyond the ninth house, one should count the houses starting from the fifth house to the position of Venus to determine the months of pregnancy. || 12 ||

->**If the Ascendant and its Lord are in day-signs, birth is by day...**<-
->**In the opposite case, the reverse is true. || 13 ||**<-

If the Ascendant is a day-sign <term>Divavali: signs that are strong during the day</term> and the Lord of the Ascendant is also in a day-sign, the birth will occur during the day. If these are strong in night-signs, the birth will occur at night. || 13 ||

->**The Moon's position in a twelfth-part at the time of the query...**<-
->**The birth occurs when the Moon reaches that same sign in the ninth or tenth month. || 14 ||**<-

At the time of the query or conception, whichever twelfth-part <term>Dwadasamsha: a 2.5-degree division of a sign</term> the Moon occupies, the birth will take place in the ninth or tenth month when the Moon returns to that same sign. This calculation should be performed according to the scriptures.

Regarding the question "Will this woman give birth or not?", if the Lord of the Fifth or the Lord of the Sixth has emerged from <term>combustion</term> <note>being too close to the Sun</note> and is rising, or if Jupiter, Mars, and Venus are in the tenth house <note>the highest point in the sky</note>, then delivery will occur. || 17 ||

# Tajika Neelakanthi

If Venus and the Sun are in the eighth house, and malefic planets occupy the second, twelfth, or eighth houses, then children die immediately after birth, and there will be no auspicious offspring in the future. ॥ 24 ॥

->If the lord of the twelfth house is in a quadrant <note>original: 'kendra', the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> and is joined or aspected by benefic planets, the child lives.<-

If Jupiter, the Moon, the Ascendant, and the Sun are in odd signs and odd <term>navamsha</term> <note>the ninth-part harmonic division of a sign</note>, they grant a son. In even signs and even divisions—meaning male sign divisions—they grant daughters. ॥ 29 ॥

->### Now, the Inquiry into the Sixth House<-

### On whether a patient will recover from illness or not.

The Ascendant represents the physician; the seventh house represents the disease; the tenth house represents the patient; and the fourth house represents the medicine. So say the great teachers. || 1 ||
<note>In horary astrology (Prashna), specific houses are assigned to different actors in a situation to determine the outcome.</note>

If the Ascendant is afflicted by cruel <note>malefic</note> planets, the physician will be of no benefit, and the disease will increase because of the medicine. If there are cruel planets in the tenth house, the disease increases due to the patient's own mistakes. || 2 ||

If there are cruel planets in the seventh house, the illness will lead to further complications; if they are in the fourth house, the medicine itself will cause the disease to worsen. If these houses (1st, 10th, 7th, and 4th) are occupied by gentle <note>benefic</note> planets or if these houses are strong, the patient will become free from disease. || 3 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon form a <term>Itthashala</term> <note>A favorable aspect or "link" in Tajika astrology indicating the coming together of two influences</note> with a gentle planet, the destruction of the disease should be predicted. However, if the planet involved is in <term>Retrograde</term> <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note> or forms an <term>Ishrafa</term> <note>A separating aspect indicating the fading of an influence</note>, the disease will return again and again. || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the fourth house and forms a <term>Muthashila</term> <note>A specific configuration where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of the matter</note> with the Moon, death may occur. Alternatively, if the Lord of the eighth house <note>the house of death</note> is in the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the eighth house, death is also indicated. || 5 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon form a <term>Muthashila</term> with the Lord of the seventh house, or if the Lord of the seventh house is in the sixth house, one should predict the death of the patient. || 6 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi
<page-num>234</page-num>
->**The Treatise of Nilakantha on Persian Astrology**<-

If the <term>Lord of the Eighth House</term><note>The Eighth House traditionally governs death and chronic illness.</note> is neither weakened nor combust <note>A planet is 'combust' when it is too close to the Sun, losing its power.</note>, and is positioned in a <term>Quadrant</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are positions of strength.</note>, and forms a <term>Muthashila</term><note>A specific aspect in Persian-Indian astrology where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of an event.</note> with the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term><note>The planet ruling the rising sign, representing the patient.</note>, then in a query regarding illness, death will occur. || 7 ||

Alternatively, if there is a *Muthashila* between these two in a Quadrant and they are afflicted by cruel planets, death occurs. If a malefic planet or the Lord of the Eighth House is in a Quadrant, there will be great suffering from the disease. || 8 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant has entered the <term>Solar Dwadashamsha</term><note>A 1/12th division of a sign (2° 30') specifically related to the Sun's position.</note>, death occurs. Likewise, if the Lord of the First House and the Lord of the Eighth House have exchanged places <note>The ruler of the 1st is in the 8th, and the ruler of the 8th is in the 1st.</note>, death is predicted. || 9 ||

If the Ascendant is in a **Movable Sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn.</note>, the patient's condition fluctuates—one moment healthy, the next moment ill. In a **Dual Sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces.</note>, one disease leads to another. In a **Fixed Sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius.</note>, the disease remains the same from beginning to end. || 10 ||

If the Moon forms a *Muthashila* with a **Retrograde Planet**, the disease will remain stable (chronic). If it forms a *Muthashila* with Saturn, a strange or unprecedented disease occurs, and the illness is known to arise from the suppression of urine. || 11 ||

Now, looking back seven or four days before the time of the query: if during those days the Moon and Sun were joined with or aspected by benefic planets, it is always auspicious for the patient. || 12 ||

In a query asking "Is this person slow/dull or not?", if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon forms a *Muthashila* with the <term>Lord of the Sixth House</term><note>The house governing sickness and enemies.</note> or is combust, then the person is indeed slow/dull. || 13 ||

### On Questions Regarding Masters, Servants, and Four-footed Animals.

<note>original Sanskrit: "īśo'nyo mamabhavitānavetilagneśvare'syayadi kendre..."</note>
If the Lord of the Ascendant is in a <term>Kendrasthana</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered pillars of power</note> and does not form a <term>Muthashila</term> with the Lords of the Sixth or Twelfth houses, then there will be no other master. || 14 ||

In response to the question "Will I have another master?" (meaning, will I find employment elsewhere?): if the Lord of the Ascendant, while in a Kendra, does not form a <term>Muthashila</term> with the Lord of the Sixth <note>house of service</note> or the Lord of the Twelfth <note>house of loss</note>, then there will be no other master. || 14 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is retrograde and forms an <term>Itthashala</term> <note>a favorable aspect indicating the completion of an event</note> with any planet situated in the third or ninth house, then the querent <note>the person asking the question</note> will indeed have another master. || 15 ||

In the inquiry "Will this master be good for me?": if the Lord of the Ascendant forms a <term>Kamboola</term> <note>a configuration involving the Moon that confirms a result</note> with a benefic planet, then that same master will be auspicious. If the <term>Lord of the Seventh House</term> <note>Dyunesha</note> forms a <term>Kamboola</term> with a benefic, then a different master will be auspicious. || 17 ||

Regarding questions about the stability or movement of houses, land, and places, the same method previously mentioned should be applied. One should carefully deliberate with their own intellect and then speak of the good or bad results to the <term>Prashta</term> <note>the querent/inquirer</note>. || 18 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi

<page-num>236</page-num>
->The Jewel of Tajika Astrology<-

> If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the sixth house, or if they form a *Muthashila* <note>A specific planetary aspect in Tajika astrology indicating the completion of an event</note> with the Lord of the sixth house, or if the Lord of the sixth house is in the Ascendant, there will be gain of servants and four-footed animals. || 19 ||

In a query regarding the gain of a servant or four-footed livestock <note>original: "chatuspada," referring to cattle or horses</note>, if the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> and the Moon are in the sixth house, or if they form a *Muthashila* yoga with the Lord of the sixth house, or if the Lord of the sixth house is situated in the Ascendant, then one will obtain them. || 19 ||

> In a query regarding servants or vehicles, the Ascendant and its Lord represent the seeker; the seventh house and its Lord represent the giver. Acquisition is determined by their respective strength. || 20 ||

In questions concerning servants or vehicles <note>original: "vahana," meaning a carriage or mount</note>, the Ascendant and its Lord represent the person asking the question (the seeker), while the seventh house and its Lord represent the person giving or selling. One should judge the gain or loss based on their strength. For example, if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the seventh house have a mutual *Muthashila* or a favorable relationship, the servant or vehicle will be acquired. If there is an *Israpha* <note>An aspect indicating separation or non-completion</note> or a lack of relationship, they will not be obtained. || 20 ||

### Disputes from Other Texts

> If a cruel planet is in the Ascendant during a query about a dispute, the seeker wins the argument in all conditions, unless the planet is in its sign of debilitation or is combust; then, they will not defeat the enemy. || 21 ||

In a query regarding a dispute, if a "cruel" planet <term>Krura-graha: a malefic planet like Mars or Saturn</term> is strong in the Ascendant, the seeker will win the dispute. However, if that planet is in its sign of debilitation or is combust <note>hidden by the sun's light</note>, the seeker will not be able to triumph over the enemy. || 21 ||

> When cruel planets in the Ascendant and the seventh house cast hostile glances at each other, the two disputants will fight and may even strike each other with knives. || 22 ||

If malefic planets are situated in both the Ascendant and the seventh house and cast "hostile glances" <note>original: "shatru-drishti," referring to square or opposition aspects</note> upon one another, the plaintiff and defendant will clash in their dispute and may resort to using knives or weapons against each other. || 22 ||

> If there are cruel planets in the Ascendant and the seventh house, the quarrel between the disputants will not cease at that time. The stronger one will overpower the weaker. Here, the Ascendant represents the seeker and the seventh house represents the opponent. || 23 ||

If malefic planets occupy both the Ascendant and the seventh house, the conflict between the parties will not be resolved quickly. In such a case, whichever planet is stronger will allow that party to dominate the weaker one. It should be understood that the Ascendant represents the seeker <term>Prashta: the person asking the question</term> and the seventh house represents the opponent <term>Prativadi: the defendant or rival</term>. || 23 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi

If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh House are joined with a malefic planet in the same location, then the man and woman will be affectionate after a period of fighting. If they are joined with the Sun, there will only be strife. If the aforementioned yoga-forming planets <note>Yoga-karta: planets creating a specific astrological combination</note> are weak, then both will remain angry. || 10 ||

### On the Return of an Angry Woman

"Will my wife, who has left in anger, return or not?" In such an inquiry, if the Sun or Venus is between the Ascendant and the Fourth House, she will not return. If Venus is retrograde <note>Vakri: appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, she will return. The houses from the Ascendant to the Fourth are the "places of joy" for the woman; from the Fourth to the Seventh are the "places of joy" for the man. One should predict the results based on the influence of the planets representing the man and woman in these houses. || 11 ||

If Venus has recently emerged from the Sun <note>Heliacal rising</note> or is retrograde, the angry woman will return on her own. If a waning Moon connects with this, she returns after many days; if a full Moon connects, she will return quickly. || 12 ||

### Now, the Examination of a Maiden

In the inquiry, "Is this maiden truly without faults or not?" if the Ascendant, the Lord of the Ascendant, and the Moon are all in fixed signs <note>Sthira Rashi: signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, indicating stability</note>, she is without fault. || 13 ||

If these are in movable signs <note>Chara Rashi: signs indicating change or instability</note>, then this maiden may possess faults. If the Moon is in a dual sign <note>Dvisharira: "two-bodied" or mutable signs</note> and the Ascendant is movable, there will be only slight faults. || 14 ||

### Now, the Knowledge of Delivery (Childbirth)

**She has indeed given birth if Venus is in Aquarius; know her as not having given birth if Mercury is in Leo. If these two are in Scorpio and Taurus respectively, the woman is known to have given birth || 17 ||**

### Now, the Examination of Fidelity

->Whether she is unfaithful or virtuous: if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are with Mars,<-

If it is with Venus, the woman is enjoyed by a man who is effeminate or very handsome. If these combinations are absent or reversed, she should be understood as virtuous. || 22 ||

If Venus aspects the aforementioned Mars, the woman will leave her lover out of fear of the lover's own wife. If Venus and Mercury aspect from the same sign, the woman feels ashamed because the lover is an old man, and thus she leaves him. || 24 ||

# Tajika Neelakanthi
<note>A classic 16th-century treatise on Tajika astrology, which blends Persian-Arabic astrological techniques with Sanskrit traditions.</note>

In a King's inquiry regarding battle, one should predict victory or defeat based on the relationship between the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>, its Lord, and the Moon's application <note>original: "Muthashila"</note> or separation <note>original: "Musaripha"</note> from them. If the Ascendant and its Lord are associated with auspicious yogas, victory belongs to the querent; if the Seventh house <note>representing the enemy</note> and its Lord are stronger, the enemy shall prevail. || 1 ||

->Alternatively, if Saturn, Mars, and Jupiter are stronger than the faster planets and positioned above,<-
->And if Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are weaker and positioned below them, consider the outcome thus:<- || 2 ||

Or, if Saturn, Mars, and Jupiter are powerful with higher degrees, and Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are weaker with lower degrees—meaning an <term>Itthashala: a favorable application where a faster planet approaches a slower one</term> is formed—then victory over the enemy is assured. Conversely, if an <term>Isarapha: a separation where the faster planet has already passed the slower one</term> occurs, the enemy will be victorious. || 2 ||

->If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh house form a Muthashila through a Decan aspect, there will be mutual affection;<-
->If they are in the sixth or twelfth houses, the enemy shall be captured or bound by another.<- || 3 ||

If the Lords of the Ascendant and the Seventh house form a <term>Musaripha: separation</term> or are combust <note>hidden by the Sun's rays</note>, the battle will not last long. If the Lord of the Ascendant is slow with higher degrees and the Lord of the Seventh is fast with lower degrees, forming a <term>Kamboola: a yoga where the Moon transfers light between two planets</term>, the querent shall be victorious. || 4 ||

->When the slower planet has higher degrees and the faster has lower degrees, and the Moon forms a Muthashila while being combust or in debilitation,<-
->Or if the Lord of the Seventh is in a quadrant, combust, or debilitated, the querent's defeat should be predicted.<- || 5 ||

If there is a benefic planet below the Ascendant and a malefic planet above it, the allies will be unhelpful. If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the eighth house <note>the house of death and transformation</note> and forms a Muthashila with the Lord of the eighth, the querent will be killed in battle. || 6 ||
