-> If a malefic is in the ascendant, joined or aspected by another malefic, or if there are malefics in the houses before and after the ascendant, then the war will be terrible. || 31 || <-

If a malefic planet is in the ascendant <note>the first house or rising sign</note> and is joined with or aspected by another malefic, or if there are malefic planets in the second and twelfth houses <note>flanking the ascendant</note>, then a horrific war will occur. || 31 ||

### Now, the Query of the Ninth House.

-> "Will my journey happen or not?" If the lord of the ascendant or the Moon forms a Muthashila with the lord of the ninth, or if the lord of the ascendant is in the ninth, the journey will occur. || 1 || <-

In response to the question "Will I go on a journey or not?", if the lord of the ascendant or the Moon forms a *Muthashila* <term>Muthashila: an aspect in Tajik astrology where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of a matter</term> with the lord of the ninth house, or if the lord of the ascendant is placed in the ninth house, the journey will take place. || 1 ||

-> If the lord of the ninth is in the ascendant and forms a Muthashila with the lord of the ascendant, one keeps wandering. If the lord of the ascendant or ninth does not aspect the ninth house, the journey will not happen. || 2 || <-

If the lord of the ninth is in the ascendant and forms a *Muthashila* with the lord of the ascendant, the person remains in constant motion. However, if neither the lord of the ascendant nor the lord of the ninth house casts an aspect <note>a planetary "look" or influence</note> upon the ninth house, the journey will not occur. || 2 ||

-> If the lord of the ascendant is in an angle and forms a Muthashila with the lord of the third house and is free from malefics, the journey will happen. If there are malefics in the angles, there is no movement. || 3 || <-

If the lord of the ascendant is in an angle and forms a *Muthashila* with the lord of the third house and is free from the influence of cruel planets, the journey will happen. If there are cruel <note>malefic</note> planets in the angles, there will be no departure. || 3 ||

## The Arrival of a Traveler from Another Text

In a query regarding a traveler's arrival, if the Lord of the Ascendant is situated within the Ascendant and forms an <term>Ithashala: a specific favorable aspect in Persian-influenced Tajika astrology</term> with the planet representing the traveler, they will return happily; if in the 4th or 7th house, they return with difficulty. || 14 ||
In a question about a traveler's arrival, if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant and forms an *Ithashala* <note>original: "muthashila"</note>, they will arrive happily; if in the 4th or 7th house, they will arrive with distress. || 14 ||

In a query about whether someone has left a place, if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 3rd or 9th house and forms an *Ithashala* with a planet in the Ascendant, this traveler is currently on the road. || 15 ||

In a query regarding whether a traveler has departed from a location or not: if the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "लग्नेश" (Lagnesha) — the planet ruling the first house</note> is in the 3rd or 9th house and forms a Muthashila <term>Muthashila: an aspect in Tajika astrology where a faster planet approaches a slower one, indicating the fulfillment of an event</term> with any planet situated in the Ascendant, then the traveler is currently on the road. || 15 ||

### On the Question of Whether One Far Away is Alive or Dead

If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the sixth, fourth, or eighth houses, or are in their deep debilitation, or are combust <note>too close to the Sun to be seen</note>, and form an *Itthashala* Yoga <note>A Tajika aspect indicating the completion of an event</note> with the Lord of the eighth house while joined by malefics, the one who has gone far away is dead. || 45 ||
<gloss>In a query regarding a traveler's life, if the primary indicators of the person (Ascendant Lord and Moon) are weakened in "dusthana" (difficult) houses and connect with the Lord of Death, it signifies a fatal outcome.</gloss> || 45 ||

If the Moon forms an *Itthashala* with a retrograde planet situated below the earth <note>in the northern houses of the chart, 1st through 6th</note>, and is not aspected by benefics, it causes the death of the person residing in a distant foreign land. || 46 ||

**If a malefic is in a Prishtodaya sign, and malefics are in the trines, angles, or the eighth and sixth houses, and they are not seen by benefics, the one in a foreign land has died of disease; the same is said if the Sun is in the ninth. || 48 ||**

If a malefic planet is in a <term>Prishtodaya</term><note>Signs that rise "back-first," such as Aries, Taurus, or Cancer</note> sign (1, 2, 4, 9) <note>original: "1 | 2 | 4 | 9 राशि"</note>, and malefic planets are in the trines, the center <insert>angles</insert>, or the eighth house, and the benefics do not see them, then the person in the foreign land has died of illness. If the Sun is in the ninth house, the same result should be predicted. || 48 ||

**If the Moon forms an Itthashala with a planet situated above the fourth house and is gazed upon by a benefic, or is joined with benefics, the one in the foreign land lives happily and will find comfort on the journey. || 49 ||**

If the Moon forms an <term>Itthashala</term> with any planet between the fourth and the seventh houses, and is also gazed upon or joined by a benefic planet, then the person in the foreign land is alive and happy, and they will travel home in comfort. || 49 ||

->Thus ends the inquiry into the Ninth House in the Tajika Neelakanthi, with the commentary by Shrimahidhara. || 9 ||<-

### Now, the Inquiry into the Tenth House.

**In a question regarding the attainment of kingdom, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon forms a Muthashila with the Lord of the Tenth, the kingdom is obtained according to one's status. || 1 ||**

In a question about gaining <term>Rajya</term><note>Kingdom, authority, or high office</note>, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon forms a <term>Muthashila</term><note>A Persian-influenced astrological term for a favorable aspect or "connection"</note> with the Lord of the Tenth house, and there is a friendly aspect, then one receives the happiness of authority according to their family lineage. || 1 ||

**If they have exchanged houses and are free of malefics, the desired object is attained; likewise if the Lord of the Ascendant forms a Muthashila with a benefic in the tenth. || 2 ||**

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the tenth house and the Lord of the Tenth is in the Ascendant, and they are free from malefic influence, the desired royal happiness is obtained. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Ascendant forms a <term>Muthashila</term> with any benefic planet situated in the tenth house, the same result will occur. || 2 ||

# Tajaka Neelakanthi

> **When the slow-moving planet is strong and the Moon is weak and separated from malefic influence,**
> **the questioner attains a kingdom through travel due to the movement of the strong Saturn. || 3 ||**

Among the yoga-forming planets, if the slow-moving planet <note>Saturn</note> is strong and the Moon is weak but free from the influence of cruel planets <note>malefics like Mars or Rahu</note>, and if Saturn remains powerful, the person asking the question will attain the happiness of a kingdom or high status through travel. || 3 ||

---

> **If the Lord of the Ascendant is in its own house and Mars is in its exaltation, there is gain of a kingdom.**
> **The same occurs if the Lords of the Ascendant and the Tenth House form a Kamboola yoga through a Muthashila with the Moon in a quadrant. || 4 ||**

If the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> is in its own zodiac sign and Mars is in its sign of exaltation <note>Capricorn</note>, the gain of a kingdom occurs. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Tenth House <term>Dashamesha: the planet ruling the house of career and status</term> form a <term>Muthashila: an auspicious aspect in Tajika astrology</term> and are joined with the Moon in a <term>Kamboola: a specific configuration where the Moon links two planets</term> while situated in a quadrant <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note>, the same successful result should be predicted. || 4 ||

---

> **Great attainment of a kingdom comes from the Moon in its own sign or exaltation.**
> **If the lord of the sign where the Ascendant Lord sits is a malefic, then the work [is affected]. || 5 ||**
> **If it is combust, it happens with difficulty; if there is a harsh aspect, there is bitterness in the work.**
> **If someone asks about the final outcome after the kingdom is attained, then: || 6 ||**

If there is an *Itthashala* <note>a favorable planetary application</note> between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Tenth House, and the Moon is in its own sign or its exaltation—forming the highest quality *Kamboola* yoga—then the attainment of the kingdom will be of the highest order and very vast. However, if the lord of the sign in which the Ascendant Lord is placed is situated in an inauspicious sign, the state-related work will not be accomplished. If that planet is <term>combust: obscured by the sun's proximity</term>, it will happen only with great suffering. If it is subject to the gaze <note>aspect</note> of an enemy planet, some form of bitterness or unpleasantness will arise in the undertaking. || 5 || 6 ||

---

> **The Ascendant represents the body's work, the seventh house represents domestic affairs, and the sky (tenth) represents the kingdom's purpose.**
> **The eleventh represents gain and friends' wealth, and the fourth represents the residence for one's work. || 7 ||**

If someone asks about the eventual outcome after a royal or state position has been attained, one should judge the following: the Ascendant <note>1st house</note> for matters of the physical body, the seventh house for household or domestic affairs, the tenth house for state-related duties, the eleventh house for gains and matters related to friends, and the fourth house for matters regarding one's residence or place of work. || 7 ||

---

> **The second house for wealth, the third for servants, and the sixth for enemies.**
> **With auspicious planets in these, there is success; with inauspicious ones, the opposite occurs for all tasks. || 8 ||**

One should consider the second house for matters of wealth, the third house for servants or subordinates, and the sixth house for matters related to enemies.

# Tajika Neelakanthi
<note>The Tajika Neelakanthi is a seminal 16th-century Sanskrit treatise on Persian-influenced Indian astrology, written by Neelakantha Daivajna.</note>

### Questions Regarding Master and Servant from Other Texts

If a "Head-rising" sign <note>original: "shirshodaya"; these are zodiac signs that rise with their head first, considered auspicious</note> is occupied or aspected by benefic planets, and if the second, eighth, and seventh houses are free of malefic planets, while the third, eleventh, and sixth houses contain malefic planets, then a servant of the king <note>or any high official</note> shall obtain happiness and financial gain. || 14 ||

In a question regarding a master and servant: if benefic planets are in a Head-rising sign, aspected by benefics, and if the 2nd, 8th, and 7th houses are occupied by benefics while the 3rd, 11th, and 6th houses contain malefics, the royal servant receives happiness and wealth. || 14 ||

If malefic planets are placed in the second, seventh, or eighth houses from the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, they cause, respectively, loss of wealth, confusion/distress, and even death to the servant at the hands of the king. Therefore, one should avoid service under such conditions. || 15 ||

If malefics are in the 2nd house from the Ascendant, the servant suffers loss of wealth from the king; if in the 7th, there is great anxiety; if in the 8th, there is death. Therefore, if malefics occupy these places, one should not enter the master's service. || 15 ||

Malefic planets situated in the 2nd, 8th, and 7th houses from the Ascendant cause the destruction of both the master and the servant. Conversely, if benefic planets are placed in those same houses, they grant wealth, health, and happiness to both. || 16 ||

Malefics in the 2nd, 8th, and 7th houses destroy both the king and the servant; benefics in those same positions bring wealth, health, and happiness to both. || 16 ||

If the Moon and the benefic planets are strong and aspect or occupy the Ascendant and the seventh house, and these places are not influenced by malefic planets, then the king will hold affection and favor in his heart for the petitioner. If the opposite occurs—malefics occupying the places of the benefics—the result is the opposite <note>disfavor or anger</note>. || 17 ||

If a strong Moon and strong benefics aspect or join the 1st and 7th houses, and no malefics are present there, the king remains affectionate and gracious toward the questioner. If malefics are there instead, the king will be unmerciful and hostile. || 17 ||

### Other Questions Regarding the Master

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnasha</note> forms an *Itthashala* <note>a specific Tajika aspect indicating the coming together of two planets</note> in a quadrant <note>Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> with the Lord of the 6th house or the Lord of the 12th house, then the master will grant wealth to the petitioner. If the configuration is contrary, the master will not be favorable. || 18 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant makes an *Itthashala* with the Lord of the 6th or 12th in a quadrant, the master will be a giver of wealth; otherwise, he will not. || 18 ||

### Now, Regarding Rumors.

> If the Ascendant, its Lord, and the Moon are joined by benefics in the centers, the news is true;
> If joined or aspected by malefics, or placed in the "Three Houses of Suffering," it is false. || 31 ||

If they are associated with or aspected by malefic planets, or placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses <note>Trik houses</note>, the rumor is false. The terms "Janashruti" or "Kimvadanti" refer to rumors or proverbs circulating among the people. || 31 ||

> Through the aspect or union of benefics, gentle news is indicated as true;
> Through the aspect or union of malefics, harsh news is declared true.
> If the Lord of the Ascendant is about to turn retrograde, the news will be false. || 32 ||

If there is an aspect or union of auspicious planets upon the Ascendant, its Lord, and the Moon, then "gentle" or positive news should be known as true, while "harsh" news is false. Conversely, if there is an aspect or union of malefic planets, then "harsh" or negative news is true, and positive news is false. If the Lord of the Ascendant is about to become retrograde <note>moving backward in the sky</note>, then all news will prove to be false. || 32 ||

### Concerning Market Prices from Another Text

**In Aries, Taurus, and Gemini, if aspected by benefics, summer crops become easily available on earth. ||**
**With benefics in Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Aquarius, one should predict cheapness for autumn crops; with malefics, they become expensive. || 7**

### Now, the Inquiry into the Twelfth House.

**In an inquiry regarding war with an enemy, if the sixth house is strong, the enemy is powerful. If the Lord of the twelfth house is aspected by benefics and is powerful, then auspicious results should be predicted for the querent.** || 1 ||

In a question regarding conflict, if the sixth house (the house of enemies) is strong, the enemy will be formidable. If the Lord of the twelfth house <term>Vyayesha: the planetary ruler of the house of loss and expenditure</term> is aspected by benefics and is strong, it will be favorable for the person asking the question. || 1 ||

**If [the Lord of the twelfth] is associated with or aspected by benefics, expenditure is for good purposes; if influenced by malefics, expenditure is due to calamities. In this manner, the wise should deduce the good or bad results for all houses.** || 2 ||

If the Lord of the twelfth house is influenced by benefic planets, money will be spent on virtuous or auspicious deeds. If it is influenced by malefic planets, wealth will be wasted on unfortunate or harmful matters. A person of sound intellect should apply this logic to determine the results of all the houses of the horoscope. || 2 ||

### Now, the Inquiry into Food from other Texts.

**Pungent, salty, bitter, mixed, sweet, sour, and astringent: these are the flavors attributed to the Sun and the other planets in their respective order.** || 3 ||

The Sun represents pungent flavors; the Moon, salty; Mars, bitter; Mercury, a mixture of flavors; Jupiter, sweet; Venus, sour; and Saturn represents astringent flavors (such as decoctions or fermented gruel). || 3 ||

# Tajika Nilakanthi

The planet that aspects <note>looks upon or influences</note> the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the rising sign at the time of inquiry</term>—the flavor associated with that planet is what will be present in the meal. Alternatively, other flavors should be identified based on the relative strength of the planets. **4**
<note>In Tajika astrology, each planet corresponds to a specific taste: e.g., the Sun is pungent, the Moon is salty, Mars is bitter.</note>
The flavor of the planet that aspects the Ascendant, or the flavor of the strongest planet, should be predicted in questions regarding food. **4**

One should specifically describe the food based on the planet with which the Moon forms a *Muthashila* <term>an aspectual configuration in Tajika astrology where a faster planet approaches a slower one</term>. A more detailed explanation of the rules regarding food has been clearly stated in the Second Tantra <note>the Varshaphala or Annual Analysis section</note> of this work. **5**
The flavor of the planet with which the Moon is in *Muthashila* should be specifically mentioned regarding the meal. The detailed consideration of food-related inquiries is explained more clearly in the second part of this book (Nilakanthi). **5**

### Special Considerations for Market Prices and Commodities from Other Texts

The consideration of affordable prices <term>Samargha; when goods are plentiful and cheap</term> is investigated by everyone first. Therefore, I am stating here the specific considerations as ordained by the scriptures. **1**
Everyone first considers whether prices will be high or low; therefore, the specific scriptural methods are described here. **1**

If, at the time of the Full Moon, the New Moon, the Moon's entry into Aries, or the Sun's entry into Aries <term>Mesha Sankranti; the solar new year</term>, the Lords of the Ascendant are associated with or aspected by benefic planets, they will bestow great happiness upon the world in that year. If they are afflicted by malefic planets, there will be disease and fear of the government <note>original: "Narendra-bhaya" - fear of the king or ruler</note> among the subjects. **2**
In any given year, if the Lord of the Ascendant at the time of the first Full Moon, the first New Moon, the Moon's first entry into Aries, and the Sun's entry into Aries are influenced by auspicious planets, the people will have complete happiness. If influenced by inauspicious planets, there will be illness and fear of the king. **2**

If the Lord of the Ascendant at the time of the Sun's entry into Aries is a benefic planet, situated in its sign of exaltation or its own sign, or placed in a quadrant <term>Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> and is strong and influenced by auspicious planets, he will bring goodness, happiness, abundant crops, and good rain to the world in that year. If the Lord is a malefic planet or is afflicted by malefics, he indicates fear of the king, distress, and expensive grain <term>Mahargha; high prices or famine</term>. **3**

### Now, the Knowledge of Rain.

> If a water-sign is in the third house from the query-ascendant,

If the Sun is behind Mars, the rain is only in name <note>negligible</note>, but if the Sun is ahead of Mars, there is much rain. || 19 ||

> or in a quadrant during the bright fortnight and aspected by auspicious planets, there is heavy rain. || 20 ||

In a rain-query, if the Moon is in a water-sign or in the ascendant, or if the Moon of the bright fortnight <term>Shukla Paksha: the waxing phase of the moon</term> is in a quadrant <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> of a water-sign and aspected by auspicious planets, there will be excessive rain. || 20 ||

> There is little rain if it is aspected by malefic planets, especially during the monsoon;
> all these same qualities should be understood for Venus as they are for the Moon. || 21 ||

If the aforementioned Moon is also aspected by malefic planets, there will be little rain. If this combination occurs during the monsoon season, rain will occur after many days. The same should be understood regarding the planet Venus. || 21 ||

One should know the directions as follows: the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the first house of a horoscope</term> represents the East, the fourth house represents the South, the seventh house represents the West, and the tenth house represents the North. || 38 ||

> In whichever direction Saturn is joined with or aspected by malefic planets, 
> in that very direction, there will surely be ill health and famine. || 39 ||

In whichever direction Saturn is associated with or viewed by "sinful" <note>original: "papa"; referring to malefic planets like Mars or Rahu</note> planets, there will be disturbances such as disease and also famine. || 39 ||

> In the direction where the Sun is located, there will be destruction of grain caused by the King; 
> where Mars is likewise situated, there will be destruction of grain and fear of fire. || 40 ||

In the direction where the Sun is seen to be joined with malefics, there will be a loss of grain due to the government or ruler. Where Mars is similarly placed, there will be loss of grain and also the danger of fires. || 40 ||

> In the direction where the benefic planets are present, endowed with full strength, 
> that direction should be known as prosperous, and there will be health and abundance. || 41 ||

In the direction where benefic planets <note>Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury</note> are positioned with full strength, all crops will be good and health will remain excellent. From weak benefics, one should predict unfavorable results; from strong malefics, some slight favor; and in mixed cases, mixed results. || 41 ||

> If in all the quadrants, malefic planets are situated with full strength, 
> then that country is considered ruined; so should it be known by those skilled in the scriptures. || 42 ||

If malefic planets are powerful in all the centers <term>Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>, then all those regions are almost destroyed. Experts in the scriptures should speak specifically after considering their strength, weakness, and various relationships. || 42 ||

> Tell me whether this specific item will be cheap or expensive—
> in such a query, whichever planet establishes a favorable state, || 43 ||
> for as many months as that planet maintains the auspiciousness of that sign, 
> for that many months, the wise say the item will be affordable. || 44 ||

In a question regarding when there will be a time of plenty or a time of scarcity for specific grains, one looks to the planet that shows favor to the zodiac sign associated with that grain's name. For as many months as it takes for that planet to move into another sign, the wise consider that the item will remain affordable <note>original: "samargha"; meaning low-priced or abundant</note>. || 43 || 44 ||

<summary>This page details astrological methods for predicting famine, disease, and market prices based on the placement of malefic and benefic planets in specific directions and houses. It emphasizes that Saturn, Mars, and the Sun bring destruction to crops and health, while strong benefics ensure prosperity.</summary>

<keywords>astrology, famine, Saturn, Mars, crop yields, market prices, quadrants, planetary aspects, mundane astrology</keywords>

--- Page 286 ---
<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of Tajika astrology, specifically focusing on timing events and the planetary rulers of various commodities.</meta>

<page-num>278</page-num>
-># Tajika Nilakanthi<-

Now, one should consider how many days it will take for this inauspicious situation to certainly transform into a favorable state based on the auspicious aspects present in the Ascendant <note>The "Lagna" or rising sign</note>. || 45 ||
The number of days or months should be understood by the wise; accordingly, the high value or price of a commodity should be explained by those who are discerning. || 46 ||

When someone asks about the time when an inauspicious situation will become auspicious, one should determine the number of auspicious influences in the Ascendant. Depending on what is possible in the specific context, a wise scholar should calculate and announce the timing in days or months. || 45 || 46 ||

The strength of the Presiding Deity <note>The planetary ruler of a specific object or matter</note> should be known when the Ascendant is devoid of its own Lord. If the Presiding Deity is weak, then one must evaluate the strength or weakness of the Lord of the Ascendant. || 47 ||

One must first understand the strength of the specific Presiding Deity <term>Adhishtatha: the planet governing a particular commodity or person</term> associated with the task or object, and then predict profit or loss according to that strength. In the Ascendant, the Presiding Deity is considered powerful if the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> is weak. If the Presiding Deity is weak, one should always look to the strength of the Lord of the Ascendant. The specific deities are described hereafter: || 47 ||

The Sun is the ruler of pearls, rubies, gold, copper, silk, mica, armor, and the wives of others. The Moon is the ruler of pearls, sugarcane, conch shells, liquid substances, silver, kings, and salt. || 48 ||
Mars is the presiding lord of lentils, copper, cinnabar, orpiment <note>yellow arsenic mineral</note>, other minerals, weapons, and coral. Mercury is the master of fragrant substances, clothes, pulses <note>split grains</note>, birds, and emeralds. || 49 ||
Jupiter is the lord of mustard seeds, wheat, barley, sugarcane products, all aquatic lotuses, camphor, and cows. Venus is the ruler of oils, horses, variegated clothes, silver, water-born products, and crystal. Saturn is the ruler of wool, elephants, indigo, hides, leather, black cloth, iron, and buffaloes. || 50 ||

The presiding rulers of objects: The Sun is the master of pearls, rubies, gold, copper, silk, mica, weapons, armor, and the wives of others. The Moon is the master of pearls, sugarcane, conch shells, liquid items, coconuts, mangoes, silver, kings, and salt. Mars is the presiding deity of lentils, copper, cinnabar, yellow arsenic and other minerals, weapons, and coral. Mercury is the lord of perfumes, clothes, pulses, grains, birds, and emeralds. Jupiter is the lord of mustard, wheat, barley, sugarcane derivatives, and aquatic plants like lotus stalks, water chestnuts, and water-caltrop.

->Commentary in the Common Tongue<-

<note>The text continues listing items ruled by specific planets</note> ...produced items, as well as camphor, are ruled by Jupiter. Other perfumes, scented oils, flowers, and similar fragrant items, along with food grains, multicolored clothes, silver, aquatic products <note>items born of the water, such as pearls or shells</note>, and crystal are ruled by Venus. Wool, pashmina, indigo, leather goods, black garments, iron, buffaloes, and similar things are presided over by Saturn. # Notice

The venerable Nilakantha previously composed the system known as *Prashna* <note>Horary astrology, or the art of answering questions based on the time they are asked</note> after his works on the results of the solar return years. That work is currently not available in its entirety, yet I consider the results of such questions to be essential. || 1 || Therefore, for the benefit of all, this highly virtuous and well-compiled collection, incorporating other scriptures along with a commentary in the common tongue, has been prepared by me, Mahidhar, a twice-born <note>Brahmin</note>, following the path of the ancients. || 2 || During the reign of King Shri Kirti Shah, in the Shalivahana era year 1808 <note>approx. 1886 CE</note>, in the city of Tehri in the land of Garhwal, at the conclusion of the commentary on the great *Jataka* <note>Natal astrology</note> in the auspicious common tongue; || 3 || This easy-to-read commentary on the three systems of Shri Nilakanthi was created. O wise saints, please forgive whatever impulsiveness I have shown. May the people make use of this "Mahidhari" commentary, which provides easy understanding for beginners, illuminates the fruits of astrology, and is helpful and clear. || 4 || Those who are intent on finding faults, who wish to destroy the work of others out of malice, who are bent on ruining others' purposes through envy, who are arrogant in their minds, slack in good deeds, and happy in misdeeds—let them criticize or let them rejoice; my work is for the sake of merit and the benefit of others, regardless of the wicked and envious. || 5 || In the Shaka year 1821 <note>approx. 1899 CE</note>, on the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada, a Thursday, Ramabharosa Sharma corrected this Mahidhari commentary, which had become inaccurate due to numerous transcriptions. || 6 ||

# Notice

The system of *Prashna* <note>Questions</note> which the astrologer Shri Nilakantha created after his two systems on the fruits of the year is not found complete at this time. The science of questions gives visible results. Here, just as *Brihat Jataka* is for natal astrology and *Nilakanthi* is for the Tajika system, for the sake of the general public, this commentary in the common tongue...

<meta>This page serves as the translator's preface and publication information for the Tajika Neelakanthi, marking the completion of the vernacular commentary.</meta>

<page-num>280</page-num>
<header>Tajika Neelakanthi</header>

If the event has occurred, then a question regarding it must also certainly arise. || 1 || For this reason, a Brahmin named Mahidhar, a resident of Tehri, the capital of the Garhwal district, has rendered this work into the common language <note>original: "bhasha"; referring here to Hindi</note> for the benefit of all readers. This work is a beautiful collection by ancient teachers, possessing many virtues and containing all types of inquiries as described in various scriptures. || 2 || Following the composition of the commentary on the *Brihat Jataka* in the year 1808 <note>This likely refers to the Samvat era; 1808 Samvat is approximately 1751 CE, though the mention of King Kirti Shah suggests a later Victorian-era context (late 19th century) and may refer to a different era or a specific regnal year calculation</note>, during the reign of the illustrious Maharaja of Tehri Garhwal, the sovereign Shri 108 Kirti Shah Sahib Bahadur, in the aforementioned city. || 3 || This "Mahidhari" commentary on the *Neelakanthi*—which covers all three systems <note>The three branches of Tajika astrology: Sanjna, Varsha, and Prashna</note>, is easy to read, and illuminates the results related to the consideration of the stars (<term>Jyotish</term> <note>The traditional Indian system of astronomy and astrology</note>)—is intended to easily produce understanding in those ignorant of the *Neelakanthi* (the "children" or beginners). May virtuous men and scholars publish this well, and may they forgive whatever ignorance or audacity I have shown herein. || 4 || As for those who are intent on finding the faults of others, who destroy the good deeds done by others, and who are envious (those who burn with fire at the well-being of others and are ready to spoil another's purpose, who are sluggish in good deeds—meaning they cannot perform any good work with their own hands—but rather find pleasure in bad deeds, being "arrogant" and of evil intellect), let them see this labor of mine for the sake of public benefit and either criticize it or be happy and praise it. However, those wise gentlemen who are free from envy, who find joy in the good deeds of others and feel concern at bad deeds, may they treat this work as a righteous act. || 5 ||
